title: House Rules Wiki
text: Everything about running a home poker night with House Rules: setting up your club, running a cash game, keeping the cash box, settling up at the end of the night, hosting a tournament and running the blind timer. New here? Start with Your First Cash Game. Can't find an answer? Search above, read the FAQ or contact support.

title: Your First Cash Game
headings: Do I have to create a club first?
How do I add my players to the club?
A player paid by bank transfer. Is that in the cash box?
I typed the wrong number. How do I fix it?
The chips don't add up at the end. What now?
Can two games run at the same time?
Do I have to collect from everyone before I settle up?
Can I reopen a finished session?
text: This guide walks you through one whole cash game in House Rules: you create a club, seat your players, track every buy-in, rebuy and cash-out, and finish with a list of who pays whom. You'll follow one real-looking game from start to finish. Read it once before your game night, then keep it open on the night itself. What you'll end up with By the end of the night House Rules shows you: every player's result in money, for example Jenna +$169 or Marcus −$149; the rake and dealer tips that came off the table; who paid for food and how it's split; a short list of transfers, like Sam → Marcus $22, that settles everything. The example game Every screenshot in this guide comes from the same game, so you can check each number against the one before it. The club: Maple Street Game, six regulars who play at Dave's: Dave, Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya and Sam. The game: No-Limit Hold'em, $1/$2. The table uses chips worth $0.25 each, so the blinds are 4/8 in chips. Buy-in: 400 chips, which is $100 at $0.25 a chip. During the night: Marcus and Tyler each rebuy for 400 chips. Sam joins later and pays at the end of the night. Jenna pays her buy-in by bank transfer, everyone else in cash. Priya leaves early. At the end: 120 chips are left on the table. 80 go to the house as rake ($20), 40 go to the dealer as tips ($10). The house is you, the host, and the dealer is whoever deals for the table. Dave bought $48 of pizza, and everyone splits it. Chips and money are never mixed up in House Rules. Chips are plain numbers, like 400. Money always has a currency sign, like $100. The chip value is the bridge between them: 400 chips × $0.25 = $100. Before you start House Rules on your iPhone or iPad. Your chip value: how much money one chip (or a stack of chips) is worth at your table. If you play with cash-value chips, it's simply 1 chip = $1. The names of the people you play with. You add them as they sit down, so there's nothing to type in advance. Step 1. Create a club A club is your regular group of players. It keeps the history of every session, each member's results, and the settings for your next game. 1. Open House Rules. You land in the Lobby. 2. With no clubs yet, tap Create Club in the middle of the screen. Once you have a club, you add more with the + next to Clubs. 3. Type the club's name and pick a color. The color marks the club's sessions everywhere in the app. 4. Tap the checkmark. The new club opens right away. The empty Lobby with No Sessions Yet, a Create Club button and Start Session at the bottom From the empty Lobby, Create Club opens the name field, Maple Street Game is typed, the blue color is picked and the club screen opens The club name field over the keyboard with Maple Street Game typed and a row of nine color dots below it, the blue one checked A club name can be up to 40 characters, and two clubs can't share a name. You can rename the club or change its color later from the More button (•••) on the club screen. The new Maple Street Game club with 0 members, 0 sessions and No Sessions Yet No club yet? You can skip this step. Tap Start Session in the empty Lobby. The session goes to a new club called Home Game, which you can rename anytime. Step 2. Start the session A session is one cash game, from the first buy-in to the last transfer. 1. In the club, tap + at the bottom, then Cash Game. From the Lobby, Start Session and Cash Game do the same. 2. The New Session form opens. Check each row: Club: the club this session belongs to. With more than one club, tap it to pick another or create a New Club. NLH or PLO: the game. Small Blind, Big Blind and Ante, in chips. When you enter the small blind, the big blind is suggested at double. Ante is optional: leave it empty for no ante. Chip Value: enter the money first, then how many chips it buys. Skip the chips and it's one chip. In the example, type 0.25 and skip the chips: 1 chip = $0.25. Typing $1 for 4 chips gives the same value. Start: Now by default. Tap it to pick another date and time. 3. Tap the checkmark. The session opens right away. The club's + button and Cash Game open New Session; the small blind is set to 4, the chip value to $0.25, and the checkmark opens the empty session New Session for Maple Street Game as it opens in a new club: NLH, empty blinds, Chip Value 1 chip = $1, Start Now New Session for Maple Street Game: NLH, Small Blind 4, Big Blind 8, Ante empty, Chip Value 1 chip = $0.25, Start Now Every number in the form opens the app's own keys. The arrow on the keys moves to the next number, the checkmark on the keys goes back to the form. A big blind smaller than the small blind shows a red line, and you can't save until you fix it. In a club's first session, the chip value starts at 1 chip = $1 until you change it. Your next session in this club starts with the same game, blinds and chip value, so next time it's just +, Cash Game and the checkmark. If another session is already running, the form says so under Club. That's fine: both run side by side. To change anything after the session has started, tap the More button (•••) in the session and choose Edit Session. A new Live Session for Maple Street Game with 0 chips on the table and no players yet Step 3. Seat your players A new club has no members yet, so on your first night each player starts as a New Member: 1. Tap + at the bottom of the session. The New Player list opens. 2. Tap New Member, type the name and tap the arrow. 3. Enter the buy-in in chips. 4. Under the keys, choose how they pay: Cash: they hand you cash now. Transfer: they send you money now, by bank or app. Not Yet: they pay later. You collect it before the end of the night, or it goes into the final transfers. 5. Tap the checkmark. The player sits down and becomes a club member: House Rules keeps their results across sessions. 6. The list stays open, so tap New Member again for the next player. Tap ✕ when everyone is seated. The + button opens New Player, New Member opens a name field, Dave is typed, then 400 chips paid in cash seat him New Player with a name field over the keyboard, Dave typed in it Buy-in, Dave: 400 chips, Cost $100, with Cash selected under the title The line above the keys shows the Cost: the chips in money at the chip value. 400 chips at $0.25 cost $100. A club can't have two members with the same name: the arrow stays off and the app tells you why. Use a last initial, like Sam K., to tell people apart. Each entry shows a short message at the bottom, like Player added, with Undo. Undo removes exactly what you just recorded, the payment and the new member included. In the example, Dave, Marcus, Tyler and Priya pay $100 in cash and Jenna sends $100 by transfer. The Live Session with five players at the table, 2,000 chips on the table and $500 in the Cash Box Players who are already members Once a club has a session, its screen shows a Members tile. Members you've seated before, or added there with Add Member, are listed under Club Members in the New Player list. Tap the name instead of typing it. Members already at the table aren't in the list. In the example, Sam texted that he'd come late, so once the session was running you added him on the Members tile with Add Member. He joins two and a half hours in and will pay later. By then Marcus has already rebought once for 400 chips in cash (Step 4 shows how), so the table has 2,400 chips and the cash box $600. New Player with New Member at the top and Sam alone under Club Members The + button opens New Player, Sam is picked from Club Members, 400 is entered with Not Yet, and Sam joins the table Buy-in, Sam: 400 chips, Cost $100, with Not Yet selected and suggestions 400 usual, 800 ×2 and 1,200 ×3 On the right, the keys suggest amounts: the usual buy-in at this table, double it and triple it. Tapping a suggestion records it right away. The Live Session with six players and 2,800 chips on the table Reading the session screen On the Table: the chips in play right now, and what they're worth at the chip value. In the example, 2,800 chips are $700. The tiles: buy-ins (all chips bought tonight), cashed out, how many players are at the table, and how long the session has been running. At the Table: each seated player with their buy-ins in chips. Cash Box at the bottom: the money you've actually received, $600 here: $500 in cash plus Jenna's $100 transfer. Sam hasn't paid his $100 yet, so it isn't in the box. Step 4. Record rebuys When a player buys more chips: 1. Tap Rebuy at the bottom of the session. 2. Pick the player. 3. Enter the chips and choose how they pay. 4. Tap the checkmark. Rebuy opens the player list, Tyler is picked, 400 is entered with Cash, and the rebuy is recorded Rebuy, Tyler: 400 chips, Cost $100, Total buy-ins 800, Cash selected, and suggestions 400 buy-in, 800 ×2, 1,200 ×3 and 200 half Above the keys, Total buy-ins shows what the player has bought tonight with this rebuy: 800 chips for Tyler. The suggestions add half a buy-in. A quicker way: swipe right on the player's row and tap Rebuy. It opens the keys for that player straight away. Step 5. Cash players out When a player leaves the table: 1. Swipe left on their row and tap Cash Out. 2. Count their chips and enter the number. 3. Tap Cash Out on the keys. A swipe left on Priya's row shows Cash Out; 548 is entered and Priya moves to Cashed Out Cash Out, Priya: 548 chips, with her buy-in, her result +$37 and the chips that stay on the table Above the keys you see Bought in, the player's Result in money, and what's Left on table after they go. Priya bought 400 chips for $100 and leaves with 548 chips, which is $137, so she's up $37. While others are still seated, a cash-out can't be more than the chips on the table. If you type too much, a line above the keys tells you by how much. Zero is allowed: a player who lost everything cashes out with 0. The last player still seated gets a Whole Stack suggestion: everything left on the table. Only they can cash out with more than that: the keys say how many chips are short, and you sort it out in Close Session. Someone wants back in? Tap their row under Cashed Out and tap Back in Game. The Live Session after Priya cashed out: 2,652 chips on the table, worth $663, 548 cashed out and 5 of 6 at the table Recording a cash-out doesn't move any money. If you pay a player out right away, record it with Pay Out in the cash box. Otherwise their money comes in the final transfers, the way Priya's does in the example. Cash everyone out the same way as the night ends. In the example, the others hand back: Jenna: 400 bought, 1,108 cashed out ($277) Dave: 400 bought, 652 cashed out ($163) Priya: 400 bought, 548 cashed out ($137) Tyler: 800 bought, 312 cashed out ($78) Marcus: 800 bought, 236 cashed out ($59) Sam: 400 bought, 224 cashed out ($56) Total: 3,200 bought, 3,080 cashed out Fixing a mistake Tap a player's row. Their sheet lists every entry: buy-in, rebuys, cash-out. Tap an entry to change the amount, or swipe left on it to delete it. Changing an amount keeps the entry's time and payment. Step 6. Record rake and tips When everyone has cashed out, the chips players handed back rarely match the chips they bought: some went to the house (rake) and some to the dealer (tips). In the example, players bought 3,200 chips and cashed out 3,080. That leaves 120 chips on the table. 1. On the session screen, tap Chips Left on the Table. 2. All 120 chips start out as rake. Type the rake, 80. 3. Tap the arrow. The tips get the rest, 40. 4. Tap the checkmark. Chips Left on the Table opens the rake and tips keys; 80 is typed as rake, tips become 40, and the card changes to Rake and Tips Wrapping Up: everyone has cashed out and a Chips Left on the Table card shows 120 chips to assign The rake and tips keys with 80 chips of rake typed, tips still 0, and 120 chips on the table Rake and tips must add up to the chips left on the table. Once they do, the keys say All chips left on the table go to rake and tips and the checkmark saves them. At $0.25 a chip, 80 chips of rake are $20 and 40 chips of tips are $10. No rake at your game? Put everything in tips, or everything in rake if the extra chips simply go back to the host. Wrapping Up with Ready to Settle: 3,200 chips bought, 3,080 cashed out, 6 players, and Rake 80 and Tips 40 Step 7. Check the cash box The cash box is the real money you're holding as the host. Tap Cash Box at the bottom of the session. Cash Box with $700: $600 in cash, $100 by transfer, $700 collected, $0 paid out, $52 still owed and $20 rake, and Sam owes $52 under Before You Settle Up The big number is what should be in the box: $700, made of $600 in cash and $100 by transfer (Jenna's buy-in). still owed: what players haven't paid yet. Sam owes $52: his $100 buy-in, minus the $56 his 224 chips are worth, plus his $8 share of the pizza. rake: the rake in money, $20. The $10 of tips isn't a tile here: it simply stays in the box until you hand it to the dealer. Before You Settle Up: what's left to do. Tap a row to fix it. Here you can also: Collect money from a player who owes. Tap Sam owes or Collect, enter the amount, choose Cash or Transfer and tap Collect Payment. You don't have to: whatever is still owed at the end goes into the transfers. Pay Out money from the box. Count Cash: count the bills and compare them with what should be in cash. Add Expenses, like food or table rent, with the + in the Expenses card. The lower part of Cash Box with the Expenses card listing Pizza, $48, paid by Dave The pizza cost $48 and Dave paid for it. Split evenly between six players, it's $8 each. Dave gets his $48 back in the final transfers, minus his own $8 share. More about the cash box: The Cash Box. More about food and other costs: Expenses. Step 8. Close the session Go back to the session and tap Close Session at the bottom. Once everyone has cashed out, it takes the place of Rebuy. It walks you through five steps, in order: 1. Cash Out: everyone has left the table. 2. Rake and Tips: the chips left over are assigned. 3. Expenses: every expense is split between players. 4. Collect: money players still owe the cash box. 5. Settle Up: who pays whom. Each step shows a checkmark when it's done, a number when it's next, or Not needed when there's nothing to do. The button at the bottom always moves you on to the current step. Close Session with Cash Out, Rake and Tips and Expenses checked, Collect current with 1 player owes $52, Settle Up waiting, and Kept by House $20 In the example, the first three steps are already done. Under Rake and Tips you also see Rakeback, for giving part of the rake back to players (not used here), and Kept by House: what the house keeps from the rake, $20. Below the steps, the Cash card shows what Should be in cash, $600 here. Tap Count Cash to count the bills before you hand any out. Collect says 1 player owes $52. This step is optional. Tap Continue to skip it, and Sam's $52 goes into the transfers. Step 9. Settle up The Settle Up step lists the transfers that settle everything, in three groups: From Cash Box: money you pay out to players. Between Players: one player pays another directly. To Cash Box: money a player pays you. Settle Up with 0 of 7 marked and the From Cash Box group starting with Jenna, $269 Each transfer explains its amount. Jenna's line reads Game +$177, expense share −$8, paid in +$100: she won $177, owes $8 for pizza and already paid $100, so she gets $269 from the cash box. All seven transfers in the example: Cash Box → Jenna, $269: won $177, pizza −$8, paid in $100. Cash Box → Dave, $203: won $63, gets back $48 for the pizza, pizza −$8, paid in $100. Cash Box → Priya, $129: won $37, pizza −$8, paid in $100. Cash Box → Tyler, $70: lost $122, pizza −$8, paid in $200. Cash Box → Marcus, $29: lost $141, pizza −$8, paid in $200, minus the $22 he gets from Sam. Sam → Marcus, $22: part of what Sam owes. Sam → Cash Box, $30: the rest of what Sam owes. After all of them, the cash box holds exactly $30: the $20 rake you keep and the $10 you hand to the dealer. The box pays out $700, but only $600 of it is in bills: Jenna's $100 came in by transfer. So pay some transfers by bank or app instead, for example Jenna's $269. Marking a transfer as paid works the same whichever way the money moved. Mark each transfer as done 1. When money moves, tap the transfer. The full amount is already filled in. 2. Tap Mark as Paid. If the player paid only part, type the smaller amount and tap Record Payment: the rest stays open as a new transfer. 3. When every transfer is marked, tap Finish Session. A tap on Jenna's transfer opens the payment keys with $269 filled in, and Mark as Paid checks it off The payment keys for Cash Box to Jenna with $269 filled in and a Mark as Paid button Close Session scrolled to the end: every transfer checked and struck through, Sam → Marcus $22 and Sam $30 to the cash box, and Finish Session at the bottom The bell next to an open transfer opens a ready reminder text for the player who pays, which you send in any messaging app. Tap a marked transfer again to unmark it. Someone pays tomorrow? While transfers are still open, the button at the bottom says Close for Now. Tap it and confirm. The session waits, and the open transfers show up in Who Owes on the club screen. When the money comes in, open the session, tap Close Session and mark them. When you tap Finish Session, the session ends and shows the final results. Each player's result includes their share of expenses: Jenna won $177 at the table and paid $8 for pizza, so her result is +$169. Session Ended for Maple Street Game: Results for 6 players, +$301 won by 3 players and −$331 lost by 3 players, 3,200 buy-ins, 3,080 cashed out, 120 chips of rake and tips Winners got $301 and losers lost $331. The $30 between them is the rake and tips, and it's exactly what's left in the Cash Box. The pizza nets out to zero: Dave's +$48 is the money he gets back, and the six $8 shares pay for it. So Dave's +$103 is really +$55 from the night plus his $48 back. Jenna: +$177 at the table, −$8 pizza, result +$169 Dave: +$63 at the table, +$48 back for the pizza, −$8 pizza, result +$103 Priya: +$37 at the table, −$8 pizza, result +$29 Sam: −$44 at the table, −$8 pizza, result −$52 Tyler: −$122 at the table, −$8 pizza, result −$130 Marcus: −$141 at the table, −$8 pizza, result −$149 A finished session can't be changed by accident. To fix a mistake, open it and tap Reopen (the lock) at the bottom. Transfers you already marked stay marked. What's next Next time, tap Start Session and Cash Game: the game, blinds and chip value are copied from tonight, and your players are waiting under Club Members. Learn more about each part: Starting a Cash Game Buy-Ins, Rebuys and Cash-Outs Chip Value When a Player Pays Later Rake, Tips and Rakeback Close Session Step by Step How Settle Up Works Questions Do I have to create a club first? No. Tap Start Session in the empty Lobby. The session goes to a new club called Home Game, and you can rename it later. How do I add my players to the club? Seat them. Everyone you seat with New Member joins the club when you record their buy-in. Once the club has a session, you can also open the Members tile on the club screen and tap Add Member. More in Clubs and Members. A player paid by bank transfer. Is that in the cash box? Yes. The cash box counts both. Its big number is split into in cash and by transfer, so you know how much paper money should be in the box. I typed the wrong number. How do I fix it? Right after the entry, tap Undo in the message at the bottom. Later, tap the player's row, then tap the entry and type the right amount. The chips don't add up at the end. What now? If players cashed out fewer chips than they bought, the rest is rake and tips: tap Chips Left on the Table. If they cashed out more than they bought, see The Chips Don't Add Up. Can two games run at the same time? Yes. Start another session while one is running. The New Session form tells you about the other one, and both run side by side. Do I have to collect from everyone before I settle up? No. The Collect step is optional. Whatever a player still owes goes into the transfers. Can I reopen a finished session? Yes. Open it and tap Reopen (the lock) at the bottom. Transfers you already marked stay marked, and the rest is worked out again.

title: Your First Tournament
headings: Is the tournament saved if I close the app?
A player paid after all. How do I record it?
Where does the house fee go?
A player hasn't paid. Can they still play?
Can a player join after the start?
What if I don't run the blind timer?
Can two players finish in the same place?
Can I reopen a finished tournament?
text: This guide walks you through one whole tournament in House Rules: you set the price of an entry, seat your players, record re-entries and busts, and finish with a list of who pays whom. You'll follow one real-looking tournament from the first entry to the last transfer. Read it once before your game, then keep it open on the night. What you'll end up with By the end of the night House Rules shows you: the prize pool and what each paid place wins, for example 1st $228 and 2nd $122; every player's finishing place and result in money, like Jenna +$173; the house fee you keep; a short list of transfers, like Sam → Marcus $20, that settles everything. The example tournament Every screenshot in this guide comes from the same tournament, so you can check each number against the one before it. The club: Maple Street Game, six regulars who play at Dave's: Dave, Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya and Sam. They're already club members. If yours aren't yet, you add them as they sit down, see Step 2. The price of an entry: a $50 buy-in that goes to the prize pool, plus a $5 house fee that goes to you, the host. So every entry costs $55. Chips: everyone starts with 20,000 chips. Blinds start at 50/100. Re-entry: a player who busts early can buy back in until the end of Level 4. During the night: Sam sits down without paying and pays at the end. Tyler busts early and re-enters for another $55. Then the players go out one by one: Priya, Sam, Dave, Tyler and Marcus. Jenna wins. Tournament chips aren't worth money. A stack of 20,000 chips is just a stack: there's no chip value like in a cash game. A player's result is their prize minus everything they paid in. Before you start The cash box is the money you, the host, hold for the night: entries go in, prizes come out. If you play too, add yourself as a player like everyone else. House Rules on your iPhone or iPad. The buy-in, the house fee (if you take one) and the starting stack. A club. If you have none yet, follow Step 1 of Your First Cash Game. Or tap Start Session and Tournament in the empty Lobby: the tournament goes to a new club called Home Game, which you can rename anytime. Step 1. Start a new tournament 1. Open the club from the Lobby. 2. Tap + at the bottom, then Tournament. From the Lobby, Start Session and Tournament do the same. 3. The New Tournament form opens. The Maple Street Game club with 6 members, 0 sessions, No Sessions Yet and the + button at the bottom The club's + button and Tournament open New Tournament; the House Fee row is set to $5 and the line under it changes to $55 per entry The price of an entry The top of the form sets what players pay and what they get: Club: the club this tournament belongs to. With more than one club, tap it to pick another or create a New Club. NLH or PLO4: the game. Buy-In: what each entry adds to the prize pool. A club's first tournament starts at $50. Bounty: Off here. With Fixed or Progressive, players also win money for every player they knock out. See Fixed Bounties and PKO. House Fee: what the house keeps from each entry. It goes to the cash box, not to the prize pool. Leave it empty for no fee. Starting Stack: the chips each entry gets, 20,000 by default. The line under them sums it up. With a $50 buy-in and a $5 fee it reads Players pay $55 per entry. The fee goes to the cash box, not the prize pool. New Tournament for Maple Street Game: NLH, Buy-In $50, Bounty Off, House Fee empty, Starting Stack 20,000, and Players pay $50 per entry, all of it to the prize pool New Tournament with House Fee $5 and the line Players pay $55 per entry. The fee goes to the cash box, not the prize pool Every number opens the app's own keys, like in a cash game: type the amount and tap the checkmark on the keys. The rules of the night Scroll down for the rest: Re-Entry: whether a busted player can buy a new stack, and until when: Off, Until Level 4, 6 or 8, Until First Break or Until Second Break. The example uses Until Level 4. Add-On: one extra stack per player at its own price. Off in the example. Guarantee: the least the paid places split, however few players come. Empty for no guarantee. See Prize Pool and Payouts. Dealer Tips: Off, Percent or Amount, taken off the buy-ins and kept in the cash box for the dealer. Tables, Draw Seats: random seats at one or more tables. It's on for a new club. With one table at home you can turn it off, as in the example. See Tables and Seats. Blinds: the Pace of the blind timer, the Level Length and how often there are Breaks. Under them you see the first levels and the length of the whole structure. The example keeps Standard: 15-minute levels, a break every 4 levels, starting at 50/100, 12 levels, ≈ 3h 20m. Payouts: Auto. The more entries, the more places get paid: 1 place up to 4 entries, 2 up to 7, 3 up to 15, 4 up to 24, then 5. You can change it later on the tournament's Payouts screen. The middle of New Tournament: Add-On off, Guarantee empty, Dealer Tips Off, Draw Seats off, Pace Standard, Level Length 15 min, Breaks Every 4 levels The bottom of New Tournament: the blinds preview 50 / 100, 75 / 150, 100 / 200, 150 / 300, 12 levels, about 3h 20m, and Payouts Auto with its explanation Your next tournament in this club starts with the same settings, so next time it's just +, Tournament and the checkmark. Start Tournament Tap the checkmark (Start Tournament). The tournament opens and its blind timer starts right away at Level 1. The first time, iPhone asks whether House Rules may send notifications: allow them, and you get an alert when the level changes, even with the phone locked. The chip under the title shows the timer: Level 1, the blinds 50 / 100 and the time left in the level. Tap it to open the timer full screen. More in Running the Timer. A new Live Tournament for Maple Street Game with the timer at Level 1, 50 / 100, a $0 prize pool, 0 entries and Payouts appear with the first entry Another timer already running? The form asks A Timer Is Running first. Link to This Tournament keeps that timer and ties it to the tournament. Start Over From Tournament Blinds restarts it with this tournament's structure. Step 2. Add your players 1. Tap + at the bottom. The Add Player list opens. 2. Leave Paid on if the player hands you the money now. The line under it says $55 goes to the cash box now. 3. Tap their name under Club Members. They're in right away, and the list stays open for the next player. 4. Someone who isn't a member yet? Tap New Member and type the name, or type it in Search Members and tap Add with their name in quotes. They join the club. 5. Tap ✕ when everyone is in. The + button opens Add Player with Paid on, and Dave, Jenna and Marcus are tapped one after another and leave the list Add Player with Search Members, Paid on, $55 goes to the cash box now, New Member, and the six club members listed Sam will pay later. Turn Paid off before you tap his name. The line changes to The player owes $55 until they pay in the cash box. Sam plays all the same, and his row shows owes $55 until he pays. Add Player with Paid off, The player owes $55 until they pay in the cash box, and only Sam left under Club Members Each entry shows a short message at the bottom, like Dave is in, with Undo. Undo removes the entry and its payment from the cash box. A club member's name can't be added twice: typing it under Search Members asks you to choose them from the list instead. Reading the tournament screen Live Tournament with a $300 prize pool, 6 entries, $30 house fee, 6 of 6 players left, 200 BB average stack, 120,000 chips in play, Payouts 1st 65% $195 and 2nd 35% $105, and $275 on the Cash Box button Prize Pool: the buy-ins, $300 for six entries. Under it: 6 entries, $30 house fee. The fee isn't in the pool. players left: 6 of 6. avg stack: the average stack in big blinds (BB), the bigger of the two forced bets of the current level: 200 BB is 20,000 chips at a 100 big blind. chips in play: 120,000. running: how long the tournament has been going. Payouts: what each paid place wins right now. Six entries pay two places, 65% and 35%: $195 and $105. Above them, 4 more out to the money counts how many more players must bust before everyone left wins a prize ("in the money"). Tap the card to open Payouts. The Cash Box button at the bottom shows the money you hold: $275, five paid entries. Sam's $55 isn't in it yet. The Still In list with Dave, Jenna, Marcus, Priya, Sam with owes $55, and Tyler, each with 1 entry Still In lists everyone who's still playing, with how many entries they've bought. Tap a player to record them out. Touch and hold a row for its menu: Player Out, Add-On when the tournament has one, and Delete Player for someone added by mistake whose entry hasn't touched the cash box. Step 3. Record a re-entry Tyler busts in the first level and wants back in. Re-entry is open until the end of Level 4, so: 1. Tap Player Out at the bottom. 2. Tap Player and pick Tyler. 3. Choose Re-Enter. The line under it says Re-entry closes after Level 4. 4. Leave Paid on if he pays now: New stack of 20,000, $55 to the cash box. 5. Tap Save. Player Out opens, Tyler is picked, Re-Enter is chosen with Paid on, and Save records his second entry Player Out for Tyler with Re-Enter selected over Out in 6th, Re-entry closes after Level 4, and Paid on: New stack of 20,000, $55 to the cash box Tyler stays in the game with a fresh stack, and his row now shows 2 entries. The prize pool grows to $350 and the house fee to $35. With seven entries Auto still pays two places, now $228 and $122. Here's why: 35% of $350 is $122.50, every place except 1st rounds down to whole dollars, and the leftover goes to 1st. Live Tournament after the re-entry: a $350 prize pool, 7 entries, $35 house fee, and payouts of $228 and $122 When the re-entry window closes, Re-Enter disappears from Player Out and a busted player is simply out. The window follows the tournament's own blind timer. If the timer isn't running, re-entry stays open and it's your call. Step 4. Record players out When a player busts for good: 1. Tap Player Out, or tap the player's row under Still In. 2. Pick the Player. 3. Leave Out in 6th selected. The app gives them the next place down: the number of players still in. 4. Optionally, under Knocked Out By, pick who busted them. It shows in their row, like by Jenna. 5. Tap Save. Player Out opens, Priya is picked, Jenna is picked under Knocked Out By, and Save moves Priya to Out in 6th place Player Out for Priya with Out in 6th selected, Knocked Out By Jenna, and No prize, 5 players left The line at the bottom tells you what the place is worth: No prize, 5 players left, or Wins $122. for a paid place. A message at the bottom confirms the bust, like Priya out in 6th, with Undo. Live Tournament with 3 more out to the money, Priya under Out in 6th place, by Jenna Record the others the same way as they go. In the example, Tyler knocks out Sam in 5th and Marcus knocks out Dave in 4th. Now it's 1 more out to the money: the next player out is the last one who wins nothing. Live Tournament with 1 more out to the money: Jenna, Marcus and Tyler still in, and Priya 6th, Sam 5th with owes $55, and Dave 4th under Out Jenna knocks out Tyler in 3rd. Then Marcus goes out in 2nd, and Jenna is the only one left: she gets 1st place and the tournament is over. Player Out for Marcus with Out in 2nd and Wins $122, Save, and the screen changes to Tournament Over with Jenna wins $228 Undoing a bust Picked the wrong player? Tap Undo in the message right away. Later, touch and hold the row of the last player out and tap Back In. Only the latest bust can be undone. Undoing the bust that ended the tournament brings the winner back into play too. Step 5. Tournament Over When one player is left, the screen changes to Tournament Over, and the blind timer pauses where it was. Tournament Over: Ready to Settle, Jenna wins $228, 6 players, 7 entries, pool $350, and Final Standings from Jenna +$173 to Priya −$55, with Settle Up at the bottom Final Standings shows every place with its result in money: what the player won minus what they paid in. 1st Jenna: won $228, paid $55, +$173 2nd Marcus: won $122, paid $55, +$67 3rd Tyler: paid $110 for two entries, −$110 4th Dave: paid $55, −$55 5th Sam: owes $55, −$55 6th Priya: paid $55, −$55 The results add up to −$35, the house fee. Seven entries cost $385 in all: $350 goes back as prizes and $35 stays with you. Step 6. Check the cash box Tap the Cash Box button at the bottom. Cash Box for the tournament with $330, and Sam owes $55, can stay unpaid until settlement, under Before You Settle Up The big number is the money you hold: $330, six paid entries of $55. Before You Settle Up says Sam owes $55 and can stay unpaid until settlement: whatever he hasn't paid goes into the transfers. The house fee works like rake in a cash game: it's money the house keeps. You can Collect Sam's $55 here if he pays now, or Count Cash to check the bills. More in The Cash Box. Step 7. Settle up Go back and tap Settle Up at the bottom. Close Tournament walks you through five steps, in order: 1. Places: everyone has a place. It's done by itself once the tournament is over. 2. House Fee: $35 to the cash box. Kept by House shows what you keep, $35, and Rakeback lets you give part of it back to players. 3. Expenses: Not needed unless you added an expense, like food. 4. Collect: 1 player owes $55. This step is optional: tap Continue to skip it. 5. Settle Up: who pays whom. Close Tournament: Places Everyone has a place, House Fee $35 to the cash box with Kept by House $35, Expenses Not needed, Collect 1 player owes $55, Settle Up waiting, Should be in cash $330 and a Continue button Below the steps, the Cash card shows what Should be in cash, $330. Tap Count Cash to count the bills before you hand any out. Tap Continue. The transfers appear: Settle Up with 0 of 4 marked: Jenna $228 and Marcus $102 from the cash box, Sam → Marcus $20 between players, and Sam $35 to the cash box, owed for the tournament Cash Box → Jenna, $228: her prize. Cash Box → Marcus, $102: his line reads Prize +$122, from Sam −$20. Sam → Marcus, $20: part of Sam's unpaid $55. Sam → Cash Box, $35: the rest of it, owed for the tournament. The app keeps the list short: instead of Sam paying the box and the box paying Marcus, part of Sam's debt goes straight to Marcus. After all four, the cash box holds exactly $35: your house fee. Mark each transfer as done 1. When money moves, tap the transfer. The full amount is already filled in. 2. Tap Mark as Paid. If the player paid only part, type the smaller amount and tap Record Payment: the rest stays open as a new transfer. 3. When every transfer is marked, tap Finish Tournament. A tap on Jenna's transfer opens the payment keys with $228 filled in, and Mark as Paid checks it off The payment keys for Cash Box → Jenna with $228, Full amount, and a Mark as Paid button The last transfer checked: To Cash Box 1 of 1, Sam $35 owed for the tournament, crossed out, and Finish Tournament at the bottom Someone pays tomorrow? While transfers are still open, the button says Close for Now. The tournament waits, and the open transfers show up in Who Owes on the club screen. The bell next to an open transfer opens a ready reminder text for the player who pays. More in Who Owes and Reminders. When you tap Finish Tournament, the screen changes to Tournament Ended with the results. The cash box button shows $35, the house fee you keep. Tournament Ended for Maple Street Game: This tournament is finished and can't be changed, Results with Jenna wins $228 and Final Standings, and $35 on the Cash Box button A finished tournament can't be changed by accident. To fix a mistake, tap Reopen (the lock) at the bottom. Transfers you already marked stay marked. Settlement shows the transfers again. What's next Next time, tap + and Tournament in the club: the buy-in, fee, stack, re-entry, blinds and payouts are copied from tonight. Learn more about each part: Setting Up a Tournament Entries, Re-Entries and Add-Ons When a Player Is Out Prize Pool and Payouts Making a Deal Running the Timer How Settle Up Works Questions Is the tournament saved if I close the app? Yes. Everything is saved on your phone as you go. Open the club again and the tournament is where you left it. A player paid after all. How do I record it? Open the Cash Box and tap Collect, or leave it for Settle Up: an unpaid entry becomes a transfer to the cash box. Where does the house fee go? To the cash box, not the prize pool. In Close Tournament it's the House Fee step, and it's what stays in the cash box after Settle Up: $35 in the example. How many places get paid? With Auto: 1 place up to 4 entries, 2 up to 7, 3 up to 15, 4 up to 24, then 5. A re-entry counts as an entry. To pay a different number of places or other shares, open Payouts from the card on the tournament screen. A player hasn't paid. Can they still play? Yes. Turn Paid off when you add them. Their row shows owes $55 until they pay in the cash box, and whatever is still unpaid at the end goes into the transfers. Can a player join after the start? Yes, while registration is open: tap + and add them like everyone else. With re-entry, it closes when re-entry closes, at the end of Level 4 in the example. Without re-entry, it closes with the first bust. After that, the + for new players is greyed out. What if I don't run the blind timer? It starts with the tournament, and you can pause it anytime. While it isn't running, re-entry and late registration don't close by themselves: it's up to you to stop offering them. Can two players finish in the same place? No. Each bust gives the next place down. If two players bust on the same hand, record the one who started the hand with fewer chips first: they take the lower place. Can I reopen a finished tournament? Yes. Open it and tap Reopen at the bottom. Transfers you already marked stay marked, and the rest is worked out again.

title: Starting a Cash Game
text: A cash game in House Rules starts with one short form: the club, the game, the blinds and the chip value (what one chip is worth in money). Most nights you don't change anything on it, because it already has what you played last time. Check it, tap the checkmark at the top right, and the session opens. This article goes through every row of that form, what each one means and what House Rules fills in for you. The example night All the screenshots come from the same club. The club: Maple Street Game, six regulars: Dave, Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya and Sam. Last week: they played No-Limit Hold'em with blinds of 4/8 (a small blind of 4 chips and a big blind of 8), and one chip was worth $0.25. So a 400-chip buy-in cost $100. Tonight: Dave, the host, starts the next session from the Lobby. Nothing has changed since last week. In the Lobby, Start Session and Cash Game open the New Session form with last week's NLH 4/8 and 1 chip = $0.25, then the blind and chip value keys open and close Open the New Session form 1. In the Lobby, the first screen of the app, tap the Start Session button at the bottom. 2. Tap Cash Game. (Tournament starts a tournament instead, see Your First Tournament.) The Lobby with one club, Maple Street Game, and the Start Session menu open with Tournament and Cash Game From the Lobby, the new session goes to the club of your most recent session, and the form's first row shows which club that is. To start it in a particular club, open that club from the Lobby and tap + at the bottom of the club's screen, then Cash Game. Both ways open the same form, with these rows from top to bottom: Club, Game, the blinds, Chip Value and Start. What's already filled in The New Session form opens with everything from the club's last cash game: the game, the blinds and the chip value. A line under the chip value says where they came from: As in the last session, followed by that session's date. The New Session form: Club Maple Street Game, Game NLH, Small Blind 4, Big Blind 8, Ante empty, Chip Value 1 chip = $0.25, As in the last session, and Start Now If tonight is the same game, you're done: tap the checkmark at the top right. The rest of this article is for the nights when something changes. Club The Club row shows where the session goes. With one club, it just shows its name. With more than one club, tap the row to pick another club. The game, the blinds and the chip value then change to that club's last cash game. At the bottom of the same list, New Club creates a club right there. Game Pick NLH (No-Limit Hold'em) or PLO (Pot-Limit Omaha). The game is shown next to the session's name, like NLH 4/8, and in the club's history. Blinds and ante Tap the Small Blind amount. One set of keys takes all three numbers in a row: the small blind, the big blind and the ante (a forced bet from every player, which many home games don't use). The round button at the top right of the keys moves you on: an arrow goes to the next number, a checkmark saves. It's a different checkmark from the one at the top of the form, which starts the session. The ✕ at the top left of the keys closes the whole form, so to fix a number, delete it with the key next to 0 instead. The blind keys open over the form: Small Blind 4, Big Blind 8, Ante empty, and a suggestion 4/8 last time next to the digits 1. Type the small blind and tap the arrow. 2. Type the big blind, or keep the one House Rules suggests, and tap the arrow again. The suggestion is the big blind from a recent session of the club with the same small blind. With no such session, it's twice the small blind. 3. The ante is optional. Leave it empty for no ante. 4. Tap the checkmark on the keys to save all three. If the numbers are already right, the keys show the checkmark straight away: tap it and you're done. Next to the digits, the keys show buttons with the blinds of the club's recent sessions, up to three. Each one says when it was played: last time for the last session, a date for older ones. Tap one to fill in both blinds at once. Here Dave types a small blind of 5. The big blind becomes 10 on its own, and the line under it says why: Small Blind 5 and Big Blind 10 on the keys with the hint Twice the small blind until you set it Small Blind 5, Big Blind 10 and an empty Ante on the keys with the hint Optional. Leave it empty for no ante., and a checkmark in place of the arrow The big blind can't be smaller than the small blind. If you type one that is, the keys tell you and don't save it. You can also leave the blinds empty. The session starts without them, and you can add them later. Chip value The Chip Value row says what the chips are worth in money, like 1 chip = $0.25. House Rules uses it to turn chips into money: results, payments and rake. Money is always in your phone's currency, and chips never show a currency sign. Tap the amount. The keys take two numbers: first the money, then how many chips that money buys. The money keys have a decimal point, so you can type 0.25. Skip the chips and it's one chip. The chip value keys: Chip Value $0.25, Chips 1, and the result 1 chip = $0.25 above the digits Use whichever pair is easier to think about. If $20 buys 100 chips, type 20, tap the arrow, type 100. The line above the keys shows what you'll get, here 100 chips = $20, which is the same as $0.20 a chip. The chip value keys with $20 and 100 chips, the hint How many chips this money buys, and 100 chips = $20 above the digits You need at least one chip: with zero chips the keys don't save. It's easiest to set the chip value before anyone buys in and keep it for the whole night. More about choosing one: Chip Value. Start Start is Now by default. That's what you want when the game starts as you fill in the form. If you're entering a game that already started, or one from another night, tap Now. It turns into a date and a time, and you can tap either to change it. The New Session form with Start showing a date and a time instead of Now Start the session Tap the checkmark at the top right. The session opens right away, with no players yet. Seat them with + at the bottom, see Buy-Ins, Rebuys and Cash-Outs. The new Live Session for Maple Street Game, NLH 4/8: 0 chips on the table, 1 chip = $0.25, No Players Yet, and Cash Box, Rebuy and + at the bottom The ✕ at the top left of the form closes it without starting anything. Change it later Typed the wrong blinds? Open the session, tap the More button (the three dots at the top right) and choose Edit Session. The More menu of the session: Edit Session, Rake and Tips, House Rules, Session Log, Share Session, Hand Over Session and Delete Session The same form opens as Edit Session, with the game, the blinds, the chip value and the start time. The club can't be changed here. Tap the checkmark to save. The Edit Session form: Game NLH, Small Blind 4, Big Blind 8, Ante empty, Chip Value 1 chip = $0.25, and Start with a date and a time A finished session, one you've closed and settled, can't be edited. See Closing. Two sessions at once You can start a session while another one is still running, for example at a second table. The form tells you about it under the club, and both sessions run side by side. The New Session form with the note A session in Maple Street Game is still running. This one runs alongside it. Your very first session With no clubs yet, the Lobby is empty and shows Start Session at the bottom. Tap it and Cash Game as usual. The form then says the session Goes to a new club, Home Game. The club is created when you tap the checkmark, and you can rename it anytime, see Clubs and Members. The New Session form with no clubs yet: Club Home Game, Goes to a new club, Home Game. Rename it anytime., empty blinds and Chip Value 1 chip = $1 In a club's first session there's nothing to copy, so the blinds are empty and one chip is worth one unit of your currency, like 1 chip = $1. Change it before you start if your chips are worth something else. For a whole first night step by step, see Your First Cash Game. Questions Do I have to fill in the form every week? No. It copies the club's last cash game. If nothing changed, open it and tap the checkmark. Can I start without blinds? Yes. Leave them empty, and add them later with Edit Session. Can I change the chip value after people bought in? Yes, with Edit Session. Results and rake in money follow the new value. Payments players have already made into the cash box, the money you hold as the host, stay as they were. I started the session in the wrong club. What now? The club can't be changed afterwards. Delete the session from More, Delete Session, and start it again in the right club.

title: Buy-Ins, Rebuys and Cash-Outs
headings: More chips than on the table
text: Every chip that changes hands between you and a player goes through the same keys in House Rules: a buy-in seats a player with their first chips; a rebuy gives a seated player more chips; a cash-out records the chips a player hands back when they leave. From these three House Rules knows how many chips are on the table, how much money you hold, and at the end of the night who won and who lost. Two words you'll see everywhere: Chip value is what a chip is worth in money, set when you start the session, like 1 chip = $0.25. You enter chips, House Rules shows the money. See Chip Value. The cash box is the money players have paid you, the host, for their chips, in cash or by transfer. It's what you'll pay winners from at the end. See The Cash Box. The example night All the screenshots come from one night at the Maple Street Game. The game: No-Limit Hold'em, blinds 4/8, 1 chip = $0.25. The usual buy-in is 400 chips, which costs $100. The host: Dave. He plays too and records everything on his phone, so in this story you are Dave. Two and a half hours in: Dave, Marcus, Jenna, Tyler and Priya have bought in for 400 each, and Marcus has rebought once for another 400. That's 2,400 chips on the table, and everyone has paid, so $600 in the cash box. What happens next, in this order: Sam sits down for the usual 400 and pays cash. Kevin, a friend of Jenna's, plays for the first time and pays by transfer. Tyler rebuys 400 and Priya 200. Then Dave, who bought in once for 400, leaves with 652 chips. The Live Session: 2,400 chips on the table, 1 chip = $0.25, $600 at chip value, 5 of 5 at the table, Dave and Jenna with 400 chips each, and Cash Box $600, Rebuy and + at the bottom The bar at the bottom of the session has three buttons: Cash Box, with the money you hold, Rebuy, and + for a new player. Seat a player Tap + at the bottom. The New Player sheet opens with a search field, New Member and the list of Club Members who aren't at the table yet. The + button opens New Player, Sam is picked from Club Members, Cash is chosen and the 400 usual suggestion seats him A club member 1. Tap their name under Club Members. 2. The keys open for their buy-in. Type the chips, or tap a suggestion next to the digits. 3. Under the amount, choose how they pay: Not Yet, Cash or Transfer. 4. Tap the checkmark on the keys. The New Player sheet: Search Members, New Member, and Sam under Club Members The buy-in keys for Sam with Cash chosen, and suggestions 400 usual, 800 ×2 and 1,200 ×3 next to the digits The suggestions for a buy-in are the usual buy-in at this table (the first buy-in most players made tonight), twice it and three times it. A suggestion records the buy-in right away, with the payment you chose, so choose Cash, Transfer or Not Yet first. Above the keys, Cost shows what the chips cost in money at the session's chip value. Someone new Kevin has never played at the club. He isn't in the list, so Dave adds him: 1. Tap New Member and type the name. You can also type it in the search field and tap Add with the name in quotes. 2. Tap the arrow next to the name. The buy-in keys open. 3. Type the chips, choose how they pay, and tap the checkmark. The name field above the keyboard with Kevin typed and an arrow button next to it The buy-in keys for Kevin: 400 chips, Cost $100, Transfer chosen Kevin becomes a member of the club, so next time he's in the list. How they pay Cash or Transfer: the player paid you now. The money goes into the cash box. Not Yet: the player will pay later. They owe the cash box until you collect, see When a Player Pays Later. Not Yet is chosen by default, unless the club's rules set paying to cash or transfer up front. Then that one is chosen. Those rules are a club setting also called House Rules, see House Rules. After a buy-in A short message at the bottom confirms it, like Player added with Kevin, $100 in the cash box. Tap Undo in it if you seated the wrong person. The New Player sheet with the message Player added, Kevin, $100 in the cash box, and an Undo button The New Player sheet stays open, so you can seat the next player straight away. Close it with the ✕ at the top right when everyone is seated. The Live Session with 3,200 chips on the table, $800 at chip value, 7 of 7 at the table, and Cash Box $800 Record a rebuy There are two ways. Both open the same keys. The Rebuy button Tap Rebuy at the bottom of the session, then the player. Here Tyler rebuys for 400 and pays cash. Rebuy at the bottom opens the list of players at the table, Tyler is picked, 400 is typed, Cash is chosen and the checkmark records it The Rebuy sheet: Search Players and the players At the Table with their chips, and Rebuy and Cash Out at the bottom The two buttons at the bottom of this sheet, Rebuy and Cash Out, switch what the list is for: pick Cash Out and a tap on a player opens their cash-out instead. When someone has cashed out, a third button, Back in Game, appears there too. The rebuy keys for Tyler: 400 chips, Cost $100, Total buy-ins 800, Cash chosen, and suggestions 400 buy-in, 800 ×2, 1,200 ×3 and 200 half A swipe on the row Swipe right on the player's row and tap Rebuy. Priya wants half a buy-in, so Dave chooses Cash and taps 200 half. A swipe right on Priya's row shows Rebuy, the keys open, Cash is chosen and the 200 half suggestion records it Priya's row swiped right with a Rebuy button on the left The rebuy keys for Priya with Cash chosen and suggestions 400 buy-in, 800 ×2, 1,200 ×3 and 200 half You can also touch and hold the row and choose Rebuy from the menu. Cash out a player When a player leaves, count their chips and record them. Swipe left on the row and tap the Cash Out button that appears. The keys open: type the chips, then tap Cash Out at the top right of the keys to save. (The Rebuy sheet's Cash Out list opens the same keys.) A swipe left on Dave's row shows Cash Out, 652 is typed and the Cash Out button on the keys records it Dave's row swiped left with a Cash Out button on the right Above the keys you see what the cash-out means before you save it: Bought in: all the chips the player bought tonight; Result: what they won or lost in money, here +$63 (652 chips minus 400, at $0.25 a chip); Left on table: the chips that stay in play after they leave. The cash-out keys for Dave: 652 chips, Bought in 400, Result +$63, Left on table 3,148, and a Cash Out button After the cash-out Dave moves under Cashed Out, and the table has 3,148 chips: the 3,800 bought tonight minus Dave's 652. Their worth at the chip value is $787. The cash box stays at $950, the money paid for all 3,800 chips. A cash-out doesn't take money out of it: Dave doesn't get paid on the spot. At the end of the night House Rules works out who pays whom, and winners are paid from the cash box first, see How Settle Up Works. The Live Session after Dave's cash-out: 3,148 chips on the table, $787 at chip value, 3,800 buy-ins, 652 cashed out, 6 of 7 at the table, Cash Box $950 More chips than on the table While other players are still seated, a cash-out can't be more than the chips on the table. If you type too many, the keys say by how much, and Cash Out stays off. Here a slip of the finger made Marcus's 500 into 50,000: The cash-out keys for Marcus with 50,000 chips, the warning 46,852 more than on the table, and the Cash Out button turned off For the last player still seated, the keys offer Whole Stack: one tap records everything left on the table as their cash-out. If they hand back a different number, record what they hand back. The last player is the one exception to the rule above: they can cash out with more chips than House Rules has on the table, which usually means a rebuy nobody recorded. The keys say how many, like 52 chips short. You can sort it out in Close Session., and Cash Out still works. You deal with the short chips when you close the session, see Close Session, Step by Step. Bring a player back A player who cashed out sits down again later? Tap their row under Cashed Out, then Back in Game. The keys open as for a rebuy: type the chips, choose how they pay, and tap the checkmark. The player moves back to the table. Dave's sheet: Cashed out, Result +$63, 400 → 652, his Cash Out and Buy-in entries, and Back in Game and Delete Player The Back in Game keys for Dave with Not Yet chosen and Total buy-ins 400 You can also swipe right on the row under Cashed Out and tap Back in Game. Fix a mistake Right after an entry, tap Undo in the message at the bottom. Later, tap the player's row. Their sheet shows what they bought in, how long they've played, and every entry with its time. Marcus's sheet: Bought In 800, $200 at chip value, 2 buy-ins, his Rebuy and Buy-in entries, Rebuy and Cash Out buttons, and Delete Player Tap an entry to change its amount, or touch and hold it for Edit Amount and Delete Entry. A new amount changes the chips only. The money the player paid into the cash box for that entry stays as it was, so if they paid more or less than you first recorded, fix the payment in the Cash Box too. Marcus's Rebuy entry held down with the menu Edit Amount and Delete Entry Delete Player at the bottom removes the player and all their chip entries from the session. It only works while none of the session's money is tied to the player. Otherwise House Rules says what to clear first: This player has cash box payments. Delete them first. A buy-in paid by cash or transfer counts: delete the player's lines in the Cash Box. This player paid for or shares an expense. Remove them from expenses first. This player has completed transfers. Unmark them first. Both deletes ask you to confirm first. After a change or a delete, the chips on the table and the player's result are counted again. Questions Do I record chips or money? Chips. House Rules turns them into money with the session's chip value. More about it: Chip Value. A player will pay at the end of the night. What do I choose? Not Yet. They owe the cash box until you collect, see When a Player Pays Later. Why didn't the cash box go down after a cash-out? A cash-out records the chips a player hands back. Who gets paid how much is worked out once, at the end of the night, in Close Session. Can a player cash out more chips than they bought? Yes, that's a win. They just can't cash out more chips than are on the table. Is there a limit on rebuys? No. Record as many as the player makes. Can I change the chip value in the middle of the game? Yes, with Edit Session in the session's More menu. See Chip Value.

title: Chip Value
headings: Set it for a new session
text: The chip value is what your chips are worth in money, like 1 chip = $0.25. Every session has one. You record chips in House Rules: buy-ins, rebuys and cash-outs are all in chips. The chip value turns them into money. With it House Rules works out what a buy-in costs, what each player won or lost, and in the end who pays whom. How it works The chip value is two numbers: an amount of money and the number of chips it buys. 1 chip = $0.25: a 400-chip buy-in costs $100. 100 chips = $20: the same as $0.20 a chip, so 400 chips cost $80. 1 chip = $1: chips and dollars are the same number. A player's result is their chips at the end minus the chips they bought, times the chip value. Buy in for 400, cash out 652, and at $0.25 a chip you're up 252 chips, which is +$63. Chips never show a currency sign. Money is always in your phone's currency. The cash box is the money players have paid you, the host, for their chips. It doesn't depend on the chip value: a payment is money, recorded once. See The Cash Box. Set it for a new session The New Session form has a Chip Value row. It starts with the club's last cash game, so most nights you don't touch it. In a club's first session it's 1 chip = $1 (one unit of your currency) until you change it. How the form works: Starting a Cash Game. To change it, tap the amount. The keys take two numbers: 1. Money first: what the chips cost. The keys have a decimal point, so you can type 0.25. 2. Tap the arrow, the round button at the top right of the keys, to move to Chips: how many chips that money buys. Leave the chips empty and it's one chip. 3. Check the line above the keys, like 1 chip = $0.25, and tap the checkmark that's now in place of the arrow. The chip value keys with $20 and 100 chips, the hint How many chips this money buys, and 100 chips = $20 above the digits You need at least one chip. Type 0 chips and the keys say Enter at least one chip. and don't save. The chip value keys with $20 and 0 chips, the warning Enter at least one chip., and the checkmark turned off Change it during the session The example: it's two and a half hours into a night at the Maple Street Game. Five players bought 2,400 chips, everyone paid, so the cash box holds $600. Dave, the host, has already cashed out with 652 chips. Then Dave notices the session says 1 chip = $0.25. He started it from last week's form, but tonight the chips are worth $0.50. The Live Session with 1,748 chips on the table, 1 chip = $0.25, $437 at chip value, 2,400 buy-ins, 652 cashed out, 4 of 5 at the table, and Cash Box $600 Dave's sheet: Cashed out, Result +$63, 400 → 652 To fix it: 1. In the session, tap the More button (the three dots at the top right) and choose Edit Session. 2. Tap the Chip Value amount. 3. Type the money, 0.5. The chips can stay empty: it's one chip. 4. Tap the checkmark at the top right of the keys to close them, then the checkmark at the top right of the Edit Session form to save. More, Edit Session, Chip Value: the money changes from 0.25 to 0.5, the chips stay empty, and Edit Session is saved with 1 chip = $0.50 The chip value keys in Edit Session with $0.5 and the chips empty, and 1 chip = $0.50 above the digits Edit Session with Chip Value 1 chip = $0.50 What changes The new value counts for the whole session, including buy-ins and cash-outs recorded before the change. So every amount House Rules works out from chips follows it: the chips on the table are now worth $874 instead of $437; Dave's result is +$126 instead of +$63; rake and tips, if you take them, are counted at the new value too (see Rake, Tips and Rakeback). The Live Session after the change: 1,748 chips, 1 chip = $0.50, $874 at chip value, and Jenna owes $100 and Marcus owes $200 on their rows Dave's sheet after the change: Result +$126, 400 → 652 What stays Payments already in the cash box stay as they were. Everyone paid $100 for every 400 chips, and that's still $600. But at $0.50 a chip 400 chips cost $200. So each player still at the table now owes the difference: Jenna, Tyler and Priya $100 each, Marcus $200 for his 800 chips, $500 in all. Their rows say so, and the cash box shows it under still owed. Dave doesn't owe anything, because he has already cashed out with a win. His result of +$126 already counts his 400 chips at $0.50, so at the end of the night he gets back the $100 he paid plus his win. The Cash Box before the change: $600, $500 in cash, $100 by transfer, $600 collected, $0 still owed The Cash Box after the change: still $600 collected, $500 still owed, and Jenna owes $100 under Before You Settle Up Collect it in the cash box when they pay, or leave it: anything unpaid at the end goes into the transfers. See When a Player Pays Later. The easiest night is one chip value from the first buy-in to the end. Check it on the New Session form before anyone buys in. If the rake or tips would no longer cover rakeback or tips you've already paid out, the new chip value isn't saved. More about those: Rake, Tips and Rakeback. A finished session can't be edited, so its chip value can't change either. Choosing a chip value Pick one that makes the usual buy-in a round number of chips and of money. A few common setups: $100 buy-in for 400 chips: 1 chip = $0.25. $20 buy-in for 100 chips: 100 chips = $20, or $0.20 a chip. $50 buy-in for 50 chips: 1 chip = $1. Questions Do I type the chip value in chips or money first? Money first, then chips. Why does a player suddenly owe money? The chip value went up after they paid. Their chips now cost more than they paid, and the difference is owed. And if I lower the chip value? Then players have paid more than their chips now cost. Nobody owes the difference: it counts in their favor, and they get it back when you settle up at the end. Does the chip value carry over to the next session? Yes. The next session in the club starts with it, and you can change it on the form. Can a tournament have a chip value? No. Tournament chips aren't worth money, see Your First Tournament.

title: When a Player Pays Later
headings: Seat a player who hasn't paid
If they still owe at the end
text: Sometimes a player sits down without the money: no cash on them, or they'll send it later. You don't have to keep them waiting or remember it yourself. Seat them with Not Yet, and House Rules keeps track of what they owe the cash box until they pay. The cash box is the money players have paid you, the host, for their chips. More about it: The Cash Box. The example It's two and a half hours into a night at the Maple Street Game. The game: No-Limit Hold'em with blinds of 4 and 8 chips, 1 chip = $0.25. The usual buy-in is 400 chips, which costs $100. The table: Dave, the host, with Jenna, Marcus, Priya and Tyler. Each bought 400 chips, and Marcus bought 400 more later (a rebuy). Everyone has paid: Jenna by transfer, the rest in cash. So the cash box holds $600: $500 in cash and $100 by transfer. What happens: Sam arrives without cash and buys in for 400 chips, paying nothing yet. An hour later he hands Dave $60 in cash. $40 is still owed. Seat a player who hasn't paid 1. In the session, tap + at the bottom right and pick the player. For a player already at the table who buys more chips, tap Rebuy at the bottom instead and pick them (see Buy-Ins, Rebuys and Cash-Outs). 2. Above the digits, choose Not Yet. It's the first of three choices: Not Yet, Cash and Transfer. 3. Type the chips, or tap a suggestion next to the digits. A suggestion records the buy-in at once. The + button opens New Player, Sam is picked from Club Members, Not Yet is chosen and the 400 usual suggestion seats him The buy-in keys for Sam with Not Yet chosen, and suggestions 400 usual, 800 ×2 and 1,200 ×3 next to the digits Not Yet is chosen for you unless your club's House Rules say players pay up front in cash or by transfer. See House Rules. The toast says Player added with just the name. When a player pays on the spot, it also says how much went into the cash box. Here nothing did. The toast Player added, Sam, with an Undo button Where you see what's owed Sam's row in the session says 1 buy-in, owes $100. His 400 chips cost $100 at $0.25 a chip, and he hasn't paid any of it. At the Table: Sam's row says 1 buy-in, owes $100, 400 chips, and the Cash Box button at the bottom shows $600 Tap Cash Box at the bottom left. It still holds $600, and the tile still owed shows $100. Under Before You Settle Up there's a line Sam owes $100: he can stay unpaid until you settle up at the end of the night. Settling up is when House Rules works out who pays whom so everyone ends the night even. The line above it, 6 of 6 players at the table, only reminds you that everyone cashes out before that. The Cash Box: $600, $500 in cash, $100 by transfer, $600 collected, $100 still owed, and Sam owes $100 under Before You Settle Up Collect when they pay An hour later Sam hands Dave $60 in cash. To record it: 1. In Cash Box, tap Collect at the bottom left. 2. Under Owe the Cash Box, tap the player. Everyone who owes is listed here first, with the amount. 3. The keys open. Tap all owed next to the digits for the whole amount, or type a part of it. Sam pays 60. 4. Choose Cash or Transfer above the digits, the way they paid you. 5. Check the two lines above the keys: Owes is what the player owed, Cash box after is what the cash box will hold. Then tap the checkmark at the top right of the keys, Collect Payment. Collect opens, Sam is picked under Owe the Cash Box, the amount changes from 100 to 60 with Cash chosen, and the payment is collected Collect: Owe the Cash Box with Sam owes $100 at the top, then Players: Dave, Jenna, Marcus, Priya and Tyler The payment keys for Sam: Owes $100, Cash box after $600, Cash chosen, and the suggestion 100 all owed The payment keys for Sam with $60 typed: Owes $100, Cash box after $660, and the checkmark on The toast says Payment collected with the name and the amount. Undo takes it back. The Cash Box with $660 and the toast Payment collected, Sam, $60, with an Undo button Now the cash box holds $660: $560 in cash and $100 by transfer. still owed is down to $40, and Sam owes $40 under Before You Settle Up. The payment is also in the list of operations further down, as Sam, payment, +$60. The Cash Box after the payment: $660, $560 in cash, $100 by transfer, $660 collected, $40 still owed, and Sam owes $40 Further down the Cash Box: Sam owes $40 under Before You Settle Up, and Sam payment +$60 at the top of Operations If they still owe at the end You don't have to collect everything before the night ends. In Close Session, the Collect step lists who still owes. Collect there, or tap Continue to skip it. See Close Session Step by Step. Whatever is still unpaid goes into the transfers, the payments House Rules lists at settle-up (not the same as paying by Transfer). Sam's $40 is counted in what he pays or gets then. See How Settle Up Works. A transfer nobody marks as done stays in Who Owes on the club screen, so it isn't forgotten after tonight. See Who Owes and Reminders. Not Yet doesn't change anyone's result. Results come from chips: Sam's win or loss is counted the same whether he paid or not. Only the money he still owes changes. Questions Can a rebuy be unpaid too? Yes. The rebuy keys have the same Not Yet, Cash and Transfer choices. The player paid the whole amount. What do I tap? In Collect, pick them and tap all owed next to the digits. It's the full amount they owe. Sam wins chips later. Does he owe less? No. He owes what his chips cost when he bought them, $100. Winning or losing changes his result, and settle-up puts the two together at the end. Can they pay part in cash and part by transfer? Yes. Collect twice: once with Cash, once with Transfer. I chose Not Yet by mistake, they did pay. Collect the payment right away with all owed. Does the cash box total include what's owed? No. In Cash Box is only the money you actually got. What's owed is shown apart, as still owed.

title: Lock Screen and Quick Rebuy
headings: Add a rebuy from the card
When the card changes or goes away
text: While a cash game runs, House Rules puts a card on your iPhone's Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island, the black pill at the top of the screen. The card shows the table at a glance, and its + button takes you straight to Rebuy. You don't have to unlock, find the app and open the session when someone wants more chips. iOS calls cards like this Live Activities. The example It's two and a half hours into a night at the Maple Street Game: five players and 2,400 chips on the table. Each chip is worth $0.25, so 400 chips cost $100. Dave, the host, has put his phone down. Marcus has already bought chips twice tonight: 400 to sit down and 400 more at 11:15 PM. Buying more chips during the game is a rebuy. Now he has lost again and wants another 400, paid in cash. The cash goes into the cash box, the money players have paid Dave for their chips (see The Cash Box). The Live Session of the Maple Street Game: 2,400 chips on the table, 5 of 5 at the table, 2:29 running Where the card appears The card appears on its own once a cash game is running and you've opened the app. There's nothing to turn on. Dynamic Island (on iPhones that have one). Outside the app, the island shows a small dot on the left and how long the session has run on the right, in hours and minutes. Tap the island to open the session. Lock Screen. The full card, at the bottom of the Lock Screen. You also see it when you swipe down from the top left of the screen to open Notification Center. The Home Screen with the Dynamic Island showing a dot on the left and 2:30 on the right The first time, iOS asks under the card: Allow Live Activities from House Rules? Tap Allow to keep the card. With Don't Allow the card goes away, and you can turn it back on later in the iPhone Settings app. The Lock Screen with the Maple Street Game card and, under it, Allow Live Activities from House Rules? with Don't Allow and Allow What the card shows The Lock Screen card: Maple Street Game, 2:30:36, At the table 5 of 5, On the table 2,400 chips, a round + button, and Last: Marcus rebuy, 400, 11:15 PM From top to bottom: The club and the clock. The dot in the club's color, Maple Street Game, and how long the session has run: 2 hours 30 minutes 36 seconds. It keeps counting on its own. At the table: how many players are still in out of everyone who played tonight. 5 of 5 means nobody has cashed out. On the table: the chips in play, 2,400. The + button, round, on the right. It opens Rebuy. Last: the latest entry, with its chips and time. Here it's Marcus's earlier rebuy of 400 at 11:15 PM. Tap anywhere on the card except + to open the session. Add a rebuy from the card 1. On the Lock Screen, tap + on the card. If the phone is locked, iOS may ask you to unlock it first. 2. House Rules opens on Rebuy, with everyone at the table. Tap the player. 3. Above the digits, choose how they pay: Cash or Transfer if they pay you now, Not Yet if they'll pay later. 4. Type the chips and tap the checkmark at the top right of the keys, or tap a suggestion next to the digits. A suggestion records the rebuy at once. + on the Lock Screen card opens Rebuy, Marcus is picked, Cash is chosen and the 400 buy-in suggestion records the rebuy Rebuy opened from the card: At the Table with Dave 400, Jenna 400, Marcus 800, Priya 400 and Tyler 400 chips The rebuy keys for Marcus: Total buy-ins 800, Cash chosen, and suggestions 400 buy-in, 800 ×2, 1,200 ×3 and 200 half The keys are the same as in the app. More about rebuys and suggestions: Buy-Ins, Rebuys and Cash-Outs. If a player pays later, see When a Player Pays Later. The toast says Rebuy recorded, Marcus, $100 in the cash box. The session now has 2,800 chips on the table. Tapped the wrong player? Tap Undo on the toast. The Live Session with 2,800 chips on the table, Cash Box $700, and the toast Rebuy recorded, Marcus, $100 in the cash box The card follows: On the table is now 2,800, and Last shows the new rebuy. The Lock Screen card after the rebuy: 5 of 5 at the table, 2,800 chips on the table, Last: Marcus rebuy, 400, 11:16 PM When the card changes or goes away When everyone has cashed out, + goes away and the card says Everyone cashed out until you close the session. Closing or deleting the session removes the card. See Close Session Step by Step. iOS removes Live Activities on its own after several hours. Open the app and the card comes back. The card shows one cash game: the latest one running. Tournaments don't get this card. They use the blind timer card instead, see Notifications and Lock Screen. Turn it off On the House Rules home screen, open Settings, and under Live Activities switch off Lock Screen. The same switch covers the blind timer card. If Live Activities are turned off for House Rules in the iPhone Settings app, the House Rules Settings say so under the switch, and the card can't appear until you turn them back on there. Questions I don't see the card. Check three things: a cash game is running, you've opened House Rules since it started, and Lock Screen is on under Live Activities in House Rules Settings. If you tapped Don't Allow when iOS asked, turn Live Activities back on for House Rules in the iPhone Settings app. Can I record a buy-in for a new player from the card? No, + opens Rebuy for players already at the table. For a new player, open the session and tap + at the bottom right. Can I cash someone out from the card? Not from the card itself. Rebuy opens with a Cash Out tab at the bottom, so you can switch to it there. My iPhone has no Dynamic Island. The card still appears on the Lock Screen and in Notification Center. Do other players see the card? No. It's only on your phone, the one running the session.

title: The Cash Box
text: The cash box is the real money of the session: what players have paid you, the host, for their chips, minus what you've handed back. Chips stay on the table; money goes through the cash box. You record two kinds of money here: Collect: a player pays you. Most payments are recorded for you when you seat a player or add a rebuy and choose Cash or Transfer on the keys. Pay Out: you hand money to a player, usually when they leave with more chips than they bought. And one check: Count Cash, to see whether the money in your hands matches what House Rules expects. The example It's three hours into a night at the Maple Street Game. The game: No-Limit Hold'em, 1 chip = $0.25, so a 400-chip buy-in costs $100. The money so far: Dave, the host, Marcus, Jenna, Tyler and Priya have bought 2,400 chips. Marcus bought twice. Jenna paid $100 by transfer, everyone else paid cash, $500. So the cash box holds $600. What happens: Priya leaves with 548 chips. At $0.25 a chip they're worth $137, so Dave pays her $137 in cash: the $100 she paid plus her $37 win. Then he counts the cash in his hands. Open the cash box In the session, tap Cash Box at the bottom left. The button shows how much it holds. The Cash Box of the Maple Street Game: $600, $500 in cash, $100 by transfer, $600 collected, $0 paid out, $0 still owed, $0 rake, and 4 of 5 players at the table under Before You Settle Up From top to bottom: In Cash Box: the money you hold for the session, here $600. Under it, in cash and by transfer split it by how it was paid. You see these two once anyone has paid by transfer. collected: everything players have paid you. paid out: everything that left the cash box, to players, for expenses and for dealer tips. still owed: what players haven't paid yet. See When a Player Pays Later. rake: the house's share in money, see Rake, Tips and Rakeback. Before You Settle Up: what's left to do before the end of the night. Here 4 of 5 players are still at the table, which only needs time. Rows with an arrow open where you fix them, like collecting from a player who owes. Expenses: pizza, rent and the like, see Expenses. Operations: every payment and payout, newest first. The three buttons at the bottom are Collect, Pay Out and Count Cash. Pay a player out Priya cashes out first, in the session (see Buy-Ins, Rebuys and Cash-Outs). A cash-out only records her chips. The money is a separate step, here: 1. In Cash Box, tap Pay Out. 2. Under Payout Due, tap the player. Players who cashed out and haven't been paid yet are listed here first, with what they're due. 3. Choose Cash or Transfer above the digits. Cash is chosen to start with. 4. Tap the suggestion next to the digits, 137 payout due, to pay the whole amount. It's recorded at once. Or type another amount and tap the checkmark at the top right of the keys. Pay Out opens, Priya is picked under Payout Due, and the 137 payout due suggestion pays her Pay Out: Payout Due with Priya, $137 to pay out, then Players: Dave, Jenna, Marcus and Tyler, and Collect and Pay Out at the bottom The payout keys for Priya: $0, Left in cash box $600, Cash chosen, a Note row, and the suggestion 137 payout due The toast says Money paid out, Priya, $137, with Undo. The cash box now holds $463: $363 in cash and $100 by transfer, and paid out is $137.
