The Cash Box with $463, $363 in cash, $100 by transfer, $600 collected, $137 paid out, and the toast Money paid out, Priya, $137 You can't pay out more than the cash box holds. If you type more, the keys say so and the checkmark waits. Collect works the same way, the other direction: tap Collect, pick the player under Owe the Cash Box or Players, enter the amount. The full walk-through is in When a Player Pays Later. To remember why money moved, tap Note above the digits before you save. The note shows under the operation. Count the cash At any point, count the cash in your hands and check it against the cash box. Only cash counts here: transfers went to your bank, not your pocket. 1. Tap Count Cash at the bottom right. 2. Type the cash you counted. Above the keys, Should be in cash is what House Rules expects, and Difference is the gap. 3. Tap the checkmark at the top right of the keys. Dave counts $343. It should be $363, so the difference is −$20. Count Cash with $343: Should be in cash $363, Difference −$20 When it doesn't match, House Rules shows how much is off, like $20 Short, and what you can do: Find It First: Session Log lists everything that happened tonight, to look for a payment you forgot to record. Leave It for Now: only notes the count. Count again later. Host Covers It: the host makes up the difference. If your club's House Rules name the host, it comes off the host's result. Otherwise it's only marked as covered. Split Among Players: the difference is shared equally by everyone who played tonight, here $4 each, 5 players. Choose one and tap the checkmark at the top right, or the ✕ at the top left to go back without recording anything. The $20 Short sheet: Find It First with Session Log, then Leave It for Now (checked), Host Covers It, and Split Among Players, $4 each, 5 players Dave finds a $20 bill under the chip tray. He taps ✕, then Count Cash again, and types $363. The difference is $0, and the toast says Cash matches. Count Cash, 363, Difference $0, the checkmark, and the toast Cash matches The Cash Box with $463 and the toast Cash matches A count that matches doesn't move any money: In Cash Box stays $463. It's kept in Operations as a Cash Count line with the amount you counted, so you can see when you last counted and whether it matched. Leave It for Now doesn't move money either. The other choices do. Split Among Players, and Host Covers It when the host is named and played tonight, record a Cash short expense paid from the cash box, so the box goes down by the difference and the players who cover it see it in their results. When you count more cash than expected, the sheet says how much is over, like $10 Over, and offers Leave It, which only notes the count, and Add to Tips, which adds the extra to the dealer tips as an Extra Cash line in Operations. See The Cash Box Doesn't Match. Operations Scroll down to Operations. Each line is one payment, payout or count: the name, what it was and when, and the amount. Money in has a plus, money out a minus. A Cash Count line shows the amount you counted, not money in. The newest is on top, and the last five show until you tap Show All. Operations, 8: Cash Count, count, matched, 11:34 PM, +$363; Priya, payout, −$137; Marcus, payment, Payment for rebuy, +$100; Priya, payment, Payment for buy-in, +$100; Tyler, payment, +$100 To fix one, swipe it to the left: Edit changes the amount, or the note of a payment or payout. You can also just tap the line. Delete removes it, after you confirm. Priya's payout line swiped to the left, showing Edit and Delete Recorded cash that was really a transfer, or the other way round? Touch and hold the line and choose Mark Paid by Transfer or Mark Paid in Cash. You can't change who a line is for. Delete it and record it again. A finished session's cash box can only be read. To change it, reopen the session from its settlement. Questions Why is there money in the cash box I didn't collect by hand? Payments you choose on the buy-in and rebuy keys go straight into the cash box, at the chip value. A player paid more than they owed. Collect it anyway. The extra goes back to them at settle-up, see How Settle Up Works. Can the cash box go below zero? No. You can't pay out more than it holds. Do I have to count the cash? No, it's a check for you. If cash goes missing, it's easier to find the same night. The cash box doesn't match my pocket and I can't find why. See The Cash Box Doesn't Match.

title: Rake, Tips and Rakeback
headings: Rake and tips in the cash box
text: In a home game everyone usually cashes out every chip. In a club, some chips stay on the table at the end: the house's share and the dealer's tips. House Rules calls them: Rake: chips the house takes from the game, to pay for the room, cards and the like. Tips: chips players give the dealer. Rakeback: part of the rake the house gives back to players, usually to regulars or to the night's biggest losers. You record rake and tips in chips, usually once everyone has cashed out and you can see what's left. Rake and Tips in the More menu is there all night, so you can also record them earlier. The cash box, the session's money (see The Cash Box), shows them in money, at the chip value. A player's result is what they won or lost tonight, and settling up is when House Rules works out who pays whom at the end. If nobody takes rake or tips at your table, you can skip this article. The example It's the end of a night at the Maple Street Game. The game: No-Limit Hold'em, 1 chip = $0.25. The chips: six players bought 3,200 chips and cashed out 3,080. So 120 chips are left on the table. Where they go: 80 chips are the rake, $20. 40 chips are tips for Leo, who dealt tonight, $10. Then: Dave, the host, gives the $20 rake back to Marcus and Tyler, the two biggest losers, and pays Leo his $10. Record rake and tips When everyone has cashed out but chips are left, the session says Everyone Cashed Out and No chips should be left on the table (now 120). Below, a row Chips Left on the Table asks you to assign them. The session Wrapping Up: Everyone Cashed Out, No chips should be left on the table (now 120), 3,200 buy-ins, 3,080 cashed out, and the row Chips Left on the Table, 120 chips 1. Tap Chips Left on the Table. You can also tap the More button (the three dots at the top right) and choose Rake and Tips. 2. All the leftover chips start in Rake: 120. Type the rake, 80. 3. Tap the arrow at the top right of the keys. The tips get the rest, 40. 4. Check that rake and tips add up to On the table, then tap the checkmark that's now in place of the arrow. Chips Left on the Table opens the keys with Rake 120; 80 is typed, the tips take the other 40, and the session shows Ready to Settle The rake and tips keys: Rake 120, Tips 0, On the table 120, over Everyone Cashed Out with 3,200 buy-ins and 3,080 cashed out The rake and tips keys with Rake 80 typed and On the table 120 Rake and tips must add up to the chips left on the table exactly. That's the point: every chip is accounted for before you settle up. The session now says Ready to Settle, and a Rake and Tips card shows Rake 80 and Tips 40. The session Wrapping Up: Ready to Settle, Everyone has cashed out, and Rake and Tips with Rake 80 and Tips 40 To change them later, tap More, then Rake and Tips. Rake and tips in the cash box Open Cash Box and scroll down. There are two cards, both in money at the chip value. Rake: 80 chips at $0.25 is $20 collected. The other tiles show rakeback you've given, rake spent to expenses (see Expenses), and what's available, the house's money for the night. The Rake card in the Cash Box: $20 collected, $0 rakeback, $0 to expenses, $20 available, and Distribute Rakeback Tips: 40 chips is $10 set aside for the dealer, how much you've paid from cash box, and what's left. We'll pay Leo below. Give rakeback 1. In the Rake card, tap Distribute Rakeback. 2. Under Who Gets Rakeback, choose how to share it: Equally, By % or Manually. 3. Tap the players who get it. With Equally, House Rules shares everything available between them. 4. Check the Check card: Distributed is what goes to players, Kept by Host is what the house keeps. Then tap the checkmark at the top right. Distribute Rakeback opens, Marcus and Tyler are picked with Equally, $10 each, and the rakeback is saved Rakeback: Available $20, Who Gets Rakeback 2 of 6 players, Equally, Marcus $10 and Tyler $10, the others not included, and Check: Distributed $20, Kept by Host $0 To keep part of the rake, use Manually and type each player's amount, or By % and give each a share. What you don't give out shows under Kept by Host. You can't give out more than is available. Back in the cash box, the Rake card lists each player's rakeback, and available is down to $0. The Rake card after rakeback: $20 collected, $20 rakeback, $0 available, Marcus rakeback $10, Tyler rakeback $10, and the Tips card with $10 set aside, $0 paid from cash box, $10 left Rakeback is added to a player's result, and they get it at settle-up. Marcus paid $200 for 800 chips and cashed out 236, worth $59: he lost $141. With $10 rakeback he's down $131, and the cash box owes him $69, $59 for his chips plus $10. Pay the dealer Tips are money you hold for the dealer. When you hand it over: 1. In Cash Box, tap Pay Out. 2. Under Expenses and Tips, tap Dealer Tips. It shows what's left to pay, $10 left. 3. Choose Cash or Transfer, the way you pay the dealer, then tap the suggestion 10 all tips. It's recorded at once, so there's no checkmark to tap. Above the keys, Left in cash box shows what the cash box holds before you pay. Pay Out, Dealer Tips under Expenses and Tips, and the 10 all tips suggestion pays Leo Pay Out: Payout Due with Dave $163, Jenna $277, Marcus $69, Priya $137 and Tyler $88, then Players with Sam, and Expenses and Tips with Dealer Tips, $10 left The Dealer Tips keys: $0, Left to pay out $10, Left in cash box $700, Cash chosen, and the suggestion 10 all tips The toast says Tips paid out, $10. The Tips card now shows $10 paid from cash box and $0 left. The Tips card after paying: $10 set aside, $10 paid from cash box, $0 left You can't pay out more tips than were set aside. Tips don't count toward anyone's result: they belong to the dealer. Rakeback does: it's money back to the player. Questions Do I have to record rake and tips? Only if chips are left on the table. Then yes: House Rules can't settle up while chips are unaccounted for. The rake and tips don't add up to the chips on the table. They must, to the chip. If a player's cash-out was miscounted, fix the cash-out instead, see The Chips Don't Add Up. Can I give rakeback before everyone cashes out? Rakeback comes from the rake you've recorded. So no rake, no rakeback. Where does the rake money go at the end? What's available after rakeback and expenses is the house's income for the night. It isn't anyone's result, and the club's stats count it as the house's. Can I pay a pizza from the rake? Yes, see Expenses.

title: Expenses and Splitting Them
text: An expense is money spent on the night itself: pizza, drinks, the room, a new deck. Someone pays for it, and usually everyone at the table shares the cost. House Rules keeps track of both: who paid and who shares. You record an expense in the cash box, the session's money (see The Cash Box). Each player's share comes off their result, what they won or lost tonight. The one who paid gets the full amount back. Nobody hands cash around during the game: it all comes out at settle-up, when House Rules works out who pays whom at the end of the night. The example It's two and a half hours into a night at the Maple Street Game. The table: Dave, the host, with Jenna, Marcus, Priya and Tyler. The cash box holds $600. What happens: Dave orders pizza for $50 and pays for it with his own card. Who shares: all five, equally, $10 each. So Dave gets $40 back: $50 he paid minus his own $10. Add an expense 1. In the session, tap Cash Box at the bottom left, and scroll down to Expenses. 2. Tap + next to Expenses. 3. Type the name, Pizza, and tap the arrow on the right. 4. Type the amount, 50, and tap the checkmark at the top right of the keys. + next to Expenses opens a name field, Pizza is typed, then 50 on the keys, and the toast Expense recorded The Cash Box with the name field Expense, Pizza, and the keyboard The amount keys with Expense, Pizza, $50 The toast says Expense recorded, Pizza, $50, with Undo. The Cash Box still holding $600, with the toast Expense recorded, Pizza, $50, and an Undo button The cash box still holds $600: Dave paid with his own money, not from the cash box. Under Before You Settle Up, a line Pizza, not split, $50 waits for you to say who paid and who shares. The Cash Box: $600, and under Before You Settle Up, Pizza, not split, $50 Split it Tap the expense, either the line under Before You Settle Up or the row under Expenses. Split Expense opens, with three steps from top to bottom. Split Expense: Pizza, Choose who paid, $50; Paid From, Step 1 of 3, with Player, Cash Box and Hosts and the players listed; Who Shares, Step 2 of 3, 0 of 5 players, with everyone not included Step 1, Paid From. Choose where the money came from: Player: one of the players paid. Pick them in the list below. Cash Box: you paid it from the session's money. The cash box must hold enough to cover all of it. Rake: paid from the rake, the house's share of the chips, see Rake, Tips and Rakeback. Players don't share an expense paid from the rake. Hosts: the hosts paid it themselves. The hosts are whoever runs the game, like Dave, or the house in a club. You see Rake only once the session has rake. This one doesn't yet, so the screen shows three choices. Here Player is chosen, so tap Dave. The top line now says paid by Dave, and the wallet icon next to his name marks the payer. Dave is checked under Who Shares for you, with the whole $50, because so far nobody else shares it. Tap him there to take him out if he shouldn't pay a share. Until you pick who paid, the checkmark at the top right stays grey. Split Expense: Pizza, paid by Dave, $50; Dave checked under Paid From, and under Who Shares, 1 of 5 players, Dave $50 Step 2, Who Shares. Dave is already in. Tap the others who share the cost: Jenna, Marcus, Priya and Tyler. With Equally, House Rules splits the amount between everyone checked, Dave included: $50 across five is $10 each. With Manually, tap a player's amount and type their share. Step 3, Check. Split shows how much of the expense is shared out, $50 of $50, and Left to Split what's left, $0. Then tap the checkmark at the top right of the screen. Dave is picked under Paid From, Jenna, Marcus, Priya and Tyler are checked under Who Shares, $10 each, and the split is saved Who Shares, 5 of 5 players, Equally: Dave, Jenna, Marcus, Priya and Tyler, $10 each; Check: Split $50 of $50, Left to Split $0 You split the whole amount or nobody at all. With part of it split, the checkmark waits and the Check card says what's left. With nobody checked, nobody is charged and the hosts carry the expense. What changes The row under Expenses now says Pizza, paid by Dave, $50. Each share comes off that player's result: Jenna, Marcus, Priya and Tyler are each $10 down. Dave paid $50 and shares $10, so his result goes up by $40. Whatever anyone wins or loses at the table is counted on top. Until settle-up, the four show under Before You Settle Up as Jenna owes $10, Marcus owes $10 and so on. Together that's $40, the same $40 Dave is owed, and the still owed tile at the top of the cash box shows it. Dave isn't listed: the list shows only who owes. The cash box still holds $600, because no money has changed hands. Nobody has to pay now: these lines can stay unpaid until settlement. At the end of the night, House Rules puts them into the transfers along with everyone's wins and losses (see How Settle Up Works). The Cash Box after the split: Jenna, Marcus, Priya and Tyler owe $10 each, can stay unpaid until settlement, and under Expenses, Pizza, paid by Dave, $50 Change or delete an expense Tap the expense to open Split Expense again and change who paid or who shares. Swipe left on it for Edit and Delete. Delete asks you to confirm. Touch and hold it for the same choices. An expense the hosts carry alone also has Cover from Rake there, to pay it from the rake instead. An expense that isn't split yet holds up the end of the night: Close Session asks you to split it first. See Close Session Step by Step. Questions Should I record what someone buys for themselves? No. Record only what the table shares. A player's own food or drink isn't an expense of the night. I paid for the pizza from the cash box. Choose Cash Box under Paid From. The cash box goes down by $50, and the players who share it pay their part back at settle-up. If the cash box holds less than the expense, the checkmark waits. Can the house pay for the pizza? Yes. Choose Rake under Paid From, if there's enough rake, or Hosts and check nobody under Who Shares. Then nobody at the table is charged. One player didn't eat. Don't check them under Who Shares. The others split the cost between them. The amount doesn't divide evenly. With Equally, House Rules gives the extra cent to the first players under Who Shares: $10 across three is $3.34, $3.33 and $3.33. Or use Manually and type each share. Can my club split food the same way every time? Yes, your club's House Rules can set who shares food by default.

title: Close Session, Step by Step
text: When the game is over, a few things are left before everyone goes home: the last players cash out, the leftover chips get assigned, the pizza gets split, and the money changes hands. Close Session walks you through all of it, one step at a time, so nothing is forgotten. This article goes through every step on one night. For a shorter first run, see Your First Cash Game. A few words used below: Cash box: the money players have paid you, the host, for their chips. See The Cash Box. Result: what a player won or lost tonight, in money. Settle up: House Rules works out who pays whom, so everyone ends the night even. The payments it lists are called transfers. The example It's late at the Maple Street Game. The game: No-Limit Hold'em, 1 chip = $0.25. The table: six players bought 3,200 chips in all, at $100 for 400 chips. Everyone except Tyler has cashed out: Jenna bought 400, cashed out 1,108: won $177. She paid by transfer. Dave, the host, bought 400, cashed out 652: won $63. Priya bought 400, cashed out 548: won $37. Sam bought 400 without paying, cashed out 224: lost $44. Marcus bought 800, cashed out 236: lost $141. Tyler bought 800 and is still playing. The cash box: $700, $600 in cash and Jenna's $100 by transfer. Still to do: Tyler is the last at the table, with 312 chips. Once he cashes out, 120 chips are left on the table: 80 are the house's rake, 40 are tips for the dealer. Dave paid $48 for pizza that everyone ate. It's recorded but not split yet. Sam sat down without paying for his chips and still owes the cash box. Open Close Session Once everyone has cashed out, Close Session is the big button at the bottom of the session screen, in place of Rebuy. While someone is still at the table, tap More (the three dots at the top right) and choose Close Session. Here Tyler is still in, so Dave uses the menu. The Live Session with Tyler still at the table, and the More menu open: Edit Session, Rake and Tips, Close Session, House Rules, Session Log, Share Session, Hand Over Session and Delete Session The five steps Close Session lists five steps, always in this order: 1. Cash Out: everyone leaves the table. 2. Rake and Tips: the chips left on the table are assigned. 3. Expenses: every expense is split. 4. Collect: money players still owe the cash box. 5. Settle Up: who pays whom. Each step shows a number while it's waiting and a checkmark when it's done. Under its name, a line says what's left, like 1 of 6 players at the table. A step you don't need says Not needed. The current step, the first one not done, is the bright one. The big button at the bottom always does the current step, and its name changes with it: Cash Out, Rake and Tips, Split Expense, Continue, and at the end Finish Session. You can also tap a step's row to open it. Close Session: Steps with 1 Cash Out current, 1 of 6 players at the table; 2 Rake and Tips, after everyone cashes out; 3 Expenses, 1 expense to split; 4 Collect, 1 player owes $44; 5 Settle Up, who pays whom; and the Cash Out button at the bottom Step 1. Cash Out Tap Cash Out at the bottom. The players still at the table are listed. Pick the player, type the chips they hand back and tap the Cash Out button next to the digits to record it. Tyler is the only one left, so he's already picked. He hands back 312 chips: he bought 800, so he lost 488 chips, which at $0.25 is $122. Above the keys you see what he Bought in, 800 chips, his Result, −$122, and what's Left on table after him, 120 chips. For the last player at the table, Whole Stack next to the digits fills in every chip still on the table, 432 here. Use it only when no chips are left for rake or tips. The Cash Out button opens the keys for Tyler, 312 is typed and Tyler is cashed out Cash Out for Tyler: 312 chips, Bought in 800, Result −$122, Left on table 120, and Whole Stack and Cash Out next to the digits More about cash-outs: Buy-Ins, Rebuys and Cash-Outs. Step 2. Rake and Tips Cash Out now has a checkmark: Everyone cashed out. Rake and Tips says 120 chips left over. Close Session: Cash Out checked, Everyone cashed out; Rake and Tips current, 120 chips left over; and the Rake and Tips button at the bottom 1. Tap Rake and Tips at the bottom. All 120 chips start in Rake. 2. Type the rake, 80, and tap the arrow (→) at the top right of the keys. The Tips get the rest, 40, on their own. 3. Tap the checkmark. The Rake and Tips keys open with 120 in Rake, 80 is typed, the tips take 40, and the step is checked The rake and tips keys: Rake 80, Tips 0, On the table 120 If nobody takes rake or tips at your table, every chip is cashed out and this step says Not needed. If the table has fewer chips than were bought, the step asks who covers the missing chips instead, see The Chips Don't Add Up. More about rake: Rake, Tips and Rakeback. Under the step, two more rows appear: Rakeback: tap it to give part of the rake back to players. Here it's Not distributed. Kept by House: the rake that stays with the house, the host's side of the game, $20 (80 chips at $0.25). The tips, $10, are the dealer's. Step 3. Expenses Expenses says 1 expense to split, and the card below lists it: Pizza, not split, $48. Close Session: Cash Out and Rake and Tips checked, Rakeback not distributed, Kept by House $20, Expenses current with 1 expense to split, and the card Expenses to Split with Pizza, not split, $48, above the Split Expense button 1. Tap Split Expense at the bottom. The Split Expense screen opens for the pizza. 2. Under Paid From, choose Player and tap Dave. Dave is then checked under Who Shares for you. 3. Under Who Shares, tap the other five, one by one. With Equally, the $48 is split six ways, $8 each. 4. Tap the checkmark at the top right of the screen. You're back in Close Session. Split Expense: Who Shares, 6 of 6 players, Equally, Dave, Jenna, Marcus, Priya, Sam and Tyler, $8 each; Check: Split $48 of $48, Left to Split $0 With several expenses, the button takes you through them one by one. Each share comes off that player's result, and Dave gets the $48 back. More about splitting: Expenses. Step 4. Collect Expenses has a checkmark: All expenses are split. Collect says 1 player owes $52. Close Session: Cash Out, Rake and Tips and Expenses checked, Kept by House $20, Collect current, 1 player owes $52, and the Cash card with Should be in cash $600, Not counted yet, and Count Cash Why $52? Sam bought 400 chips, $100, without paying. He cashed out 224 chips, worth $56, and his pizza share is $8. So he owes $100 − $56 + $8 = $52. Before the pizza was split, the step said $44. The cash box holds $700, but only $600 of it is cash: Jenna's $100 came by transfer. Two cards are under the steps: Cash: Should be in cash is the cash House Rules expects you to hold, $600. It counts only cash, not transfers. Tap Count Cash to count your bills against it before you hand any out, see The Cash Box. Owes the Cash Box: everyone who still owes, here Sam owes $52. Further down: Cash with Should be in cash $600, Not counted yet, and Count Cash; then Owes the Cash Box, optional, unpaid amounts go to transfers, with Sam owes $52, and the Continue button Sam pays his $52 in cash: 1. Tap Sam owes. The payment keys open. 2. Cash is chosen. Tap 52 all owed next to the digits. 3. Tap the checkmark at the top right of the keys. Sam owes is tapped, the payment keys open, 52 all owed fills in the amount, and the payment is collected The payment keys for Sam: $0, Owes $52, Cash box after $700, Cash chosen, a Note row, and the suggestion 52 all owed Once nobody owes, Collect gets its checkmark, Everyone has paid, and you move straight on to Settle Up. Collect is optional. If a player can't pay tonight, tap Continue at the bottom: what they owe goes into the transfers in the next step. More about it: When a Player Pays Later. Step 5. Settle Up The last step lists the transfers that settle the night: Settle Up, 0 of 5 marked. Here they're all From Cash Box: Dave hands each player their money from the cash box, which now holds $752. Dave is on the list too: his $203 is the part of the box that's his, so he just keeps it. Settle Up scrolled down: From Cash Box transfers to Dave $203, Priya $129, Tyler $70 and Marcus $51, each with a line explaining it, and Close for Now at the bottom. Jenna's $269 is above, off screen Each transfer explains its amount. Tyler's line reads Game −$122, expense share −$8, paid in +$200: he lost $122, owes $8 for pizza and paid $200 for his chips, so he gets $70 back. The five transfers: Jenna, $269: won $177, pizza −$8, paid in $100. Dave, $203: won $63, gets back $48 for the pizza, pizza −$8, paid in $100. Priya, $129: won $37, pizza −$8, paid in $100. Tyler, $70: lost $122, pizza −$8, paid in $200. Marcus, $51: lost $141, pizza −$8, paid in $200. Together they're $722, and $30 stays in the box. Nothing for Sam: he paid what he owed in step 4. How House Rules finds these transfers: How Settle Up Works. When money moves, tap the transfer, then Mark as Paid. The full amount is already filled in. A marked transfer gets a checkmark and is struck through. See Marking Transfers Done. Finish or close for now While any transfer is still open, the button at the bottom says Close for Now. Tap it and confirm: the session waits in a Needs Settling group, a list of sessions with open transfers, in the Lobby and on the club screen, and the open transfers show in Who Owes (see Who Owes and Reminders). When the money comes in, open the session, tap Close Session and mark the rest. Close Session for Now? 5 transfers are still open. The session waits until they're marked. A Close for Now button To keep the session open and carry on marking, tap anywhere on the screen outside this box. Once every transfer is marked, the button says Finish Session. The end of the transfer list: Tyler $70 and Marcus $51 checked and struck through like the others above, and Finish Session at the bottom Tap Finish Session. The session ends and shows Session Ended with everyone's results. These include the pizza: Dave is up $40 for it, everyone else down $8. So the winners have +$301 in all, and the three losers −$331. The $30 between them is the rake and tips, $20 and $10, and it's exactly what's left in the Cash Box. Session Ended for the Maple Street Game: This session is finished and can't be changed. To fix a mistake, reopen it. Results for 6 players, +$301 won by 3 players, −$331 lost by 3 players, 3,200 buy-ins, 120 rake and tips, 3,080 cashed out, Rake 80 and Tips 40, and Cash Box $30, Settlement and a lock at the bottom A finished session can't be changed by accident. To fix a mistake, tap the lock at the bottom right to reopen it. Transfers you already marked stay marked. Questions Do I have to do the steps in order? The button always does the first step that isn't done. You can tap the rows of Cash Out, Rake and Tips and Expenses to open them, but Settle Up waits until steps 1 to 3 are done and Collect is done or skipped with Continue. Can I close the session while someone is still playing? Yes, from More, Close Session. Step 1 is then to cash them out. A step says Not needed. There's nothing to do there tonight, like Rake and Tips when every chip was cashed out, or Expenses when there are none. I closed for now. Where's the session? In the Lobby and on the club screen, under Needs Settling. Open it and tap Close Session to carry on with the transfers. Can I share the transfers with the players? Yes. On the Settle Up step, tap the share button at the top right. See Sharing Results.

title: How Settle Up Works
headings: Night 1: everyone pays at the end
text: At the end of the night some players are up, some are down, and some money is already in your hands. Settle up is how House Rules turns all of that into a short list of payments, so that everyone ends the night even. Each payment on the list is a transfer: who pays, who gets it, how much. You see the transfers in the last step of Close Session, see Close Session, Step by Step. This article explains where they come from, on two nights at the Maple Street Game. Dave is the host: he runs the game, holds the money and plays too. What goes into a result A player's result is what they won or lost tonight, in money: The chips they cashed out minus the chips they bought, times the chip value, what one chip is worth (see Chip Value). Plus any rakeback they got, part of the house's share given back (see Rake, Tips and Rakeback). Plus expenses they paid for, minus their expense share, their part of a shared cost like pizza (see Expenses). Money a player paid you for chips, or got back from you, doesn't change their result. It changes how much is still owed to or by them. That money sits in the cash box: the money players have paid you, the host, for their chips (see The Cash Box). How the transfers are built House Rules builds the list in three passes: 1. From Cash Box. The money in the cash box goes to the players it owes, the biggest amount first, until the box is empty. You hand it out. 2. Between Players. Players still owed money get it straight from players who lost, the biggest loser paying the biggest winner first. That keeps the list short. 3. To Cash Box. Whatever a player still owes after that, they pay to you. The transfers come in these three groups, in that order. A group with nothing in it isn't shown. Night 1: everyone pays at the end On this night nobody paid for chips during the game: everyone played on Not Yet, the payment choice for "pay later" (see When a Player Pays Later). The cash box is empty. There's no rake, no tips and no pizza. 1 chip = $0.25, so 400 chips cost $100. Dave plays and wins. Jenna bought 400 chips, cashed out 1,108: +$177. Dave bought 400, cashed out 652: +$63. Priya bought 400, cashed out 548: +$37. Tyler bought 400, cashed out 92: −$77. Marcus bought 800, cashed out nothing: −$200. The winners are up $277 in all, and the losers are down the same $277. In Close Session, Collect says 2 players owe $277: Marcus and Tyler. The Cash card shows Should be in cash $0, because nobody has paid you anything. Dave doesn't collect from them now: he taps Continue, so what Marcus and Tyler owe goes into the transfers. Close Session: Cash Out checked, Rake and Tips and Expenses Not needed, Collect current with 2 players owe $277, Settle Up waiting, and the Cash card with Should be in cash $0 With nothing in the cash box, every transfer is Between Players. Four transfers settle the night. A transfer is marked once you record it as paid, so 0 of 4 marked means none is paid yet. Marcus → Jenna, $177. The biggest loser pays the biggest winner. Jenna is done. Marcus → Dave, $23. The rest of Marcus's $200 goes to the next winner. Tyler → Dave, $40. Dave was up $63 and has $23, so Tyler pays him the other $40. Tyler → Priya, $37. The rest of Tyler's $77. Settle Up, 0 of 4 marked: Between Players, Marcus → Jenna $177, Marcus → Dave $23, Tyler → Dave $40, Tyler → Priya $37, each with a bell Five players, four transfers. Marcus and Tyler pay the winners directly, and the money never passes through the host: Dave only gets his own $63. The bell next to a transfer between players sends the payer a reminder, see Who Owes and Reminders. Night 2: the usual night This night is the one from Your First Cash Game. Sam joins the five, and 1 chip is still $0.25. The chips: six players bought 3,200 chips and cashed out 3,080. Sam bought 400, $100, and cashed out 224. The other 120 went to the house: 80 chips of rake, $20, and 40 chips of tips for the dealer, $10. The pizza: Dave paid $48, and all six share it, $8 each. The cash box: $700. Everyone paid for their chips except Sam: Jenna $100 by transfer, the rest $600 in cash. Rakeback, part of the rake given back to players: none tonight, so the step says Not distributed. The results, with the pizza: Jenna: won $177, pizza −$8, result +$169. Dave: won $63, +$48 back for the pizza, pizza −$8, result +$103. Priya: won $37, pizza −$8, result +$29. Sam: lost $44, pizza −$8, result −$52. Tyler: lost $122, pizza −$8, result −$130. Marcus: lost $141, pizza −$8, result −$149. Sam lost $44 at the table and shares the pizza, so his result is −$52. He hasn't paid anything yet, so he owes all $52. In Close Session, Dave skips Collect with Continue, so Sam's $52 goes into the transfers. Seven transfers settle the night. Close Session: the steps checked, Rakeback Not distributed, Kept by House $20, Settle Up current with 0 of 7 marked, and From Cash Box, 0 of 5, starting with Jenna $269 From Cash Box First, the cash box pays out what it holds, $700. What each player gets is their result plus what they paid in: they get back their own money, and their win or loss on top. From Cash Box: Jenna $269, Dave $203, Priya $129, Tyler $70 and Marcus $29, each with a line like Game +$177, expense share −$8, paid in +$100; then Between Players, Sam → Marcus $22 Under each name, a line explains the amount: Jenna, $269: Game +$177, expense share −$8, paid in +$100. Dave, $203: Game +$63, paid for expenses +$48, expense share −$8, paid in +$100. Priya, $129: Game +$37, expense share −$8, paid in +$100. Tyler, $70: Game −$122, expense share −$8, paid in +$200. He lost, but he paid in more than he lost, so he gets the difference back. Marcus, $29: Game −$141, expense share −$8, paid in +$200, from Sam −$22. Marcus is owed $51 in all, but the box runs out first: $269 + $203 + $129 + $70 is $671, so only $29 is left for him. The rest, $22, comes from Sam, and his line says so: from Sam −$22. Dave is on the list too. His $203 is the part of the cash box that's his, so he just keeps it. Between Players Sam → Marcus, $22. Marcus is the only one still owed, and Sam is the only one who still owes. So Sam pays Marcus directly. To Cash Box Sam, $30, owed for the session. Sam owed $52 and paid Marcus $22. The other $30 comes to you. Why $30? The results add up to −$30: winners +$301, losers −$331. That $30 is the house's $20 of rake and the dealer's $10 of tips, chips that left the game. The cash box paid out everything it held, the house's money too, so the last player who still owes pays it back in. The end of Settle Up: Priya $129, Tyler $70 and Marcus $29 from the cash box, Between Players with Sam → Marcus $22, and To Cash Box with Sam, owed for the session, $30 When every transfer is done, the cash box holds exactly $30: $20 rake for the house and $10 for the dealer. Cash and transfers The cash box pays out $700, but you hold only $600 of it in cash: Jenna's $100 went to your bank. Handing out $700 in cash would leave you $100 short. So pay at least $100 of it by bank or payment app. For example, send Jenna her $269 by transfer: you hand out $431 in cash and keep $169, the same $169 that left your bank on top of her $100. Record it with Mark Paid by Transfer (touch and hold the transfer), so that Count Cash, the check of the cash in your hands, expects the right amount. See Marking Transfers Done. The list is built when you reach Settle Up. If you then change the rake, tips, rakeback or an expense in Close Session, House Rules builds it again. Questions Why does a player who lost get money from the cash box? Because they paid for their chips first. Tyler paid $200 and lost $130 with the pizza, so $70 of his money comes back. Why doesn't Sam pay the cash box all $52? Because Marcus is still owed $22 after the box is empty. Paying Marcus directly saves a step: Sam doesn't pay you so that you can pay Marcus. Can I choose who pays whom? No, House Rules works out the list, and you can't pick who pays whom. You can record a partial payment, and the rest stays open, see Marking Transfers Done. Nobody owes anybody. Then there are no transfers. Settle Up shows each player's result, and you finish the session with the button at the bottom. A transfer looks wrong. See A Transfer Looks Wrong.

title: Marking Transfers Done
headings: Paid by bank: Mark Paid by Transfer
Paid in cash: tap and Mark as Paid
Part of the amount: Record Payment
text: At the end of the night, Settle Up lists the transfers: who pays whom, and how much. As money changes hands, you mark each transfer as paid. When every transfer is marked, you finish the session. Where the list comes from is in How Settle Up Works. The example It's the end of a night at the Maple Street Game. Dave is the host: he runs the game, holds the money and plays too. 1 chip = $0.25. The cash box, the money players paid Dave for their chips: $700. Jenna paid $100 by bank transfer, the rest $600 in cash. Sam hasn't paid yet. The list: seven transfers. From Cash Box: Jenna $269, Dave $203, Priya $129, Tyler $70, Marcus $29. Dave hands this money out. Between Players: Sam → Marcus, $22. Sam pays Marcus directly. To Cash Box: Sam, $30. Sam pays Dave. Where the amounts come from: each line under a name shows it, for example Jenna's Game +$177, expense share −$8, paid in +$100: she won $177, her share of the pizza is $8, and she gets back the $100 she paid for her chips. Dave paid $48 for the pizza, so his line also has paid for expenses +$48. How the list is built is in How Settle Up Works. What happens: Dave sends Jenna her $269 by bank. He pays the others in cash and keeps his own $203. Sam pays Marcus $22, but has only $20 for Dave, so $10 stays open. You find the list in the last step of Close Session, Settle Up (see Close Session, Step by Step). Each transfer has a circle on the left. 0 of 5 under a group means none of its five transfers is marked yet. Settle Up, From Cash Box, 0 of 5: Jenna $269, Dave $203, Priya $129, Tyler $70 and Marcus $29, each with an empty circle and a line like Game +$177, expense share −$8, paid in +$100; then Between Players with Sam → Marcus $22 Paid by bank: Mark Paid by Transfer The five transfers from the cash box add up to $700, but Dave holds only $600 in cash: Jenna's $100 is in his bank. If he paid everyone in cash, he'd be $100 short. So he pays Jenna, the biggest one, by bank. A cash box transfer counts as cash unless you say otherwise, so tell House Rules it went by bank. Then Count Cash, the check of the cash in your hands, expects the right amount. 1. Touch and hold Jenna. 2. Choose Mark Paid by Transfer. Touch and hold Jenna opens a menu with Mark as Paid, Mark Partial Payment and Mark Paid by Transfer; Mark Paid by Transfer is chosen and Jenna's row is checked The menu over Jenna's transfer: Mark as Paid, Mark Partial Payment, Mark Paid by Transfer Jenna's row is checked and crossed out, and the group says 1 of 5. From Cash Box, 1 of 5: Jenna checked and crossed out, $269; Dave, Priya, Tyler and Marcus still open The menu has two more choices: Mark as Paid marks the full amount in cash, and Mark Partial Payment opens the keys, like a tap. Paid in cash: tap and Mark as Paid Dave plays too, and the cash box owes him $203 like anyone else. He takes it from the cash box himself, so it's still a transfer to mark. 1. Tap Dave. The keys open with the full amount, $203, and Full amount under it. 2. Tap Mark as Paid at the top right of the keys. Tapping Dave opens the keys with Cash Box → Dave, $203, Full amount; Mark as Paid checks the row The keys are the number pad that opens at the bottom. The 203 All button next to the digits puts the full amount back if you've changed it. The keys for Cash Box → Dave: $203, Full amount, the suggestion 203 All, and Mark as Paid at the top right A marked cash box transfer also records the money in the cash box: a payout to the player, or a payment from them. You don't record it twice. From Cash Box, 2 of 5: Jenna and Dave checked and crossed out, Priya, Tyler and Marcus still open Marked by mistake Say Dave tapped his row by accident. Tap a checked transfer to take the mark off. It's open again, and its cash box entry goes with the mark. From Cash Box, 1 of 5: Jenna still checked, Dave open again with $203 To mark it again, Dave taps his row and Mark as Paid. Between players: Confirmed By Sam pays Marcus $22 directly. Dave doesn't hold that money, so the keys ask who says it was paid. 1. Tap Sam → Marcus. 2. Confirmed By is a menu: tap it to choose Marcus confirmed, Sam showed it or I saw it myself. It starts on the one who gets the money, Marcus confirmed. I saw it myself means you watched the money change hands. 3. Tap Mark as Paid. The keys for Sam → Marcus: $22, Full amount, Confirmed By Marcus confirmed, the suggestion 22 All, and Mark as Paid A transfer between players doesn't touch the cash box, and its menu has no Mark Paid by Transfer: how two players pay each other is up to them. Dave pays Priya, Tyler and Marcus in cash the same way: tap, Mark as Paid. Everything but Sam's $30 is now marked. Settle Up: Marcus checked in From Cash Box, Between Players 1 of 1 with Sam → Marcus checked, and To Cash Box 0 of 1 with Sam, owed for the session, $30 Sam's line says owed for the session: he lost at the table and hasn't paid for his chips. The results add up to −$30, because $20 of rake and $10 of dealer tips left the game. Sam's $30 brings that money back to the cash box, where it belongs to the house and the dealer. Part of the amount: Record Payment Sam has only $20 for Dave. 1. Tap Sam under To Cash Box. The keys open with $30. 2. Delete it and type 20. Under the amount: $10 stays open. The button at the top right is now Record Payment. 3. Tap Record Payment. Sam's transfer to the cash box opens the keys, 20 is typed, $10 stays open, and Record Payment saves it The keys for Sam → Cash Box: $20, $10 stays open, the suggestion 30 All, and Record Payment at the top right A partial payment changes what's still owed, so House Rules builds the list again. Sam now has a transfer of $10, with Paid $20 of $30 under it. Sam's $20 counts as a transfer of its own, so there are eight now: seven paid and Sam's $10. Settle Up says 7 of 8 marked. The transfers you marked move to Already Done, with a grey check: Done before the plan was recalculated. The plan above already counts them. They're kept as a record, and tapping them does nothing. To undo one of those, delete its payment or payout in the cash box (see The Cash Box). Settle Up, 7 of 8 marked: To Cash Box, Sam, Game −$44, expense share −$8, Paid $20 of $30, $10, with a bell; then Already Done, 7 transfers: Cash Box → Jenna $269, Cash Box → Dave $203, Sam → Marcus $22, Cash Box → Priya $129 The end of Already Done: Cash Box → Dave $203, Sam → Marcus $22, Cash Box → Priya $129, Cash Box → Tyler $70, Cash Box → Marcus $29 and Sam → Cash Box $20 So record partial payments last, after the transfers you might still want to undo with a tap. When something stays open While a transfer is open, the button at the bottom says Close for Now. Tap it, then Close for Now again: the session waits until the last transfer is marked. The bell next to Sam sends him a reminder, see Who Owes and Reminders. Close Session for Now? 1 transfer is still open. The session waits until it's marked. A Close for Now button over the Close for Now button at the bottom When every transfer is marked, the button becomes Finish Session. A finished session can only be read. To change it, open the session, then its settlement, and tap Reopen. Questions I marked the wrong transfer. Tap it again. If it's already under Already Done, delete its payment or payout in the cash box. Should I mark my own transfer? Yes. Dave's $203 is his money in the cash box, and marking it records that he took it. Does a transfer between players change my cash? No. That money goes from one player to another, not through you. Where do I see what's still owed later? In the club's Who Owes, see Who Owes and Reminders.

title: Who Owes and Reminders
headings: Who Owes on the club screen
text: Not everyone pays at the table. When you close a session with transfers still open, they don't get lost: they stay with the club, in Who Owes. There you see who still owes whom, mark payments as they come in, and send reminders. A transfer is one payment from settle-up: who pays, who gets it, how much. How they're built is in How Settle Up Works, and how you mark them in Marking Transfers Done. The example It's the end of a night at the Maple Street Game. Dave is the host: he runs the game, holds the cash box, the money players paid for their chips, and plays too. In this article, "you" is Dave. Paid tonight: Dave sends Jenna her $269 by bank, keeps his own $203, and pays Priya $129 and Marcus $29 in cash. Still open: Cash Box → Tyler, $70. The cash box owes Tyler $70, but Tyler has already gone home. The money stays in the cash box for now. Sam → Marcus, $22. Sam owes Marcus. Sam → Cash Box, $30. Sam owes Dave. The next day: Sam pays Marcus his $22, and Dave sends Tyler $20 of the $70 he's owed. Close the session for now In Settle Up, the last step of Close Session, mark what's paid: a checked, crossed-out transfer is paid. Three transfers stay open, Tyler's $70 further up under From Cash Box, and Sam's two below. So the button at the bottom says Close for Now. Tap it, then Close for Now again. Settle Up: Tyler's row at the top, Marcus checked, Between Players with Sam → Marcus $22 open, To Cash Box with Sam, owed for the session, $30 open, and Close for Now at the bottom The session isn't finished: it needs settling. The Lobby shows it under Needs Settling with 1 to settle at the top, and so does the club screen. $800 not settled is the session's buy-ins, $800 of chips, not what's owed. The Lobby, 1 to settle: Needs Settling, 1 session, Mon, November 23, Maple Street Game, NLH 4/8, 6 players, $800 not settled; then Clubs with Maple Street Game Who Owes on the club screen Tap the club in the Lobby, here Maple Street Game, and scroll to the Who Owes card. $52 under Who Owes: what players owe in all. Each player who owes, with the total: Sam, 2 transfers, oldest Nov 23, $52. The card shows up to three players. You Owe, from the cash box: what the cash box still has to pay out, here Tyler's $70. That's your debt as the host, so it's apart from the players. Show All opens the full list. The club screen: Needs Settling with the Nov 23 session, and the Who Owes card, $52: Sam, 2 transfers, oldest Nov 23, $52; You Owe, from the cash box, $70; Show All When nobody owes, the card isn't there. The full list Tap Show All. Who Owes has two tabs, Open and Paid. At the top of Open: Players Owe: what players owe, $52, from 1 player. You Owe: what the cash box owes, $70. Below, one card per person, with their total. The cash box has no bell: what it owes is yours to pay. The cash box has its own card, Cash Box, for what you owe. Under each, their open transfers with the session's date, oldest first. Show All opens Who Owes, Sam → Marcus is tapped, the keys open with $22, and Mark as Paid moves it out of the list Who Owes, Open: Players Owe $52, 1 player; You Owe $70, from the cash box; Cash Box, $70, Cash Box → Tyler, Nov 23, $70; Sam, $52, with a bell, Sam → Cash Box, Nov 23, $30, and Sam → Marcus, Nov 23, $22 Mark a payment The next day Sam tells Dave he paid Marcus. 1. Under Sam, tap Sam → Marcus. The same keys as in Settle Up open, with the full amount. 2. Confirmed By is a menu, for a transfer between players only, since you didn't see that money move: Marcus confirmed, Sam showed it or I saw it myself. It starts on Marcus, who gets the money. 3. Tap Mark as Paid. The keys for Sam → Marcus: $22, Full amount, Confirmed By Marcus confirmed, the suggestion 22 All, and Mark as Paid With the full amount the button says Mark as Paid. With less, it says Record Payment, and the rest stays open. The transfer moves to Paid. Sam now owes $30. Who Owes, Open: Players Owe $30, 1 player; You Owe $70; Cash Box, Cash Box → Tyler, $70; Sam, $30, Sam → Cash Box, Nov 23, $30 A partial payment Dave sends Tyler $20 of his $70. 1. Under Cash Box, tap Cash Box → Tyler. 2. Tap ⌫ until the amount is gone, then type 20. Under it: $50 stays open. 3. Tap Record Payment. The keys for Cash Box → Tyler: $20, $50 stays open, the suggestion 70 All, and Record Payment The transfer stays in the list with what's left, $50, and paid $20 of $70 under it. You Owe is down to $50. Who Owes, Open: Players Owe $30, You Owe $50; Cash Box, $50, Cash Box → Tyler, Nov 23, paid $20 of $70, $50; Sam, $30, Sam → Cash Box, $30 Touch and hold a transfer for more choices: Mark as Paid for the full amount at once, Mark Partial Payment, and Open Session to go to the session it's from. A transfer between players also has Ask with the name of the one who gets the money, like Ask Marcus: it opens the share sheet with a message to Marcus asking whether Sam paid him. Nothing is sent until you send it. The menu over Cash Box → Tyler: Mark as Paid, Mark Partial Payment, Open Session When the last open transfer of a session is marked, that session finishes on its own. Remind a player The bell next to a player's name writes one message with everything they owe, across all sessions, and opens the share sheet, the iPhone's panel for sending things. Pick the app you message players with. Nothing is sent until you send it. The preview shows only the first line. Sam's message starts with Hi Sam,, says how many open transfers he has from Maple Street Game, lists each one, like To the cash box: $30 with the session's date, and ends with Thanks! The share sheet over Who Owes with a message starting Hi Sam, and Reminders, More, Copy and Save to Files If you set Your Payment Link in Settings, under Getting Paid, a message about money owed to the cash box includes it, so players can pay you right away. In Settle Up, the bell next to a single transfer reminds a player about that one payment only. Paid The Paid tab lists paid transfers by month, with the month's total. Each shows the session and when it was paid. A transfer between players also shows who confirmed it, like Nov 23 session, paid Nov 24, Marcus confirmed. Dave settled up after midnight, so the payments of the night say paid Nov 24 too. Tap one to open its session. Who Owes, Paid: November 2026, $672: Cash Box → Tyler $20, Sam → Marcus $22, Nov 23 session, paid Nov 24, Marcus confirmed, Cash Box → Marcus $29, Cash Box → Priya $129, Cash Box → Dave $203, Cash Box → Jenna $269 Weekly reminders Tap the gear at the top right of the Lobby to open Settings. Under Notifications: Who Owes Reminders sends you a weekly reminder while anyone owes. Game Reminders reminds you a day before a planned game and two hours before it starts. On game day it also tells you who still owes from past sessions. Settings: Help, then Data with Sync with iCloud, Back Up All Data and Restore from Backup, then Notifications with Level Change on, Game Reminders on, Who Owes Reminders off and Lock Screen on These are notifications on your phone, not messages to players. Questions Does an unpaid player get blocked from the next game? No. What they owe shows under their name on their member screen, when you seat them and when you sell them a rebuy. It doesn't block anything. Sam owes from two sessions. Both show under Sam, oldest first, and the bell sends one message for both. Why isn't You Owe added to Players Owe? They're different debts: players owe the cash box or each other, and you owe players from the cash box. I marked a payment by mistake. Open the session with Open Session or from Paid, and fix it in its settlement, see Marking Transfers Done.

title: Sharing Results
text: At the end of the night, everyone wants to know where they stand: what they won or lost, and whom they pay. House Rules writes it for you. You can send each player only their own part, share the whole list of payments in a group chat, or make a Session Report, a picture of the night. You share from Settle Up, the last step of Close Session (see Close Session, Step by Step). A transfer is one payment from settle-up: who pays, who gets it, how much (see How Settle Up Works). The example It's the end of a night at the Maple Street Game. Dave is the host: he runs the game, holds the cash box, the money players paid for their chips, and plays too. The game: 1 chip = $0.25. Rake was 80 chips, $20, and tips for the dealer 40 chips, $10. Dave paid $48 for pizza, shared by all six, $8 each. Six players: Jenna, Dave and Priya are up. Sam, Tyler and Marcus are down. Everyone paid for their chips except Sam. Seven transfers. What the cash box pays a player is what they paid for their chips plus their result: Jenna paid $100 and won $169, so she gets $269. Tyler paid $200 and lost $130, so he still gets $70 back. Sam paid nothing and lost $52, so he owes $52: $22 to Marcus and $30 to the cash box, that is to Dave. Marked: Dave has already sent Jenna her $269 by bank and marked it paid, see Marking Transfers Done. The other six are open. What Dave does: sends Sam his own message, shares the list in the group chat, and makes a Session Report. The Share button In Settle Up, tap Share at the top right, the square with an arrow. The menu opens over it with three choices: Send to Each Player: a personal message for each player. Share Transfers: the whole list as text. Session Report: an image or text with the results and transfers. The Share menu over Close Session: Send to Each Player, Share Transfers, Session Report Once the session is finished, open it from the club or the Lobby: its Settlement has the same Share button. Send to Each Player Tap Send to Each Player. The list, titled Send to Each, has the players in groups: Pays: players who owe, with what's still open. Sam, 2 transfers, $52. Receives: players who get money, like Dave, from the cash box, $203. Dave holds the cash box, so he takes his own share from it. Tyler and Marcus are down tonight but get money back, because they paid more for their chips than they lost. Jenna's is already paid, so she has All received. Even: players with nothing to pay or get, if there are any. Send to Each Player opens the list, Sam is tapped, the share sheet opens with his message, and Sam's row shows Sent Send to Each: Each player gets only their own part, 0 of 6 sent. Pays: Sam, 2 transfers, $52. Receives: Dave, from the cash box, $203; Jenna, All received; Marcus, 2 transfers, $51; Priya, from the cash box, $129; Tyler, from the cash box, $70 Tap a player. The share sheet opens, the iPhone's panel for sending things: pick the app you message players with. Nothing is sent until you send it. Each player's message has only their part: Hi Sam,, the club and the date. Your result, and How it adds up: the game, the expense share and what they paid in. Please send: the transfers they make, like Sam's $22 to Marcus and $30 to Dave. You'll receive: the ones they get. Paid ones go under Already sent: and Already received:. For a player who pays another player: Send it straight to them, not to me. Thanks! and Calculated with House Rules. If a member has a payment link saved in the club, the message to whoever pays them includes it. Back in the list, Sam's row says Sent, and the caption at the top counts 1 of 6 sent. Sent only means you tapped the row: House Rules can't tell whether the message went out. It lasts while the list is open. Send to Each: 1 of 6 sent, and Sam's row with $52 and Sent Tap ✕ at the top left to close the list. Share Transfers Tap Share, then Share Transfers. The share sheet opens with Session Settlement: the club and date, then every transfer, grouped like in Settle Up, with the open ones and the paid ones apart. Good for a group chat where everyone can see the whole picture. The share sheet over Close Session with Session Settlement, and Reminders, More, Copy and Save to Files Session Report Tap Share, then Session Report. At the top, choose Image or Text. Under Include, choose what goes in: Player Results: each player's chips, expense share and result. In is the chips they bought, in money, whether they've paid or not: Sam's in $100 is chips he still owes for. Out is what their chips were worth at the end. Transfers: who pays whom, with a check next to the paid ones. House Numbers: rake, tips and what the house keeps. Expenses are always in the report. The club remembers your choice for the next time. Session Report opens with Image chosen, and the preview scrolls through the player results, the Pizza expense and the transfers Session Report: Image and Text, Include with Player Results and Transfers on and House Numbers off, and the Preview: Session Report, Maple Street Game, November 23, 2026, 6 players, Not settled yet, 6 transfers open, then Jenna +$169, in $100, out $277, expense share −$8 Below Include is the Preview, exactly what you'll send. When some transfers are marked and others are still open, it says so at the top: Not settled yet, 6 transfers open. A session where nothing is marked yet doesn't get this line. The end of the report: Tyler −$130 and Marcus −$149, Expenses with Pizza, split equally, $8 each, $48, then Transfers with Cash Box → Jenna checked and the other six open, and Calculated with House Rules House Numbers Players may not need to see what the house took. So when you turn House Numbers on, House Rules asks first: Players will see what the house took tonight: rake, tips and what the house keeps. Tap Show House Numbers. The question over the House Numbers switch: Players will see what the house took tonight: rake, tips and what the house keeps. Show House Numbers The report gets a House part: Rake and house fee $20 is what the house took. Kept by House $20 is what it keeps after rakeback, all of it here, since no rakeback was given. Dealer tips $10 goes to the dealer. See Rake, Tips and Rakeback. The report with House: Rake and house fee $20, Kept by House $20, Dealer tips $10, between the Pizza expense and the Transfers Image or text Image makes a picture for a chat. Text makes the same report as plain text, for a message or a note. House Numbers is still on here, so the text has the house part too, further down. Session Report with Text chosen: the preview as text, Session Report, Maple Street Game, November 23, 2026, 6 players, Not settled yet, 6 transfers open, Results, Jenna: +$169 (in $100, out $277, expense share −$8), and so on Tap the checkmark at the top right. The share sheet opens: send the report to a chat, or save the image to Photos or Files. Questions Will players see each other's results in Send to Each Player? No. Each message has only that player's result and transfers. Use Share Transfers or the report to show everyone everything. Can I share before every transfer is paid? Yes. Open transfers are marked as open, and once some of them are paid the report says Not settled yet. How do I remind someone who still hasn't paid? Use the bell next to their transfer, or Who Owes on the club screen, see Who Owes and Reminders. Can I send the whole session to another phone? Yes, as a file, see Export and Import.

title: Setting Up a Tournament
headings: The next tournament starts the same
text: A tournament in House Rules starts from one sheet, New Tournament. In it you set the whole price of an entry and the rules of the night: how much goes to the prize pool and how much to the house, whether busted players can buy back in, the add-on, the guarantee, dealer tips, the tables and the blinds. Two words you'll see everywhere: The prize pool is the money the places split at the end. Buy-ins and add-ons go there, less any dealer tips. The cash box is the money players have paid you, the host. House fees and dealer tips stay in it. See The Cash Box. The example tournament The screenshots come from a tournament at the Maple Street Game. The other tournament pages use their own examples, so numbers there can differ. The club: the Maple Street Game usually plays cash, but once a month Dave, the host, runs a tournament. He expects about twelve players, so two tables. The price: a $50 buy-in for the prize pool and a $5 house fee for the club's cards and snacks, so $55 an entry. Everyone starts with 20,000 chips. The rules: players who bust can re-enter until the first break, and anyone still in can take one $20 add-on for 10,000 more chips. The money on top: Dave promises the places at least $600, and 3% of the buy-ins goes to the dealer. Tables and blinds: seats are drawn at tables of 6, the blinds go up every 20 minutes. In this story you are Dave. Open New Tournament 1. Open your club. 2. Tap + and choose Tournament. In the Maple Street Game club, + is tapped, Tournament is chosen and the New Tournament sheet opens The sheet opens with sensible starting values: a $50 buy-in, 20,000 chips, no house fee, no re-entry, no add-on, no guarantee and no tips. The club is already chosen at the top, and the game is NLH, No-Limit Hold'em. Tap PLO if you play Pot-Limit Omaha. The New Tournament sheet: Club Maple Street Game, NLH and PLO, Buy-In $50, Bounty Off, House Fee empty, Starting Stack 20,000, the note Players pay $50 per entry, all of it to the prize pool, then Re-Entry Off, Add-On off, Guarantee empty and Dealer Tips Off Tap a row to change it. A row with an amount opens the same keys at the bottom of the screen: type the number and tap the checkmark on the keys. Above the digits there's a short line on what the amount is for. A row with arrows next to its value opens a short menu. The price of an entry The first card holds everything a player pays to get in. Buy-In is what each entry adds to the prize pool. Dave keeps $50. The Buy-In keys with $50 and the line Goes to the prize pool House Fee is what the house keeps from each entry. It goes to the cash box, not the prize pool. Leave it at zero if you don't take a fee. House Fee is tapped, 5 is typed on the keys and the checkmark sets it to $5 Under the card, a note sums up what a player pays. With the fee it says Players pay $55 per entry. The fee goes to the cash box, not the prize pool. Buy-In $50, Bounty Off, House Fee $5, Starting Stack 20,000 and the note Players pay $55 per entry. The fee goes to the cash box, not the prize pool Starting Stack is the chips each entry gets. Chips never show a dollar sign, they're only for play. Bounty puts money on every player's head. Players pay it on top of the buy-in and the fee: Off, Fixed or Progressive. Dave's tournament has none. Bounties have their own article, Fixed Bounties and PKO. Re-entry and the add-on Re-Entry decides whether a player who busts can pay again and come back with a fresh stack. Tap the row and choose how long that stays possible: Off: one entry per player. Until Level 4, Until Level 6 or Until Level 8. Until First Break or Until Second Break. The Re-Entry menu: Off, Until Level 4, Until Level 6, Until Level 8, Until First Break and Until Second Break Dave picks Until First Break. A re-entry costs the same as an entry, $55 here. Add-On gives each player one extra stack at its own price. Turn it on and two rows appear: Add-On Price: what the add-on costs. All of it goes to the prize pool, there's no house fee on an add-on. Add-On Chips: the chips it gives. When you turn it on, the price starts at the buy-in and the chips at half the starting stack. Dave changes the price to $20 and keeps 10,000 chips. The note under the card reminds you: One add-on per player. Re-Entry Until First Break, Add-On on, Add-On Price $20, Add-On Chips 10,000 and the note One add-on per player Recording entries, re-entries and add-ons during the night is in Entries, Re-Entries and Add-Ons. Guarantee and dealer tips Guarantee is the least the places split. If the buy-ins come up short, the house fee covers the gap first and you add the rest. Leave it at zero for no guarantee. The Guarantee keys with $600 and the line The places split at least this much. Zero for no guarantee Dealer Tips sets aside money for the dealer. It comes off the top of the buy-ins and stays in the cash box for the dealer: Off: no tips. Percent: a share of the buy-ins, from 1% to 20%. It starts at 3%. Amount: one sum for the whole tournament. The Dealer Tips menu: Off, Percent and Amount Dave picks Percent and keeps 3%. The note under the card sums up both rules: The house fee covers a guarantee shortfall first, you add the rest. Dealer tips come off the top of the buy-ins. Guarantee $600, Dealer Tips Percent, Tips, % 3% and the note about the house fee and dealer tips, with the Tables card below: Draw Seats on, Seats per Table 9, Tables Auto How the guarantee and tips change the money the places split is worked through in Prize Pool and Payouts. Tables The Tables card is for a tournament where House Rules hands out seats. Draw Seats: on, and House Rules gives players random seats when you draw them. Late entries go to the shortest table. Turn it off if you seat people yourself, and the other two rows disappear. Seats per Table: from 2 to 10. It starts at 9. Tables: Auto opens as many tables as the players need, or pick a number from 1 to 8. Dave's table seats six, so he sets Seats per Table to 6 and leaves Tables on Auto. Tables: Draw Seats on, Seats per Table 6, Tables Auto, then Blinds: Pace Standard, Level Length 15 min, Breaks Every 4 levels, and Payouts Auto Drawing seats and moving players during the night is in Tables and Seats. Blinds The Blinds card sets the tournament's blind timer: Pace: the blind structure. Standard is a good start, Turbo goes up faster, Deep Stack slower. Structures you made yourself in the Blind Timer are in the same menu, see Blind Structures and Templates. Level Length: minutes per level, from 1 to 180. The keys suggest 10, 15, 20 and 30. Breaks: None, or a break every 3, 4, 5 or 6 levels. Under the card you see the first levels, how many levels the pace has and how long the whole structure runs, breaks included. Standard has 12 levels. Dave sets Level Length to 20 min and keeps a break every 4 levels: 12 levels of 20 minutes plus two breaks, ≈ 4h 20m. The Level Length keys with 20 and suggestions 10, 15, 20 and 30 min Level Length 20 min, Breaks Every 4 levels, the preview 50 / 100, 75 / 150, 100 / 200, 150 / 300, and 12 levels, about 4h 20m, then Payouts Auto Running the timer during play is covered in Running the Timer. Payouts The last row, Payouts, says Auto. Auto pays more places as more players enter: 1 place up to 4 entries, 2 up to 7, 3 up to 15, 4 up to 24, then 5. You change places and percents later, on the tournament's Payouts screen. Start the tournament Tap the checkmark at the top right. If something is missing, a line in the sheet says what, like Set the buy-in., and the tournament doesn't start until you fix it. The tournament opens at once, and its blind timer is already running at Level 1. There are no players yet, so nobody has paid into the prize pool and the whole guarantee would come from you: $600 guaranteed, $600 from you. Every entry's buy-in, and then the house fees, cut the part from you, until the prize pool reaches $600 on its own. Live Tournament with the timer at Level 1, 50 / 100, 19:47, Prize Pool $600, 0 entries, $600 guaranteed, $600 from you, Payouts 1st 100% $600, and Cash Box, Player Out and + at the bottom Now add the players with +. See Entries, Re-Entries and Add-Ons. Change the money later The guarantee, dealer tips and payouts can still change after the start. Tap the More button (three dots) at the top right and choose Payouts. The tournament's More menu: Payouts, Tables, House Rules, Blind Timer, Share Tournament, Hand Over Tournament and Delete Tournament The Payouts screen has the places, Guarantee, Dealer Tips and Tips, %, and at the bottom Where the Money Goes: what the guarantee adds, the prize pool and what comes from you. The screen calls the gap between the buy-ins and the guarantee the overlay. The Payouts screen: Places Paid Auto (1), Round To $1, 1st 100% $600, Guarantee $600, Dealer Tips Percent, Tips, % 3% Where the Money Goes: Guarantee +$600, $600 guaranteed, Prize Pool $600, From You $600, and the note The house fee covers the overlay first. You add the rest to the cash box Entries you've already recorded keep the price they were paid at. The Payouts screen is explained in full in Prize Pool and Payouts. The next tournament starts the same House Rules remembers the club's last tournament. Next month, when Dave taps + and Tournament again, the sheet opens with the same buy-in, fee, re-entry, add-on, guarantee, tips, tables and blinds, and the same game. Back in the club, + and Tournament open New Tournament with $50, $5, 20,000, Until First Break and the $20 add-on already filled in New Tournament with Buy-In $50, House Fee $5, Starting Stack 20,000, Re-Entry Until First Break, Add-On on, Add-On Price $20, Add-On Chips 10,000 Good to know The house fee and dealer tips never go into the prize pool. Both stay in the cash box. The add-on pays no house fee: all of it goes to the prize pool. Re-entry closes by the tournament's own blind timer. If the timer isn't running, re-entry stays open and it's your call. To close the sheet without starting anything, tap the cross at the top left. Related Entries, Re-Entries and Add-Ons Tables and Seats Prize Pool and Payouts Fixed Bounties and PKO The Cash Box

title: Entries, Re-Entries and Add-Ons
text: During a tournament, every time a player pays to play you record it in House Rules: an entry puts a player in the tournament with the starting stack; a re-entry brings back a player who busted, with a fresh stack, for the same price as an entry; an add-on gives a player who is still in one extra stack, at its own price. From these House Rules counts the prize pool, the chips in play, the places paid and the money in your cash box. Every entry and re-entry pays the full price, buy-in plus house fee. An add-on pays its own price, and all of it goes to the prize pool. The example tournament All the screenshots come from one tournament at the Maple Street Game. Dave, the host, records everything on his phone, so in this story you are Dave. The price: a $50 buy-in plus a $5 house fee, $55 an entry, for 20,000 chips. Re-entry is open until Level 4. The add-on is $20 for 10,000 chips. How these are set is in Setting Up a Tournament. Twenty minutes in: Dave, Jenna, Marcus, Priya, Sam and Tyler are in. Everyone has paid except Sam, who'll pay later. That's a $300 prize pool and $275 in the cash box. What happens next, in this order: Kevin arrives late. Then Rosa, a friend of Jenna's who has never played at the club. Tyler busts and re-enters. Later Jenna, Marcus and Dave take the add-on. Live Tournament: Prize Pool $300, 6 entries, $30 house fee, 6 of 6 players left, 20,000 avg stack, 120,000 chips in play, Payouts 1st 65% $195 and 2nd 35% $105, and $275, Player Out and + at the bottom The bar at the bottom of the tournament has three buttons: the cash box with the money you hold, Player Out, and +. Scroll down and you find Still In, the list of players who are still playing, one row each. Add a player Tap + and choose Add Player. The + menu open over the tournament with Add-On and Add Player The Add Player sheet opens. At the top there's a search field, then the Paid switch, New Member and the Club Members who aren't in the tournament yet. The Add Player sheet: Search Members, Paid on with $55 goes to the cash box now, New Member, and Kevin under Club Members Paid or not Before you tap a name, check Paid: On when the player has paid you. The note under it says what goes to the cash box now, $55 here. Off when they'll pay later. The player is in the tournament anyway and owes the entry until they pay you in the cash box. See The Cash Box. Sam played on credit like this: his row in Still In says owes $55. A club member Tap their name. That's the whole entry: the player is in, with the starting stack, and a short message slides up at the bottom of the screen, Kevin is in, $55 paid. Add Player with All club members are already in the tournament, and the message Kevin is in, $55 paid with an Undo button The sheet stays open, so you can add several players in a row. Tap the cross at the top right when you're done. Tapped the wrong name? Tap Undo in the message right away. The entry goes, and so does its payment in the cash box. Kevin is back in the list. Add Player with Kevin back under Club Members The message stays only a few seconds. If it's gone, see Mistakes below. Someone new Rosa has never played at the club, so she isn't in the list. Dave types her name in the search field and taps Add “Rosa”. She becomes a club member and is in the tournament at once, paid, like any other entry. You can also tap New Member and type the name there. Kevin is tapped in Club Members, then Rosa is typed in Search Members and Add Rosa puts her in the tournament The search field with Rosa typed, Paid on, and Add Rosa below it Back in the tournament, the two late entries are counted: 8 entries, a $400 prize pool and $40 of house fees. The places paid follow the entries when payouts are on Auto, the default: 2 places up to 7 entries, 3 places from 8. See Prize Pool and Payouts. Prize Pool $400, 8 entries, $40 house fee, 8 of 8 players left, 160,000 chips in play, Payouts 1st 50% $200, 2nd 30% $120, 3rd 20% $80, and $385 in the cash box A re-entry Tyler loses all his chips early. Re-entry is open until Level 4, so he pays again and comes back. 1. Tap Player Out. 2. Tap the Player row at the top of the sheet and pick Tyler from the list. 3. Choose Re-Enter instead of Out in 8th. 4. Check Paid, the same as for an entry. 5. Tap the checkmark at the top right of the sheet. The Player Out sheet: Player Tyler, Re-Enter checked, Out in 8th, the note Re-entry closes after Level 4, Paid on and New stack of 20,000, $55 to the cash box Player Out is tapped, Tyler is picked, Re-Enter is chosen and the checkmark records the re-entry Tyler stays in the tournament with a new 20,000 stack, and his row now shows 2 entries. The prize pool grows by $50 and the cash box by $55. A note under Re-Enter and Out in 8th tells you when re-entry closes, Re-entry closes after Level 4 here. After that, the sheet has no Re-Enter: a busted player is out. When re-entry closes You choose how long re-entry stays open when you set up the tournament: until a blind level or until a break. See Setting Up a Tournament. It closes by the tournament's own blind timer. If the timer isn't running, re-entry stays open, and whether a player may still re-enter is up to you. Re-entry is for a player who just busted. Marking players out is in When a Player Is Out. The add-on Each player who is still in can take one add-on. There are two ways to record it. From the + menu Good for the add-on break, when several players take it at once. 1. Tap + and choose Add-On. 2. Check Paid. 3. Tap each player who takes it. The Add-On sheet: Paid on, 10,000 more chips for $20, all of it to the prize pool. One add-on per player, and the start of the Still In list: Dave, Jenna, Kevin and Marcus Each tap records the add-on at once and shows a message, like Add-on for Marcus, $20 paid, with Undo. The player leaves the list, since it's one add-on per player. + and Add-On open the sheet, Jenna and then Marcus are tapped and leave the list The Add-On sheet with the message Add-on for Marcus, $20 paid and Undo, and the list starting with Dave, Kevin, Priya and Rosa From a player's row Good for one player. Touch and hold the player's row in Still In and choose Add-On. This records a paid add-on right away, with the same message and Undo. For an add-on that isn't paid yet, use the + menu with Paid off. Dave's row held in the Still In list with a menu of Player Out and Add-On The Still In list with the message Add-on for Dave, $20 paid and Undo Players who took the add-on say add-on under their name. Prize Pool $510, 9 entries, 3 add-ons, $45 house fee, 8 of 8 players left, 26,250 avg stack, 210,000 chips in play, Payouts 1st 50% $255, 2nd 30% $153, 3rd 20% $102 Still In: Dave add-on, Jenna add-on, Kevin, Marcus add-on, Priya, Rosa, Sam owes $55, and Tyler with 2 entries What's in the cash box Tap the cash box button at the bottom left. Dave holds $500: eight paid entries at $55, Tyler's re-entry among them, plus three add-ons at $20. Sam's $55 is still owed. The rake tile is the house fee on all 9 entries, $45, Sam's $5 included. Everything else in the box belongs to the prize pool. Cash Box: In Cash Box $500, $500 collected, $0 paid out, $55 still owed, $45 rake, and Before You Settle Up: Sam owes $55, can stay unpaid until settlement Sam can pay any time before the end. When he does, tap Collect at the bottom of the cash box. See The Cash Box. Mistakes Right after an entry or add-on: tap Undo in the message. It removes the payment from the cash box too. A payment recorded by mistake, after the message is gone: open the cash box, find it under Operations, swipe it left, tap Delete and confirm. A player you added by mistake: hold their row and choose Delete Player. The item appears only once the player has nothing in the cash box, so delete their payment first. A wrong bust: see When a Player Is Out. A wrong re-entry: tap Undo in the message, like Tyler re-entered, while it's still there. Good to know Every entry and re-entry pays the full price, buy-in plus house fee. The add-on pays no house fee. One add-on per player, only for players still in. If House Rules draws the seats, a late entry gets a seat at the shortest table. See Tables and Seats. Auto pays more places as entries grow. Re-entries count as entries. Related Setting Up a Tournament When a Player Is Out Prize Pool and Payouts The Cash Box

title: Tables and Seats
headings: Show the seats to the players
Follow the hints as players go out
text: When a tournament has more players than one table can hold, House Rules can seat everyone for you. It draws a random seat for each player, tells you when the tables get uneven and when to close one, and finally draws the final table. You read the seats off your phone and say them out loud. You don't have to use this. If your game fits at one table, or you prefer to seat people yourself, leave it off and nothing on this page shows up. The example tournament All the screenshots come from one night at the Maple Street Game. Dave, the host, runs the tournament on his phone, so in this story you are Dave. The price: a $50 buy-in plus a $5 house fee, $55 an entry, 20,000 chips, no re-entry. How these are set is in Setting Up a Tournament. The players: fifteen, all paid. That's a $750 prize pool and $825 in the cash box. The room: Dave's basement has three tables of 6 seats.
