Kevin buys back in at once with a new 10,000-chip stack, so Dave taps Re-entry. Now 7 of 9 players are left, with 9 entries and 90,000 chips in play, an average of 12,857, or 32 BB. After a Re-entry: Average Stack 12,857, 32 BB at Level 5, 7 of 9 Players Left, 9 Entries, 90,000 Chips in Play, 10,000 Starting Stack. A message: Re-entry, 7 of 9 left, Undo Every tap shows a message at the bottom with Undo, in case you tapped by mistake. To go back to the clock, tap More and Show Timer. The Stacks view only counts. It doesn't know who went out: the timer has no list of players or money. Leave the timer running The arrow at the top left goes back to the Lobby. The timer keeps running there: a card shows the level, the blinds and the time left, here Level 5, 200 / 400, 14:10 left. Tap the card to come back to the timer. Lobby with No Sessions Yet and a timer card: Level 5, 200/400, big blind ante 400, 14:10 left The timer keeps the right time while the phone sleeps, while you use other apps, and even if House Rules restarts. The one limit is a day: a timer started more than 24 hours ago isn't brought back when House Rules restarts. Stop the timer At the end of the night, tap Stop at the top right. House Rules asks: Stop the timer? Level alerts and the Lock Screen timer go away. The template stays loaded. Stop and Exit stops the clock and goes back to where you came from, here the Lobby. Restart from Level 1 stops the clock and stays on the timer, back at the start of the structure. Tap outside the box to keep the clock running. Stop the timer? Level alerts and the Lock Screen timer go away. The template stays loaded. Stop and Exit in red, Restart from Level 1 After Stop and Exit, the Lobby card says Blind Timer, Standard, ready to start. The template stays loaded: tap the card, and the timer is back at Level 1, Not started, for the next game. Lobby with a Blind Timer card: Standard, ready to start The timer after Stop: Standard, 8 players, Level 1, 15:00, 50/100, Not started. Start at the bottom A club tournament's own timer When you run a club tournament in House Rules, it has its own timer, made from the blinds you chose when you set it up. Open the tournament, tap More and Blind Timer. It works the same way, and its Stacks follow the tournament's own entries and knockouts. See Setting Up a Tournament. Good to know Pause before a long break in the game, and the time left stays exactly where it was. The arrows and a jump always start a level from its full time. There's one timer in the app. Loading another template stops the one that's running, after House Rules asks. Related Blind Structures and Templates Notifications and Lock Screen Timer Window on iPad

title: Timer Window on iPad
headings: Start the timer on the iPad
text: On an iPad, the Blind Timer can open in a window of its own: a big clock with nothing else on it, readable from across the room. Stand the iPad at the end of the table, and everyone sees the level, the time left and the blinds coming next. The timer window is only on the iPad: on the iPhone the timer always stays in the app. This page shows how to open the timer window, what it shows and how to close it. How the timer itself works is in Running the Timer. The example club All the screenshots come from the Maple Street Game. Dave is the host and also plays, so in this story you are Dave. The game: eight players, the built-in Standard template: 10,000 chips each and 15-minute levels starting at 50 / 100, a small blind of 50 and a big blind of 100. What happens: Dave starts the clock on his iPad, opens the timer window, and stands the iPad on the sideboard so the whole table can see it. Start the timer on the iPad On the iPad, House Rules shows a sidebar on the left. Under Library, tap Blind Timer. The templates open on the right. A template is a ready-made blind schedule: the levels, their blinds and minutes, and the breaks. Built-In has Standard, Turbo and Deep Stack, My Templates has the ones you built, and Build Step by Step at the bottom makes a new one. House Rules on iPad: the sidebar with Tonight, Clubs, Library with All Sessions, Stats and Blind Timer selected, and Settings. On the right, Blind Timer: Built-In with Standard, Turbo and Deep Stack, My Templates empty, Build Step by Step at the bottom Tap Standard. Its levels open, with Use Template at the bottom: tap it. The timer loads: Level 1, 15:00, 50 / 100, Not started. Tap Start, the big button in the middle at the bottom. The running timer on iPad: Standard, 8 players. Level 1, 14:47, 50/100. Up Next Level 2 75/150, Level 3 100/200. Previous, Pause and Next at the bottom. At the top right: Open in New Window, More, Stacks, Levels and Stop On the iPad the buttons at the bottom are bigger and have names: Previous, Pause and Next. At the top right are, from left to right, Open in New Window (an icon of a window with a plus, no label), More (three dots), Stacks, Levels and Stop. Stacks and Levels work as on the iPhone, see Running the Timer. Open the timer window Tap Open in New Window, the first icon at the top right. With a keyboard attached, you can also press Shift-Command-T, or swipe down from the top edge of the screen to show the menu bar and choose File, then Open Blind Timer in New Window. The window shows only the clock, as big as the window allows: Level 1 at the top left, and the template's name, Standard, at the top right with a round close button next to it. The time left, 14:40, across the middle, and the blinds, 50 / 100, under it. The next two levels along the bottom, each with how long until it begins: Level 2, 75 / 150, starts in 14:40, the moment this level ends, and Level 3, 100 / 200, starts in 29:40, one 15-minute level later. Previous, Pause and Next, the same buttons as in the main window. The timer window: Level 1 at the top left, Standard and a close button at the top right, 14:40 in big numbers, 50/100 under it. Along the bottom: Level 2 75/150 starts in 14:40, Level 3 100/200 starts in 29:40. Previous, Pause and Next The clock keeps running between the screenshots on this page, so each one shows a little less time. Here the window fills the screen. To make it smaller and place it next to House Rules, turn on Windowed Apps in the iPad's Settings, under Multitasking & Gestures. The clock grows or shrinks with the window. The screen stays on while the timer window is open, so the iPad doesn't go to sleep in the middle of a level. Keep it plugged in for a long tournament. One clock, two windows There's only one timer in the app. The window shows the same clock as the main window, and both control it. Dave taps Pause in the timer window when the pizza arrives: the window says Paused, the time stops at 14:33, the Pause button turns into Resume, and the main window is paused too. The timer window paused: Level 1, 14:33 dimmed, 50/100, Paused. Level 2 starts in 14:33, Level 3 in 29:33. Resume between Previous and Next He taps Resume, and both windows count down again. Close the timer window Tap the round X at the top right of the timer window, next to the template's name. Only the window closes: the timer keeps running, and the main window still shows it. Back in the main window after closing the timer window: Standard, 8 players, Level 1, 14:22, 50/100, Pause at the bottom To stop the clock, tap Stop in the main window. See Running the Timer. A club tournament's timer A club tournament you run in House Rules has its own timer, made from the blinds you chose when you set it up. Open the tournament from your club, tap More at the top right and Blind Timer, then Open in New Window. When the timer window is wide enough, for example full screen, it adds a column on the right with the tournament's players left, the average stack, the prize pool and the payouts, so the table sees what they're playing for. See Setting Up a Tournament. Good to know If the timer window is open but no timer is loaded, it says No Timer Running and asks you to pick a blind structure in the main window. Opening the window again brings the same window forward. There's never more than one. Related Running the Timer House Rules on iPad Notifications and Lock Screen Blind Structures and Templates

title: Notifications and Lock Screen
headings: The card on the Lock Screen
text: The Blind Timer doesn't need House Rules on screen. When a level ends, your phone gets a notification with the new blinds, even when it's locked or you're in another app. The Lock Screen and the Dynamic Island show the clock too, so a glance at the phone tells you how long the level has left. This page shows the two settings behind this, what the Lock Screen card and the notification look like, and what to check when something is missing. Starting and running the clock is in Running the Timer. The example club All the screenshots come from the Maple Street Game. Dave is the host and also plays, so in this story you are Dave. The game: a tournament at Marcus's place with the built-in Standard template: 8 players, 10,000 chips each, 15-minute levels starting at 50 / 100, a small blind of 50 and a big blind of 100. What happens: Dave starts the clock, puts his phone down next to his chips and plays. When level 1 runs out, the phone tells him the blinds went up. The two settings Both are in House Rules' Settings, under Notifications, and both are on from the start. To open Settings, tap the gear at the top right of the Lobby, the app's home screen. Level Change: a notification each time the timer moves to the next level on its own. Lock Screen: a card with the clock on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island, the pill-shaped area at the top of newer iPhones. Live Activities are the iPhone's name for such live cards, and this one switch controls both places. The same switch also shows a running cash game there, see Lock Screen and Quick Rebuy. Settings: Help, then Data with Sync with iCloud, Back Up All Data and Restore from Backup, then Notifications with Level Change on, Game Reminders on, Who Owes Reminders off and Lock Screen on The other switches on this screen are for club games and debts, not for the timer. Turn either timer switch off if you don't want that part. The timer itself works the same either way. Start the clock In the Lobby, tap Blind Timer, tap Standard, then Use Template, and tap Start at the bottom. More on this in Running the Timer. Dave's clock starts at Level 1, 50 / 100. The first time you start a timer, your phone asks whether House Rules may send notifications. Tap Allow. Without it there are no level alerts, and the timer shows how to turn them on in the iPhone's Settings app, under Apps, House Rules, Notifications. The running timer: Standard, 8 players, Level 1, 14:49, 50/100. Up Next Level 2 75/150 15 min, Level 3 100/200 15 min. Pause at the bottom The card on the Lock Screen Dave locks his phone. Under the clock on the Lock Screen there's now a card for the timer: The template's name, Standard, and the level, Level 1. The blinds now, 50 / 100, and the time left, 14:42, counting down. A round Pause button. Under them, the next blinds, Next: 75 / 150, and the players left with their average stack in big blinds (BB), the average stack divided by the big blind: 8 of 8 left, average 100 BB, because 10,000 chips is 100 big blinds of 100. The Lock Screen at 9:41 with the timer card: Standard, Level 1, 50/100, 14:42 and a Pause button. Next: 75/150, 8 of 8 left, average 100 BB. Under the card: Allow Live Activities from House Rules? Don't Allow, Allow The first time, the iPhone asks under the card: Allow Live Activities from House Rules? Tap Allow to keep the card. With Don't Allow, the card goes away. To turn it back on later, open the iPhone's Settings app, then Apps, House Rules, and turn on Live Activities. What you can do from the card: Tap Pause to pause the clock without unlocking the phone. The card then says Paused, and the button turns into a play button, a triangle, that resumes it. In the Dynamic Island a paused clock shows a pause sign instead of the time. Tap anywhere else on the card to open the timer in House Rules. When the level changes When the 15 minutes of level 1 run out, the timer moves to level 2 by itself, and the phone shows a notification: Level 2, Blinds 75/150. The card above it has moved on too: Level 2, 75 / 150, and the next blinds are 100 / 200. The average is now 66 BB: the same 10,000 chips, but the big blind is 150. The Lock Screen: the timer card on Standard, Level 2, 75/150, 14:36, Next: 100/200, 8 of 8 left, average 66 BB. Under it a notification from House Rules: Level 2, Blinds 75/150, now Tap the notification to open the timer. If you pause the clock, House Rules holds the notifications back, so a paused level doesn't ring when its time would have run out. When you resume, the alerts are set again for the new times. The Dynamic Island On an iPhone with the Dynamic Island, the clock moves there when you're in another app or on the Home Screen. On the left it shows the level, L2 for level 2, and on the right the time left, 14:31. Touch and hold it to see the whole card, or tap it to open the timer. An iPhone without the Dynamic Island has a plain black notch or bar at the top: there, the Lock Screen card is where you see the clock. The top of the Home Screen: the Dynamic Island shows L2 on the left and 14:31 on the right Back in House Rules, the timer shows the same clock: Level 2, 75 / 150. The timer back in the app: Standard, 8 players, Level 2, 14:28, 75/150. Up Next Level 3 100/200, Level 4 150/300. Pause at the bottom When you stop the timer with Stop at the top right, the card and the level alerts go away. If something is missing No notification when the level changed: check that Level Change is on in House Rules' Settings, and that notifications for House Rules are allowed in the iPhone's Settings app, under Notifications. No card on the Lock Screen: check that Lock Screen is on in House Rules' Settings, and that Live Activities are allowed for House Rules in the iPhone's Settings app. The card went away during a long game: iOS keeps a card for about eight hours at most. Open House Rules and the card comes back. The card says Open to see the level: the timer moved on, but the phone hasn't redrawn the card yet. Just open House Rules, and the card shows the right level again. The notifications still come on time. Good to know The notification and the card show only the timer: levels, blinds, time and stacks. Money stays in the app. A club tournament's own timer sends the same notifications and has the same card. See Setting Up a Tournament. To keep the clock in view on an iPad, open it in its own window: Timer Window on iPad. Related Running the Timer Timer Window on iPad Blind Structures and Templates Settings

title: Clubs and Members
text: A club is the group you play with: your regulars, the office game, the cousins at Thanksgiving. Its members are the players in it. Add them once, and every session you run in the club builds their history: how many games they played, how much they won or lost, and when they last showed up. This page shows how to create a club, add and manage its members, and keep private tags and notes on them. Each member's numbers are in Player Stats and CSV. The example club All the screenshots come from the Maple Street Game, Dave's home game on Maple Street. Dave is the host, so in this story you are Dave. The start: Dave has just installed House Rules and creates the club. A month later: the club has had four cash games with six regulars: Dave, Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya and Sam. Dave adds Kevin, a friend from work who's coming next time, marks Tyler as a regular and writes himself a note about him. Create a club The Lobby is the screen House Rules opens on. A session is one game night. When there's no club yet, the Lobby shows No Sessions Yet with two ways in: Create Club to set the club up first, or Start Session at the bottom to go straight to tonight's game. Dave taps Create Club. The empty Lobby: No Sessions Yet, Start your first game with the button below. It goes to a club named Home Game, which you can rename later. Create Club button. Blind Timer, Not running. Start Session at the bottom If you tap Start Session instead, House Rules puts the game in a club named Home Game. To rename it later, open the club, tap the three dots at the top right, then Rename. Create Club opens a card with a name field over the keyboard. Type the club's name, here Maple Street Game, and tap a color under it. The color marks the club's name and its sessions in lists, which helps once you have more than one club. Tap the check mark at the right of the name field to save. A card over the keyboard: Maple Street Game typed in the name field, a check mark button, and a row of nine colors with the blue one picked The new club opens. It says 0 members, 0 sessions, and Set House Rules is at the bottom: the club's buy-in limits and rules, see House Rules. The + button at the bottom right of the club's screen starts the club's first session. The new club screen: Maple Street Game, 0 members, 0 sessions. No Sessions Yet, Start the club's first session with the + button below. Set House Rules. A + button at the bottom right A new club has no Members tile yet: it appears with the first session. The players you seat at the table in that session become the club's members. See Starting a Cash Game. Once you have a club, the Lobby lists it under Clubs. To make another club, tap the + next to Clubs. The club in the Lobby A month later the Lobby lists the Maple Street Game under Clubs: 6 members, 4 sessions, last played Nov 17. Tap the club to open it. The Lobby: 1 club, 4 sessions. Recent Sessions with three past games of the Maple Street Game, NLH 4/8. Clubs: Maple Street Game, 6 members, 4 sessions, Nov 17 last session, with a + next to Clubs. Blind Timer and Start Session Touch and hold a club in the Lobby to Rename or Delete it. Deleting a club deletes all its sessions and members, and it can't be undone, so House Rules asks first. The club's screen The club's screen has everything about the club in one place: Plan Next Game at the top, see Planned Games and Reminders. The Members tile: how many there are, and the biggest winner this year. Here Top: Jenna, up $236.50 in 2026. The Stats tile: $2,400 in buy-ins in 2026. It opens the club's stats, see Club Stats. Set House Rules, see House Rules. Recent Sessions, the club's games, newest first. Maple Street Game, 6 members, 4 sessions. Plan Next Game. Members tile 6, Top: Jenna +$236.50. Stats tile $2,400 total buy-ins in 2026. Set House Rules. Recent Sessions: four NLH 4/8 games with 5 or 6 players and $500 to $700 total buy-ins The three dots at the top right open More: Rename and Color change the club's name and color, and the menu also has Plan Game, All Games, New Season and Hide House Rules, which hides the House Rules card on the club's screen if you don't use it. The club's More menu: Rename, Plan Game, All Games, New Season, Color with a submenu arrow, Hide House Rules The members list Tap the Members tile. Each row shows the member's name, how many sessions they played, when they last played, and their total result for all time: green for up, red for down. Members, Maple Street Game, 6 members: Dave +$93 4 sessions, Jenna +$236.50 4 sessions, Marcus +$41.50 4 sessions, Priya −$62 3 sessions, Tyler −$92 4 sessions, Sam −$217 2 sessions. At the bottom, Search Members and a + button Add a member Players join the club when you seat them at the table, so you rarely need to add anyone by hand. To add someone before their first game, tap Add Member, the + in the bar at the bottom of the list, type the name and tap the check mark. Dave adds Kevin. Search Members, in the same bar at the bottom, finds a member by name when the list gets long. A card over the keyboard with Kevin typed in the name field and a check mark button, over the members list Kevin is now in the list with No sessions yet. Next game, Dave finds him among the club's members when he seats players. Members, 7 members: the six regulars and Kevin at the bottom, No sessions yet. Search Members and the + below Two members can't have the same name in one club. If the name is taken, House Rules says so under the field. Add a last initial, like Sam K. A member's screen Tap a member to open their screen. Tyler's shows his Result for 2026, −$92, a chart of how it went game by game, and the tiles: 4 sessions played, 50% winning sessions, −$23 per session and $0 rakeback. All of it is in Player Stats and CSV. Tyler, Maple Street Game, 4 sessions. Result for 2026 −$92 with a line chart. Tiles: 4 sessions played, 50% winning sessions, −$23 per session, $0 rakeback. Tags and Note, Only you see these: Add Tags, Add Note Tags and a note Under the numbers is Tags and Note, with the reminder Only you see these. Tags and notes stay in House Rules on your phone: they're never shared, sent to players or exported. Tap Add Tags. Every club starts with four tags: Backup, New, Pays Late and Regular. The number next to each says how many members have it. Tap a tag to give it to this member, tap it again to take it away. Dave taps Regular, and a check mark shows next to it. Tap the round check mark at the top right of the list to close it. Tags for Tyler: Backup 0, New 0, Pays Late 0, Regular 1 with a check mark. New Tag. Tap to add or remove. Swipe a tag to edit or delete it for the whole club New Tag makes your own, with a name and a color. Swipe a tag to Edit or Delete it. This changes the tag for the whole club: deleting it takes it off every member who has it, and the members stay in the club. Then tap Add Note and write whatever helps you host. Dave writes Pays by Venmo. Brings the good chips. and taps the check mark. A note can be up to 500 characters. The note card for Tyler, Note, 37/500, with Pays by Venmo. Brings the good chips. typed above the keyboard and a check mark button Both show on Tyler's screen now: the Regular tag and the note. Tyler's screen: Result for 2026 −$92, the tiles, and Tags and Note with a Regular tag and the note Pays by Venmo. Brings the good chips. In the members list, the tag shows under the member's name. The button at the top right of the list filters by tag: pick a tag to see only those members, for example only the regulars when you're inviting people to a game. Rename or delete a member Touch and hold a member in the list. A menu opens with Rename and Delete. Members list with Marcus's row lifted and a menu: Rename, Delete in red. Tyler's row shows the Regular tag Rename fixes a typo or changes a nickname. The member's past games stay with them under the new name. Delete asks first: Delete Member? The member will be removed from the club. Their past sessions stay as they are. Tap Delete Marcus to go ahead. There's no Cancel button: tap anywhere outside the box to keep him. Dave keeps him. Delete Member? The member will be removed from the club. Their past sessions stay as they are. Delete Marcus button in red, coming from Marcus's row The past sessions keep the deleted member's name and amounts, so those sessions, the club's buy-in totals and the settle-ups don't change. The member just has no row in the members list and no stats screen any more. Good to know Results count only sessions that ended: settled, or waiting for settlement. A game still in progress isn't counted yet. The same person in two clubs is two separate members, each with their own stats. To count a player's games for a club, seat them as that club's member. A guest name typed at the table becomes a member of the club too. Related Player Stats and CSV Club Stats House Rules Planned Games and Reminders Starting a Cash Game

title: House Rules
text: Every home game has its rules: how much you can buy in for, whether phones stay off the table, who pays for the pizza. House Rules is where the club keeps them. You write them once, and House Rules shows them with every session, sends them to players as text or a picture, and reminds you at the table when a buy-in is outside the limits. The rules only remind, they never stop anything. If a player buys in above the max, House Rules says so, and you still decide. This page shows how to set the buy-in limits, write the rules, pick the money settings, share the rules with players, and what the rules do during a game. Creating the club itself is in Clubs and Members. The example club All the screenshots come from the Maple Street Game, Dave's home game on Maple Street. Dave is the host, so in this story you are Dave. The club: six regulars and four cash games so far, all No-Limit Hold'em at 4/8 blinds: a small blind of 4 chips and a big blind of 8, the second number. Each chip is worth $0.25, so 400 chips cost $100. The chip value is set when you start a session, see Chip Value. What happens: Dave writes down the rules everyone has been following anyway: a buy-in from 50 to 150 big blinds, phones off the table, pay the host before you leave, straddles allowed, last orbit at 1 a.m., and cash on the table before you get chips. Then he sends the rules to the group, and at the next game House Rules reminds him of them. Open House Rules In the Lobby, the screen House Rules opens on, tap the club under Clubs. On the club's screen, tap Set House Rules under the Members and Stats tiles. Maple Street Game, 6 members, 4 sessions. Plan Next Game. Members tile 6, Top: Jenna +$236.50. Stats tile $2,400 total buy-ins in 2026. Set House Rules. Recent Sessions with four NLH 4/8 games The House Rules screen has four parts: All Games: rules for every game the club plays. Shown with every session. Cash Games: the buy-in limits, Min Buy-in and Max Buy-in, and rules only for cash games. Money: four settings for paying, food, short chips and the host, used in cash games. Tournaments: rules only for tournaments. A tournament's buy-in, starting stack and re-entries come from its own settings, not from here. See Setting Up a Tournament. House Rules, empty: All Games with Add Rule, Shown with every session. Cash Games with Min Buy-in and Max Buy-in, both empty, and Add Rule. Money with Paying, Food, Short Chips and Host, all Not Set. Tournaments below There's no Save button. Everything you change here is saved right away. The buy-in limits The limits are in big blinds (BB), not in chips or money. A buy-in of 50 BB is 50 times the big blind, so the same rule works whatever blinds you play: at 4/8 it's 400 chips, at 1/2 it's 100. House Rules turns it into chips with each session's blinds. Tap the empty box at the right of the Min Buy-in row. A keypad opens. Type 50. The card above the keys says In big blinds, and the line under it shows what that means at the club's last blinds: At 4/8, 400 chips. The keys on the right are shortcuts: 50, 100 and 200 big blinds. Tap the check mark to save. The Min Buy-in keypad: 50 typed, In big blinds, At 4/8 400 chips. Number keys with shortcuts 50, 100 and 200 big blinds on the right, a close button and a check mark Then tap the box at the right of Max Buy-in and type 150: At 4/8, 1,200 chips. The max has its own shortcuts, bigger ones: 200, 300 and 500 big blinds. The Max Buy-in keypad: 150 typed, In big blinds, At 4/8 1,200 chips. Shortcuts 200, 300 and 500 big blinds. Min Buy-in above now shows 50 BB Both rows now show 50 BB and 150 BB, and the line under the Cash Games card turns them into chips and money: At 4/8 that's 400 to 1,200 chips, $100 to $300. The money comes from the chip value of the club's last game, here $0.25 a chip. A few things to know: You can set only one of them: only a max, or only a min. The min can't be bigger than the max. If it is, the line under the number turns red and the check mark waits until you fix it. Min and max can be the same. A limit can be from 1 to 10,000 big blinds. To clear a limit, open it, delete the number and tap the check mark. Write the rules Every section has Add Rule. Tap it in All Games. A text field opens over the keyboard, with ready-made rules above it and a choice of All Games, Cash or Tournaments under it. Tap a ready-made rule to add it, or type your own. Dave taps Phones off the table, then Pay the host before you leave. Add Rule over the keyboard: an empty Rule field with a close button and a check mark, ready-made rules Phones off the table and Pay the host before you leave above it, and All Games, Cash, Tournaments under it with All Games picked The ready-made rules change with the section. Under Cash they're poker rules like Run it twice, No rabbit hunting and Stay an hour after a big win. Dave taps Straddle allowed, then types his own: Last orbit at 1 a.m., with Cash picked under the field, and taps the check mark. Add Rule with Last orbit at 1 a.m. typed and Cash picked. Ready-made rules above: Run it twice, No rabbit hunting, Stay an hour after The rules are on the screen now: two under All Games, two under Cash Games. House Rules: All Games with Phones off the table and Pay the host before you leave, an Edit button. Cash Games with Min Buy-in 50 BB, Max Buy-in 150 BB, Straddle allowed, Last orbit at 1 a.m. and Add Rule. At 4/8 that's 400 to 1,200 chips, $100 to $300. Money below, all Not Set To change the rules later: Tap a rule to change its text. Pick another section under the field to move the rule there. Cash under the field means the Cash Games section. Edit at the right of a section's title, shown once the section has rules, lets you delete rules or drag them into a new order. You can also swipe a rule to the left to delete it. A section holds up to 20 rules. A ready-made rule you've already added isn't offered again. Money The Money settings are for cash games. Each is a menu: tap it and pick an option. The Paying menu open over House Rules: Not Set with a check mark, Cash Up Front, Transfer Up Front, Settle at End Paying: how players pay for chips. Cash Up Front, Transfer Up Front or Settle at End. It picks the payment on the buy-in and rebuy keys: with Cash Up Front, every buy-in starts as Cash. See Buy-Ins, Rebuys and Cash-Outs. Food: who shares a new expense. Split Equally checks everyone, Host Pays only the host, Winners Pay the players who are up. You can still change it on each expense. See Expenses and Splitting Them. Short Chips: who pays the difference when the chips counted at the end are fewer than the chips handed out, for example when a chip fell under the table: Winners, Everyone or the Host. It's the first choice when you close the session, and you can pick another there. See Close Session, Step by Step. Host: the club member who hosts, picked from the club's members. Food and Short Chips use it when they're set to the host. Dave picks Cash Up Front, Split Equally and Dave as the host. He leaves Short Chips at Not Set. Money: Paying Cash Up Front, Food Split Equally, Short Chips Not Set, Host Dave. Paying sets the default on buy-in and rebuy keys. Food sets how a new expense is split. Short Chips is the first choice in Close Session. Tournaments with Add Rule below Send the rules to players Tap the share button at the top right, a square with an arrow pointing up. Pick Share as Text or Share as Image. The share menu at the top right of House Rules: Share as Text, Share as Image Share as Text sends the rules as a message: the All Games rules first, then Cash games: with the buy-in, here Buy-in: 50 to 150 BB (400 to 1,200 chips at 4/8, $100 to $300), the money settings and the cash rules, then the tournament rules. Share as Image sends the same as a picture in a dark card, ready for a group chat. Both open the iPhone's share sheet. Pick the app or the person to send it to. The share sheet with a picture House Rules, Maple Street Game, Reminders, Preview and More, Copy, Assign to Contact, Print and View More Settings you didn't set aren't in the message. The share button is dimmed only while the screen is completely empty: no rules, no buy-in limits and no Money settings. The House Rules card Back on the club's screen, Set House Rules has turned into a House Rules card. It shows the paying setting, Cash up front, the buy-in, Buy-in 50–150 BB, the first two rules and +2 more for the rest. Tap it to open the rules. Maple Street Game club screen: the House Rules card with Cash up front, Buy-in 50–150 BB, Phones off the table, Pay the host before you leave and +2 more. Members and Stats tiles above, Recent Sessions below If you don't use House Rules, tap the three dots at the top right of the club's screen and Hide House Rules. The card goes away. To bring it back, pick House Rules in the same menu. At the table The next week Dave starts a cash game at 4/8 again. See Starting a Cash Game. When he adds Jenna, her buy-in is already 400, the min, and it costs $100. Payment is set to Cash, from the Paying setting. The keys on the right have changed too: 400 min, 1,200 max, and 800, which is 100 BB, halfway. New Player with Jenna checked. Buy-in, Jenna 400, Cost $100. Not Yet, Cash picked, Transfer. Keys on the right: 400 min, 1,200 max, 800 100 BB Marcus wants 1,600. Dave types it, and House Rules says Above the max buy-in of 1,200 under the number. The check mark still works: the rules only remind. Dave tells Marcus about the limit, and Marcus buys in for 1,200. Buy-in, Marcus 1,600, Above the max buy-in of 1,200, Cost $400. Keys on the right: 400 min, 800 ×2, 1,200 max. The check mark is active How each move is checked: A buy-in and Back in Game are checked against both limits: Below the min buy-in or Above the max buy-in. A rebuy is checked only against the max, because a rebuy can be small. A cash-out and the rake aren't checked. During a game, the session's More menu has House Rules too, with the Cash Games and All Games rules. Changes there apply to the whole club, not just this session. A tournament's More menu shows the Tournaments and All Games rules, with the tournament's own buy-in and re-entries. Good to know The rules belong to the club. Every game in the club uses them, and a session outside a club has none. The limits follow each session's blinds. At 2/4 the same 50 to 150 BB is 200 to 600 chips. If the club hasn't played a game with blinds yet, the screen explains the limits in big blinds instead of showing chips. When the club's host is deleted from the club, Host goes back to Not Set. title: Planned Games and Reminders
headings: Edit, add to your calendar or cancel
text: The hardest part of a home game is getting people to the table. A week before, the group chat says five are in, two are maybe and three haven't answered. A planned game keeps all of it in one place: when and where you play, the seats, and who said they're coming. On the night, you start the session right from it. House Rules doesn't send anything to players by itself and players don't answer in the app. You send the invite to your group chat, they reply there as usual, and you mark each reply. House Rules reminds you, the host, before the game. This page shows how to plan a game, invite players, keep track of replies and the waitlist, and start the session on game day. Clubs and members are in Clubs and Members. The example club All the screenshots come from the Maple Street Game, Dave's home game on Maple Street. Dave is the host, so in this story you are Dave. The club: six regulars, Dave, Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya and Sam, who play No-Limit Hold'em (NLH) at 4/8 blinds every Tuesday: a small blind of 4 chips and a big blind of 8. A chip is worth $0.25. Today: Tuesday, November 24, the week after the club's last game. What happens: Dave plans next Tuesday's game at his place, with five seats at the table. Over the week he marks the replies. Marcus asks to bring a friend, Nick, but the table is full, so Nick waits for a seat. Then Priya can't make it, and Nick gets her seat. Plan a game In the Lobby, the screen House Rules opens on, tap the club under Clubs. If you have no club yet, see Clubs and Members. When the club has no game planned, Plan Next Game is at the top of the club's screen. Tap it. You can also tap the three dots at the top right of the club's screen, then Plan Game. It works even when a game is already planned, and adds another one. Maple Street Game, 6 members, 4 sessions. Plan Next Game at the top. Members and Stats tiles, Set House Rules, Recent Sessions with four Tuesday NLH 4/8 games New Game opens with most of it filled in: The name: Tuesday Game, from the day of the week, shown in gray. Type over it to call the game something else. Starts: the next 7:00 PM that's at least an hour away. Tap the date or the time to change them. Where: empty, type the place. Cash Game or Tournament, at the top of the Game section. For a cash game there are two more rows: Game, the kind of poker, NLH (No-Limit Hold'em) or PLO (Pot-Limit Omaha), and Stakes: NLH 4/8, 1 chip = $0.25, the blinds and chip value of the club's last session. You can change them when you start the session. For a tournament you set the buy-in and the blinds when you start it. Seat Limit: off. Turn it on to set how many players fit at the table. Note: anything players should know. Invite All Members: on, so the club's members are on the list from the start. New Game: Tuesday Game in gray, Starts Nov 24, 2026, 7:00 PM, Where empty. Game: Cash Game picked, Game NLH, Stakes NLH 4/8, 1 chip = $0.25. Seat Limit off. Note empty. A close button and a check mark at the top Dave taps the date and picks Tuesday, December 1, a week from today. The time stays at 7:00 PM. The calendar open over New Game: December 2026, Tuesday the 1st picked. Starts now shows Dec 1, 2026, 7:00 PM He types Dave's place, 14 Maple St. under Where, turns on Seat Limit and sets Seats to 5 with the minus button: his table fits five. When the seats are taken, anyone else who says they're going joins the waitlist. Under Note he writes Pizza at 7. Cash for the buy-in, please. Invite All Members stays on: 6 members. New Game, scrolled down: Seat Limit on, Seats 5 with minus and plus buttons. Players who say they're going after the seats are taken join the waitlist. Note: Pizza at 7. Cash for the buy-in, please. Invite All Members on Tap the check mark at the top right, Add Game, to save. The game's screen The game opens. At the top: its name, the club and the time, Tue, Dec 1, 7:00 PM. Under it, the seats: 0 of 5 in big numbers, with seats taken, 5 left under them. Then Details with Where, Game and Note, and Players: 6 invited, all six under No Reply for now, the host too. At the bottom are Invite and Start Session. The first time you plan a game, your phone asks whether House Rules may send notifications. Tap Allow to get the reminders described at the end of this page. Tuesday Game, Maple Street Game, Tue, Dec 1, 7:00 PM. 0 of 5, seats taken, 5 left. The question House Rules Would Like to Send You Notifications with Don't Allow and Allow. Players, 6 invited, No Reply 6: Dave, Jenna, Marcus. Invite and Start Session at the bottom Mark the replies Players answer in your chat, and you mark each answer. Tap a player's row. A menu opens with Going, Maybe, Out and No Reply, and Remove to take the player off the list. The reply menu over Marcus's row: Going, Maybe, Out, No Reply with a check mark, and Remove in red. Dave, marked first, is under Going By Thursday, five players are in: Dave, Marcus, Jenna, Tyler and Priya. Sam says maybe. The list sorts itself into groups, Going first, then Maybe, No Reply and Out, each with a count. Players, 6 invited. Going 5: Dave, Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya. Maybe 1: Sam. Add Player at the bottom Add a player Add Player under the list adds someone who isn't invited yet: Club Members picks from the club's members who aren't on the list. Here it's dimmed, because everyone is invited. Guest adds someone by name. A guest is on this game's list only and doesn't become a club member. The Add Player menu: Club Members dimmed, Guest Marcus wants to bring his friend Nick. Dave taps Guest, types Nick and taps the check mark. A card over the keyboard with Nick typed in the guest name field, a close button and a check mark The waitlist Nick says he's going, and Dave marks him Going. But all five seats are taken, so Nick goes to the Waitlist. The waitlist shows only when the game has a seat limit. Players on it are in the order you marked them Going. Players, 7 invited. Going 5: Dave, Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya. Waitlist 1: Nick, Going. Maybe 1: Sam. Add Player On Monday Priya texts that she can't come. Dave marks her Out. Her seat goes to the first player on the waitlist, and House Rules says so: Nick moved off the waitlist. Tell Nick yourself, House Rules doesn't message players. Going 5: Dave, Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Nick. Maybe 1: Sam. Out 1: Priya. A message at the bottom: Nick moved off the waitlist If you lower the seat limit later, with Edit in the game's More menu, the players you marked Going last move to the waitlist. Invite players Tap Invite at the bottom. There are two ways to send the game: Invite: a message for your group chat. Calendar Event: a calendar file. Players who open it can add the game to their own calendar. The Invite menu over the game: Calendar Event and Invite Both open the iPhone's share sheet, the panel of apps and people to send to. Pick the app your group uses, like Messages or WhatsApp, and the chat. The message has the game's details and the latest count of players and seats. Dave's reads: The last line always has the latest count, so you can send the invite again later to show who's coming and how many seats are left. The share sheet over the game with Tuesday Game at the top, Reminders and More, Save to Files Edit, add to your calendar or cancel The three dots at the top right of the game open More: Edit opens the game's details again: the name, time, place, game, seats and note. Add to Calendar puts the game in your own calendar. A New Event card opens with the name, the time from 7:00 PM to 11:00 PM, four hours, and the place. Tap the check mark to add it. Cancel Game asks first. The game stays in the list as cancelled. Let the players know yourself. The game's More menu: Edit, Add to Calendar, Cancel Game in red New Event from the iPhone's calendar: Tuesday Game, Starts Dec 1, 2026 7:00 PM, Ends Dec 1, 2026 11:00 PM, Repeat Never, Location Dave's place, 14 Maple St., Calendar, Alert None Where the game shows up Back on the club's screen, Plan Next Game has turned into the Next Game card: Tue, Dec 1, 7:00 PM, the place and the game, a bar of the seats taken, and 5 going, 1 maybe, 0 no reply. 5 seats is at the top right. Tap the card to open the game. Maple Street Game: the Next Game card with 5 seats, Tue, Dec 1, 7:00 PM, Dave's place, 14 Maple St., NLH 4/8, 1 chip = $0.25, a full bar, 5 going, 1 maybe, 0 no reply. Members and Stats tiles below In the Lobby, Upcoming lists the next games of all your clubs, up to three: Tue, Dec 1, 7:00 PM, Maple Street Game, 5 of 5 going. All Games under it lists every planned game, including past and cancelled ones. On game day, the line under Lobby says Game tonight. The Lobby: 1 club, 4 sessions. Upcoming: Tue, Dec 1, 7:00 PM, Maple Street Game, NLH 4/8, 1 chip = $0.25, 5 of 5 going. All Games. Recent Sessions below and Start Session at the bottom Start the session On Tuesday night, open the game and tap Start Session. New Session opens with the game's club, blinds and chip value, and the line From Tuesday Game, Tue, Dec 1. Change anything that's different tonight, then tap the check mark. New Session: Club Maple Street Game, Game NLH, Small Blind 4, Big Blind 8, Ante empty, Chip Value 1 chip = $0.25. From Tuesday Game, Tue, Dec 1. Start Now The session doesn't seat anyone by itself: add the players as they arrive, see Starting a Cash Game. The game's screen then shows Session started at and the time. Tap it to open the session. On game day, Start Session at the bottom of the Lobby opens the same New Session for tonight's game. With two games that day, it takes the earlier one. A game that was never started shows Didn't start once its end time has passed, or 12 hours after its start if it has no end time, and leaves Next Game and Upcoming. It stays in All Games. Reminders House Rules reminds you, the host, up to three times: A day before: for example Tuesday Game tomorrow, with the replies so far: 5 going, 1 maybe, 0 no reply. No seats left. Two hours before: Game in 2 hours, Tuesday Game, 5 going. Tap it to open the game. Three hours before, only if someone still owes: for example Tuesday Game today, Sam still owes $52.00 from past sessions. It's there so you can write to them before the game. More in Who Owes and Reminders. They're on from the start. To turn them off, open Settings with the gear at the top right of the Lobby and turn off Game Reminders, under Notifications. The one switch covers all three. Players don't get reminders from House Rules, only you do. Settings: Help, then Data with Sync with iCloud and the backup buttons, then Notifications with Level Change on, Game Reminders on, a day and two hours before a planned game, Who Owes Reminders off, which is about debts, and Lock Screen on If you said Don't Allow to notifications, there are no reminders, and everything else works. To allow them later, open the iPhone's Settings app, then Apps, House Rules, Notifications. Good to know The game is planned on this phone only. Players see what you send them: the message and the calendar file. Deleting a session started from a game puts the game back to planned, so you can start it again. On an iPad, planned games aren't shown in the club yet. Plan them on the iPhone. Planned games aren't in a .pokersession file when you move sessions to another phone. Related Clubs and Members House Rules Starting a Cash Game Export and Import

title: Player Stats and CSV
text: Every session you close in a club adds to its members' numbers. Each member has a screen with their result, how often they win, their average per session and every game they played, for this year, the last month or all time. You can send a player their stats as a picture, or export them as a CSV file for a spreadsheet. This page shows how to read a member's stats, change the period, switch between cash games and tournaments, and share or export them. Adding and managing members is in Clubs and Members. The example club All the screenshots come from the Maple Street Game, Dave's home game on Maple Street. Dave is the host, so in this story you are Dave. The club: six regulars, Dave, Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya and Sam. They play No-Limit Hold'em cash games at 4/8 blinds with a chip worth $0.25, and now and then a $50 tournament. The games: six cash games, one in October 2025, one in September 2026 and four Tuesdays in a row this fall, and two tournaments, on October 31 and November 14, 2026. What happens: Jenna asks how she's doing this year. Dave opens her stats, looks at a few periods, sends her a picture and exports a CSV for his own spreadsheet. Open a member's stats Open the club from the Lobby, the screen House Rules opens on, and tap the Members tile. It shows how many members there are and the biggest winner this year: Top: Jenna, +$371.50. Maple Street Game, 6 members, 8 sessions. Plan Next Game. Members tile 6, Top: Jenna +$371.50. Stats tile $2,800 total buy-ins in 2026. Set House Rules. Recent Sessions with cash games and tournaments The club's 8 sessions count cash games and tournaments together. The members list shows each member's cash games (sessions) and tournaments separately, the date they last played, and their result for all time, cash games and tournaments together: green for up, red for down. Jenna is up $426.50 over 6 sessions, 2 tournaments. The button at the top right of the list shows only members with one tag. Tap Jenna's row. Members, Maple Street Game, 6 members: Dave +$173, Jenna +$426.50 6 sessions 2 tournaments Nov 17, Marcus +$76.50, Priya −$172, Tyler −$272, Sam −$292, all time Read the stats Jenna's screen opens on 2026, this year, because she played this year. A member who hasn't played this year opens on all time. Under her name: Maple Street Game, 6 sessions, 2 tournaments, all her games, whatever the period. She played both kinds of games, so there's a switch with Cash Games and Tournaments. Cash Games is first. Jenna, Maple Street Game, 6 sessions, 2 tournaments. 2026 and a share button at the top. Cash Games and Tournaments switch. Result for 2026 +$181.50 with a chart from about −$55 up to about $180. Tiles: 5 sessions played, 60% winning sessions, +$36 per session, $0 rakeback. Tags and Note below Result for 2026: +$181.50, what she won minus what she paid for chips in this year's cash games. The result already includes rakeback, money the club gives back to a player out of the rake, and her share of expenses like food. See Rake, Tips and Rakeback and Expenses and Splitting Them. The chart: her result added up game by game. Her September game was a loss of $55, so the line starts below zero, then the four Tuesdays take it to +$181.50. Touch and hold the chart to see the total after each game. sessions played: 5 this year. winning sessions: 60%, three of the five ended above zero. per session: +$36, the result divided by the sessions and rounded to whole dollars. rakeback: $0, the club doesn't give rakeback here. Tap the small i next to a title or a tile for a one-line explanation. The list of sessions Scroll down. Under the tags and note, which are in Clubs and Members, are Credit and Payment, see Who Owes and Reminders, and Sessions: every game in the period, newest first, with her buy-ins in chips and her result. On Tuesday, November 17 she bought in for 400 chips, $100 at $0.25 a chip, cashed out $75 and lost $25.00. On November 10 she won $177.00. Tap a session to open it. Jenna's screen scrolled down: Tags and Note with Add Tags and Add Note. Credit and Payment with Credit Limit None and Payment Link None. Sessions 5: Tue, November 17 buy-ins 400 −$25.00, Tue, November 10 buy-ins 400 +$177.00, Tue, November 3 buy-ins 400 +$9.00 Change the period The button at the top right, 2026, picks the period. It lists All Time, each year the member played, newest first, here 2026 and 2025, then 90 days and 30 days. The period menu: All Time, 2026 with a check mark, 2025, 90 days, 30 days With 30 days, the title says Result for Last 30 Days: +$236.50 from the 4 Tuesday games, 75% of them winning, +$59 per session. The September loss is older than 30 days, so it's not counted. 30 days picked. Result for Last 30 Days +$236.50 with a chart from Nov 1 to Nov 15. Tiles: 4 sessions played, 75% winning sessions, +$59 per session, $0 rakeback With All Time, the title says All-Time Result: +$236.50 from 6 sessions. Last year's win of $55 and September's loss of $55 cancel out. 66.7% of her sessions were winning, and +$39 per session. All Time picked. All-Time Result +$236.50 with a chart from late 2025 to November 2026. Tiles: 6 sessions played, 66.7% winning sessions, +$39 per session, $0 rakeback The days count back from today, today included. A period with no games says No Sessions in This Period, with Show All Time to go back. Tournaments Tap Tournaments on the switch. Tournaments have their own numbers, because a tournament is paid for differently: everyone pays the same buy-in, and the prizes come from the pool. See Prize Pool and Payouts. Jenna's All-Time Tournament Result is +$190: tournaments played: 2. in the money: 100%, 2 of 2. She won a prize both times. wins: 1, finished first. ROI: +173%, the result divided by everything she paid in. She paid $55 each time, the $50 buy-in that goes to the prize pool and a $5 fee for the house, set up with the tournament. Paid includes both, so $110 in all, and $190 is 173% of $110. Tournaments picked, All Time. All-Time Tournament Result +$190 with a chart. Tiles: 2 tournaments played, 100% in the money 2 of 2, 1 wins, +173% ROI. Tournaments 2: Sat, November 14, 2nd of 6, paid $55, +$50 Below, the list of Tournaments shows each one with her place and what she paid: on Saturday, November 14 she was 2nd of 6, paid $55, and is up $50. The total on the Members tile and in the members list adds cash games and tournaments together: Jenna's +$426.50 for all time is $236.50 from cash games and $190 from tournaments. Send a player their stats The share button at the top right has two choices: Share Stats and Export CSV. The share menu at the top right of Jenna's screen: Share Stats, Export CSV Share Stats makes a card to send to the player. At the top, pick Image, a picture, or Text, the same numbers as plain text to paste into a message. Under Include, pick the Period and what goes on the card: Cash Games, Tournaments and Last Sessions, her five most recent games. The Preview below shows the card: here Maple Street Game, 2026, Jenna, and a Total Result of +$371.50, cash games and tournaments together for this year: $181.50 from cash games and $190 from tournaments. The Members tile shows the same this-year total. Tap the check mark to send it from the share sheet. Share Stats: Image and Text, Image picked. Include: Notes and tags never leave your phone. Maple Street Game remembers your choice. Period 2026, Cash Games on, Tournaments on, Last Sessions on. Preview: Maple Street Game, 2026, Jenna, Total Result +$371.50, cash games and tournaments, with a chart Tags and notes never go on the card. The club remembers which parts you included, so the next card starts the same way. Export a CSV Export CSV makes a spreadsheet file of the tab you're on and the period you picked, and opens the share sheet. Save it to Files, mail it to yourself, or open it in Numbers, Excel or Google Sheets. Here it's Stats, Jenna, her cash games in 2026. The share sheet over Jenna's stats with Stats, Jenna at the top, Reminders, More and Save to Files The file is named after the member and the time, for example playerstatsjenna202611241530.csv. Each line has a section, then the item and its value: meta: the member, the club, when the file was made, and the period. summary: Sessions Played, Winning Sessions, Total Result, Per Session, and Result to Buy-ins, the result divided by what she paid for chips. turnover: Buy-ins, Cash-outs and Rakeback for the period. session: one line per game with its date, buy-ins, cash-out and result. Money is written as plain numbers like 181.50, without the currency sign, so a spreadsheet can add them up. On the Tournaments tab, Export CSV makes a separate file, tournamentstatsjenna...csv, with tournaments played, in the money, wins, ROI, paid in, prizes, and one line per tournament. What counts Only the club's sessions that are settled or waiting for settlement count. A game still in progress isn't in the stats yet. The result is in money, at each session's chip value, so games with different chip values add up correctly. Rakeback and expense shares are already in the result. A member's stats belong to one club. The same person in two clubs has separate stats in each. Good to know On the iPhone you export one member at a time. On the iPad, Export CSV at the top of the club's screen exports all members at once. The Stats tile on the club's screen is about the whole club, not one member: the total buy-ins for the period. See Club Stats. A member who hasn't played yet shows No Sessions Yet. Their tags and note still work.
