title: Club Stats
text: Club Stats shows how your club plays as a whole: how much money goes through the table, the prize pools of your tournaments, what the house keeps, and who's up and who's down. Pick a year, the last 90 or 30 days, or all time. The example club All the screenshots come from the Maple Street Game, Dave's home game on Maple Street. The club: Dave hosts for Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya and Sam. They play No-Limit Hold'em at 4/8 blinds, and now and then a $50 tournament. The history: six cash games since last year, five of them this year, and two tournaments in November. Dave took rake in three of this year's cash games and the dealer got tips in one. What Dave wants to know: how this year went for the club, and who's leading. Open Club Stats Open the club from the Lobby. Next to Members is the Stats tile, with the total buy-ins for the period: here $2,800, total buy-ins in 2026. Tap it. The Maple Street Game, 6 members, 8 sessions. Plan Next Game, the Members tile with 6, Top: Jenna +$341.50, and the Stats tile with $2,800, total buy-ins in 2026. Set House Rules and Recent Sessions Club Stats, Maple Street Game, 2026. Total Buy-ins, 5 sessions, $2,800, with bars for September, October and November. $560 per session, 5 players per session, $60 rake, $10 tips. Prize Pools below Club Stats opens on this year if the club played this year, otherwise on all time. It counts sessions that are settled or waiting to be settled up. A game that's still running isn't counted yet. Total Buy-ins The first card is about the cash games: all the money players bought in for, rebuys included. Under the title, how many cash games the period has: 5 sessions. The bars show the buy-ins month by month, from the first game of the period to the last. Touch and hold a bar to see the month, the amount and the number of sessions. With only one month, there are no bars. per session: the average buy-ins of one game, here $560. players per session: how many played on average, here 5. rake, tips and expenses: the totals for the period, shown only when they're more than zero. Here $60 of rake and $10 of tips; nobody added an expense. Tap an i to see what its number means. The same words are in the Glossary. The note for Total Buy-ins over Club Stats: all buy-ins and rebuys of every player in the period's cash game sessions, in money at the chip value. Counts sessions that are settled or waiting for settlement Prize Pools and House Prize Pools shows up when the period has tournaments: the prize pools added together, $600 for 2 tournaments, the average pool per tournament, players per tournament, and entries, re-entries included. Tips and the house fee aren't part of a prize pool. See Prize Pool and Payouts. House is what the house kept: rake and the tournaments' house fee, minus rakeback and expenses paid from the rake. Here it's $120, kept by the house in 5 sessions: $60 of rake from the cash games and $60 of house fee from the two tournaments, with no rakeback and no expenses from the rake. Dealer tips are the dealer's money and aren't counted. See Rake, Tips and Rakeback. Prize Pools, 2 tournaments, $600: $300 per tournament, 6 players per tournament, 12 entries. House, kept by the house in 5 sessions, $120: Rake and house fee $120, Rakeback paid $0, Expenses from rake $0 Results Results lists the members by their result for the period, cash games and tournaments together, from the top: place, name, how many sessions and tournaments they played, and the result, green for up and red for down. Jenna leads 2026 with +$341.50, Sam is last with −$292. House $120 at the top, then Results, 6 members: 1 Jenna 5 sessions, 2 tournaments +$341.50, 2 Dave +$198, 3 Marcus −$3.50, 4 Priya −$172, 5 Tyler −$202, 6 Sam −$292 Tap a member to open their own stats for the same period, see Player Stats and CSV. Jenna, Maple Street Game, 6 sessions, 2 tournaments, with 2026 at the top right. Cash Games: Result for 2026 +$151.50 with a chart, 5 sessions played, 60% winning sessions, +$30 per session, $0 rakeback A member you deleted from the club isn't on the list. Change the period The button at the top right shows the period. Tap it and choose All Time, one of the years the club played, or the last 90 days or 30 days. The period menu over Club Stats: All Time, 2026 checked, 2025, 90 days, 30 days Club Stats for All Time: Total Buy-ins, 6 sessions, $3,200, with bars from last October to this November. $533 per session, 4.8 players per session, $60 rake, $10 tips All time adds last year's game: $3,200 in 6 sessions, $533 per session. A period with no games says No Sessions in This Period, with Show All Time to go back. Good to know A new club shows No Sessions Yet until its first cash game or tournament gets to the settling up. A club with only tournaments shows Prize Pools, House and Results, without Total Buy-ins. Its Stats tile shows the prize pools instead of buy-ins. On the iPad, Stats in the sidebar lists your clubs; pick one to see its stats next to the list. Related Player Stats and CSV Clubs and Members Rake, Tips and Rakeback

title: Export and Import
text: House Rules keeps your games on your phone and, while Sync with iCloud is on in Settings, in your own iCloud, so your own iPhone and iPad show the same games, see Sync with iCloud. Another host's phone is a different matter: there's no account to share, so to give a session to someone else, you send it as a file. The file ends in .pokersession and carries the whole game: players, buy-ins and cash-outs, the cash box, expenses and the transfers of the settlement. A tournament travels the same way, with its entries, places and payouts. This page shows how to send a session, how to bring it in on the other device and what happens when the same game arrives twice. Handing a running game to another host has its own page, Handing a Session Over. The example club All the screenshots come from the Maple Street Game, Dave's home game on Maple Street. The club: Dave hosts on Tuesdays for Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya and Sam. They play No-Limit Hold'em at 4/8 blinds with a chip worth $0.25. Marcus's phone: Marcus keeps the Maple Street Game on his own phone too, with Dave, Jenna and Tyler as members, and runs a second club of his own, the Office Game. What happens: Dave sends Marcus last Tuesday's game, played on November 17 by five of them, without Sam. Send a session Open the session and tap More, the button with three dots at the top right. Choose Share Session. For a tournament, the same item is called Share Tournament. Session Ended, Maple Street Game, Tue, Nov 17, NLH 4/8. The More menu is open: House Rules, Session Log, Share Session, Delete Session The share sheet opens with the file, here 11/17/2026, Maple Street Game. Send it with AirDrop, Messages or Mail, or tap Save to Files to keep it. The share sheet over the session: 11/17/2026, Maple Street Game at the top, then More and Save to Files Dave keeps a copy: Save to Files, pick a folder, here On My iPhone, and tap Save. Then he sends the same file to Marcus by AirDrop, and Marcus saves it to Files on his phone. The share sheet shows the date the US way, 11/17/2026, but the file name always puts the day first and drops the spaces from the club's name: 17.11.2026-MapleStreetGame.pokersession. The Files sheet on On My iPhone, which is empty, with Save at the top right and Save as 17.11.2026-MapleStreet at the bottom You can share a session at any stage: while it's running, after it's closed and waiting for players to settle up, or when it's finished. Sharing never locks your copy, both phones keep working with it. In a club's list of sessions, touch and hold a session and choose Share to send it without opening it. Import a file On the other device, open the file and choose House Rules, for example by tapping it in Messages or Mail. Or go to Settings, the gear at the top of the Lobby, the screen House Rules opens on (on the iPad, Settings in the sidebar), and under Sessions from Other Hosts tap Import Session, then pick the file. Marcus picks 17.11.2026. The other file is tonight's game, which comes later on this page. The file picker on On My iPhone with two files, 17.11.2026-MapleS...ession and 24.11.2026-MapleS...ession The Import Session sheet shows what's in the file and asks where it goes: Session from File: the date, November 17, 2026, and 5 players. Import to Club: your clubs. Marcus keeps Maple Street Game checked. Tap another club to pick it. New Members: players in the file who aren't members of that club. Priya isn't in Marcus's copy of the club, so she's listed and checked. Import Session sheet. Session from File: November 17, 2026, 5 players. Import to Club: Maple Street Game checked, Office Game. New Members: Priya checked. These players aren't in the club. Selected players become members; for the rest, this session won't count in club stats A checked player becomes a member of the club. Uncheck a player who shouldn't be one: they stay in the session with their results, but the session won't count in the club's stats for them. Players who are already members are matched by name and aren't listed. See Clubs and Members. Tap the check mark. The session opens on Marcus's phone with the same results and cash box, and a message says Session imported. Session Ended, Maple Street Game, Tue, Nov 17 on Marcus's phone: won $59 by 3 players, lost $59 by 2 players, 2,000 buy-ins, 2,000 cashed out. A message at the bottom: Session imported, 11/17/2026, Maple Street Game No club yet? The sheet offers a new club, Home Game, and all the players become its members. You can rename the club later. The same game twice House Rules recognizes a session it already has. The same file again: nothing changes, and a message says Session already imported. A different version: say Dave fixed a cash-out and sent the file again. House Rules asks Session Already Imported with Replace and Skip. Replace swaps your copy for the one in the file and erases your own edits to it, such as transfers you marked as done. Skip keeps your copy. Settings on Marcus's phone with Import Session under Sessions from Other Hosts, and a message at the bottom: Session already imported, 11/17/2026, Maple Street Game Your own session that went to another phone and came back unchanged is the same session too: it's recognized, not added twice. Hand a running game over Share Session sends a copy and both phones keep working with it. To pass a running game to another host, so only one phone runs it, use Hand Over Session in the More menu instead. It sends the same kind of file and locks your copy. The whole story, with Dave leaving early and Marcus finishing the game, is in Handing a Session Over. When a file won't import The message Couldn't Import Session says what's wrong and what to do: The file is damaged or isn't a House Rules session. Ask the sender to send it again. The file is from a different version of House Rules. Update the app on both devices, then open the file again. Two players in the file match one member of the club, for example two players called Sam in the file and one Sam in the club. Choose another club, or ask the sender to rename one of them. The app can't access the file. Save it to Files and choose it from there. Good to know Both devices need a version of House Rules that reads the same file format. If the file comes from a different one, House Rules says so: update the app on both devices and open the file again. The club's color, house rules and seasons stay on each device: the file carries the session, not the club. A file larger than 5 MB isn't a House Rules session and isn't imported. On the iPad you can also drop a file on the window, see Dropping a File on iPad. Related Handing a Session Over Dropping a File on iPad Clubs and Members Marking Transfers Done Player Stats and CSV

title: Handing a Session Over
headings: Take it back without the file
text: When you can't stay until the end of the game, another host can run the rest of it on their phone. Hand Over Session sends the running game as a file and locks your copy, so only one phone runs the game at a time. This page shows how to hand a game over, how the new host takes it, and how the game comes back. The example club All the screenshots come from the Maple Street Game, Dave's home game on Maple Street. The club: Dave hosts on Tuesdays for Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya and Sam. They play No-Limit Hold'em at 4/8 blinds with a chip worth $0.25. Marcus's phone: Marcus keeps the Maple Street Game on his own phone too, and runs a second club of his own, the Office Game. Last week Dave sent him the November 17 game, see Export and Import, so Priya is already a member there. What happens: tonight, November 24, Dave has to leave early, so he hands the running game over to Marcus, who finishes it on his phone. Why not just share it With two copies of a running game, both hosts could add rebuys and the totals would no longer match. Hand Over Session sends the game and locks Dave's copy, so there's only one host at a time. Share Session, the item next to it, never locks anything: both phones keep a copy you can change, and changes from two phones never merge. Use it to send a copy for the record, see Export and Import. Hand it over Open the running session, tap More and choose Hand Over Session. For a tournament it's Hand Over Tournament. The item is only there while the game is running. Live Session, Maple Street Game. The More menu: Edit Session, Rake and Tips, Close Session, House Rules, Session Log, Share Session, Hand Over Session, Delete Session The share sheet opens with tonight's file, 11/24/2026, Maple Street Game. Send it to Marcus the way you'd send any file. The share sheet over the Live Session: 11/24/2026, Maple Street Game, More and Save to Files Once the file has gone, Dave's copy is read-only: the screen says This session was handed over to another host. To make changes here, take it back. Dave can still look at everything, including the cash box. If you close the share sheet without sending, nothing is locked. Live Session on Dave's phone: This session was handed over to another host. To make changes here, take it back. Take Back button. On the Table 2,400 chips, 1 chip = $0.25, $600 at chip value. Only Cash Box at the bottom The new host takes over On Marcus's phone, the import sheet says Handed over to you. You run this session from now on. Priya became a member when Marcus imported last Tuesday's game, so there are no new members this time. Import Session sheet. Session from File: November 24, 2026, 5 players. Handed over to you. You run this session from now on. Import to Club: Maple Street Game checked, Office Game After the check mark, tonight's game opens on Marcus's phone as a Live Session he can change: the same five players, 2,400 chips on the table and $600 in the cash box. Live Session, Maple Street Game, Tue, Nov 24 on Marcus's phone: On the Table 2,400 chips, $600 at chip value, 5 of 5 at the table, running for about two and a half hours. Cash Box $600, Rebuy and + at the bottom. Message: Session imported The new host doesn't need your club. They pick one of their own clubs in the import sheet, or the session goes to a new club if they have none. Players who aren't members there are listed under New Members. Hand it back To give the game back, Marcus opens it, taps More, Hand Over Session and sends the file to Dave, who opens it in House Rules. Then: Unchanged: Dave's copy unlocks and a message says Session is back. With Marcus's changes: the import sheet says Back from the other host with their changes. You run this session here again. The check mark replaces Dave's copy with Marcus's, without asking about Replace, and unlocks it. Take it back without the file Can't wait for the file? Take Back unlocks Dave's copy. It asks first, because changes made on the other phone won't come with it: Take Back Session? To keep Marcus's changes, ask him to hand the game back instead. Take Back doesn't reach Marcus's phone: his copy stays open there, so agree who runs the game from now on. Take Back Session? Changes made on the other phone won't be here. To keep them, ask the other host to hand it back. Take Back button Good to know Hand Over Session is in the More menu until the session is finished. For a tournament it's Hand Over Tournament. Close the share sheet without sending, and nothing is locked. A locked copy is read-only: you can still look at everything, including the cash box. Take Back doesn't reach the other phone. Their copy stays open, so agree who runs the game from now on. Changes from two phones never merge. When a different version comes back, you keep one copy or the other, so let only one host make changes at a time. The blind timer doesn't travel with the game. Start it again on the new host's device, see Running the Timer. iCloud sync is for your own iPhone and iPad, not for another host's phone. Between your own devices, the game is already the same everywhere, see Sync with iCloud. Related Export and Import Dropping a File on iPad Running the Timer

title: Dropping a File on iPad
text: On the iPad there's a quicker way to bring in a session than Import Session: drag the .pokersession file from Files, Mail or another app and drop it on the House Rules window. The same import sheet opens, and from there everything works as in Export and Import. The example club All the screenshots come from the Maple Street Game, Dave's home game on Maple Street. The club: Dave hosts on Tuesdays for Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya and Sam. They play No-Limit Hold'em at 4/8 blinds with a chip worth $0.25. Marcus's iPad: Marcus keeps the Maple Street Game on his iPad, with Dave, Jenna and Tyler as members, next to his own club, the Office Game. What happens: Dave sent Marcus the file for last Tuesday's game, played on November 17, and Marcus saved it to Files on his iPad. Sending and saving the file is in Export and Import. Now he brings it into House Rules. Drop the file House Rules takes a dropped file in its full iPad layout, with the sidebar on the left: the sections Tonight, Clubs and Library, and Settings at the bottom. House Rules on an iPad in landscape: the sidebar with Tonight, Start Session, Clubs, Maple Street Game, Office Game, New Club, Library, All Sessions, Stats, Blind Timer and Settings. On the right: No Session Running, Start tonight's game, or pick a club in the sidebar, Start Session 1. Put Files and House Rules on the screen together: open Files, then House Rules, and arrange their windows side by side, or use Slide Over. Mail works the same way with a file in an email. 2. Touch and hold the file until it lifts, then drag it onto the House Rules window and let go. Anywhere in the window works. 3. The import sheet opens. Pick the club and the new members, then tap the check mark. Nothing on the screen shows where to drop: the whole window takes the file. The import sheet The sheet is the same one Import Session opens, and it looks the same however you got to it; in the screenshot, Settings is behind it. Here it shows last Tuesday's game: November 17, 2026, 5 players. Marcus keeps Maple Street Game checked. Priya isn't a member of his copy of the club yet, so she's under New Members, checked, and she becomes a member with the import. The Import Session sheet over Settings on the iPad. Session from File: November 17, 2026, 5 players. Import to Club: Maple Street Game checked, Office Game. New Members: Priya checked After the check mark, the session opens on the right, in place of the screen that was there, and a message says Session imported. Session Ended, Maple Street Game, Tue, Nov 17 on the iPad: won $59 by 3 players, lost $59 by 2 players, five players. Message at the bottom: Session imported, 11/17/2026, Maple Street Game A file House Rules already has works the same way as on the iPhone: the same file again changes nothing, and a different version asks Replace or Skip. A game that was handed over to you opens with Handed over to you. You run this session from now on. See Export and Import. Without dragging When dragging is awkward, go to Settings in the sidebar, tap Import Session and pick the file. The file picker opens on the iPad's Files, here in On My iPad, where Marcus saved the file. iCloud Drive and On My iPad are under Locations, and Recents has the files you opened last. The file picker over Settings on the iPad: Recents, Shared, Locations with iCloud Drive and On My iPad, Tags. On My iPad: the file 17.11.2026-Maple...ession, 5 KB, and the House Rules folder Good to know Drop several files at once, and only the first one is imported, with no message about the rest. Drop the others one at a time. Dropping works in the full layout with the sidebar. When House Rules is in a narrow window, it shows the iPhone layout: use Import Session in Settings there. Only .pokersession files are taken. The window doesn't take a photo or a PDF: nothing happens. Related Export and Import House Rules on iPad Timer Window on iPad Clubs and Members

title: Sync with iCloud
text: House Rules keeps your clubs, sessions, cash boxes and the blind timer the same on every iPhone and iPad signed in to your Apple Account. There's nothing to set up: iCloud sync is on from the start, and your data goes to your own iCloud, not to us. The example club The screenshots come from Dave's iPhone. Dave hosts the Maple Street Game on Tuesdays and keeps the club in House Rules, with its members and a few weeks of sessions. He has an iPad too and wants the same club on both. Where to find it Open Settings, the gear at the top right of the Lobby. The Data section has the Sync with iCloud switch, a status line under it, and the two backup buttons, Back Up All Data and Restore from Backup. The note under the section says what to do when something is wrong. Settings in House Rules. Data: Sync with iCloud switched on, Back Up All Data and Restore from Backup, and the note: syncing starts after you close House Rules and open it again. A backup is one file you keep yourself What the status line says The line under the switch tells you how syncing is going right now: Last Synced: Everything is in step. It shows when the last sync finished, for example Today at 9:41 PM or Yesterday at 9:41 PM, and Not Yet before the first one. Syncing: Changes are going up or coming down right now. The first sync of a big club shows this for a while. Not Signed In to iCloud: The iPhone isn't signed in to an Apple Account. Sign in in the iPhone's Settings app. Until then, everything stays on this iPhone. iCloud Is Unavailable: iCloud is turned off for apps on this iPhone, for example by Screen Time, or can't be reached for now. Your changes stay on this iPhone and sync when it's back. iCloud Storage Is Full: New changes stay on this iPhone. Free up space or get more storage in the iPhone's Settings app. Update House Rules to Sync: This version of House Rules can't sync anymore. Update it in the App Store. Until then, new changes stay on this iPhone. The four warnings come in the warning color, with what to do in the note under the section. Short hiccups, like a dropped connection, don't show up: iCloud retries them by itself. Right after you turn the switch on or off, there's no status line at all: the note says the change waits until you open House Rules again, see below. Your first sync When you turn on a new iPhone or iPad and open House Rules, your clubs and sessions come down by themselves. A club with a long history can take a while the first time, up to an hour or more on a slow connection. You can use House Rules meanwhile; it goes faster with the app open and the device on Wi-Fi. The status line shows Syncing until it's done. Turn sync off You can play with sync off, for example on a second iPhone you only use for the timer. 1. Open Settings and turn off Sync with iCloud. 2. House Rules asks first: everything stays on this iPhone, and changes from your other devices stop arriving until you turn it back on. Tap Turn Off iCloud Sync, or tap anywhere else to keep syncing. 3. The change takes effect the next time you open House Rules. Until then, the note under the section says: Syncing stops after you close House Rules and open it again. The question next to Sync with iCloud: everything stays on this iPhone, changes from your other devices stop arriving until you turn it back on. Turn Off iCloud Sync Nothing is deleted when you turn sync off. Your data stays on this iPhone, and the copy in iCloud stays as it was. Turn it back on Turn Sync with iCloud on again. There's no question this time. If House Rules was opened with sync off, the note says Syncing starts after you close House Rules and open it again, as in the first screenshot. Close House Rules from the app switcher and open it: what you changed on this iPhone goes up, and what changed on your other devices comes down. What syncs and what doesn't Synced through iCloud: Clubs with their house rules, seasons and members. Sessions and tournaments, with buy-ins, cash-outs, the cash box and transfers. Planned games. Your own blind structures and the running blind timer. Stays on each device: Your payment link under Getting Paid. The switches under Notifications. Small display choices, like how seats are drawn. The timer runs on every device, but only the device where you started it sends the level change notifications, so you don't get the same alert three times. Good to know iCloud sync is for your own devices. It doesn't share a club with another host who has a different Apple Account. To pass a session to someone else, send them the file, see Export and Import and Handing a Session Over. iCloud keeps your devices in step, but it isn't a backup: a session you delete is deleted everywhere. Keep a backup file now and then, see Back Up and Restore. Getting a new iPhone? See Moving to a New iPhone. Related Back Up and Restore Moving to a New iPhone Settings

title: Back Up and Restore
headings: Add what's missing or replace everything
text: A backup is one file with everything you keep in House Rules: every club, member, session and tournament. You save it where you like, in Files, in iCloud Drive or on your Mac, and you can bring it back on this iPhone or on another one. iCloud sync keeps your devices in step; a backup is a copy you keep yourself, for the day something goes wrong. The example club The screenshots come from Dave's iPhone. Dave hosts the Maple Street Game on Tuesdays for Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya and Sam, and has a few weeks of sessions in House Rules. He saves a backup to Files, then brings it back. Back up all data 1. Open Settings, the gear at the top right of the Lobby. 2. Under Data, tap Back Up All Data. 3. The share sheet opens with the backup file. Its name has today's date, for example 27.11.2026-HouseRulesBackup.houserules. Choose Save to Files and pick a folder, or send the file to your Mac with AirDrop. Settings in House Rules. Data: Sync with iCloud, Back Up All Data and Restore from Backup, then Notifications The share sheet with House Rules Backup at the top, More and Save to Files Save to Files in On My iPhone: Save as 27.11.2026-HouseRules and the Save button at the top right Once the file is saved, Back Up All Data shows the date of your last backup under it. Settings with Back Up All Data and Last backup Nov 27, 2026 under it With Sync with iCloud off, House Rules reminds you when your last backup is more than a month old: the line under Back Up All Data turns to the warning color. What's in a backup Your clubs, with their house rules and seasons. Members and their tags. Sessions and tournaments, with buy-ins, cash-outs, the cash box, expenses and transfers. Planned games and who said they're going. Your own blind structures and the blind timer. Settings that live on the iPhone itself aren't in the backup: your payment link, the notification switches and small display choices. Set them again after a restore on a new iPhone. House Rules doesn't back up on its own. Save a new backup now and then, for example after a big game or before you change phones. Restore from a backup 1. Open Settings and tap Restore from Backup, under Data. 2. Pick the backup file in Files. 3. The Restore Backup sheet shows what's in the file: when and on which device it was made, and how many clubs, members, sessions and tournaments it has. 4. Under How to Restore, choose what happens to what's on the iPhone now, and tap the check mark. Files, Recents: the file 27.11.2026-House...serules, 10:19 PM, 19 KB Restore Backup: House Rules Backup, Nov 27, 2026 at 10:19 PM, from iPhone, 1 club, 6 members, 4 sessions, 0 tournaments. How to Restore: Add What's Missing checked, Replace All Data, and the note: sessions you already have are recognized, not added twice Add what's missing or replace everything Add What's Missing is the choice to start with. It keeps everything on the iPhone and adds what's in the backup but not here: a deleted session comes back, and sessions you added since the backup stay. A message says what was added, for example Backup Restored, Added 3 clubs, 41 members and 62 sessions. If everything in the file is already here, it says Nothing to Add. Replace All Data deletes what's on the iPhone now and puts the backup in its place. Use it to go back to the day of the backup, for example after a mistake you can't undo. A blind timer that's running keeps running. Replace asks first: Replace All Data? It says how many sessions and clubs on this iPhone are deleted, and that with iCloud on they're deleted on your other devices too. Before it deletes anything, House Rules saves what's on the iPhone to a backup of its own, so you can go back. You'll find it in Files, On My iPhone, House Rules, Backups, with BeforeRestore in its name. Restore Backup with Replace All Data checked and the note: your current data is saved to a backup in Files first Replace All Data? 4 sessions and 1 club on this iPhone are deleted, and with iCloud on, on your other devices too. Your current data is saved to a backup in Files first. Replace All Data button Settings after the restore, with the message All Data Replaced: your previous data is in Files, in the Backups folder On an iPhone with no data yet, Replace doesn't ask: there's nothing to delete. When something goes wrong If the backup can't be made, a message says Couldn't Back Up Data. Try again in a moment. If a restore doesn't work, the message Couldn't Restore Backup says why, and nothing on the iPhone changes: The file isn't a House Rules backup. Choose a file that ends in .houserules. A .pokersession file is one session; bring it in with Import Session, see Export and Import. The backup is from a newer version of House Rules. Update the app, then restore again. The backup is damaged. Choose another backup. The app can't access the file. Save it to Files and choose it from there. Your current data couldn't be saved to Files first. With Replace All Data, nothing is replaced until the copy of what's here is saved. Free up space on the iPhone and try again. Finish the edit in progress. Close the screen you were editing, then restore again. A backup file can be up to 200 MB. You can also open a .houserules file from Files or Mail and choose House Rules: the same Restore Backup sheet opens. Good to know A backup is a whole file of your data, with your players' names and money. Keep it somewhere private. A backup is different from sharing one session: a .pokersession file carries one game for another host, see Export and Import. Changing phones? With iCloud on, you may not need a backup at all, see Moving to a New iPhone. Related Sync with iCloud Moving to a New iPhone Settings

title: Moving to a New iPhone
text: Got a new iPhone? Your clubs, players and every past session can come with you. There are two ways: iCloud brings them over by itself, and a backup file works with or without iCloud. The example club The screenshots come from Dave's phones. Dave hosts the Maple Street Game on Tuesdays for Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya and Sam, and has a few weeks of sessions in House Rules on his old iPhone. He moves them to a new one. With iCloud: just wait If Sync with iCloud is on on your old iPhone, which it is unless you turned it off, there's nothing to move: 1. On the new iPhone, sign in with the same Apple Account as on the old one. 2. Install House Rules from the App Store and open it. 3. Your clubs and sessions come down from iCloud by themselves. A club with a long history can take a while the first time, up to an hour or more. Keep House Rules open and the iPhone on Wi-Fi until everything is there. To check, open Settings on the new iPhone and look at the line under Sync with iCloud, see Sync with iCloud. A simulator can't sign in to iCloud, so there are no screenshots of this way here. Before you wipe the old iPhone, open House Rules on it once more with internet on, so its last changes go up to iCloud. Then check on the new iPhone that your last session is there. With a backup file Use a backup if iCloud sync is off, if you play under another Apple Account on the new iPhone, or if you'd simply like to have a copy. On the old iPhone Open Settings, tap Back Up All Data and save the file somewhere the new iPhone can reach: Save to Files in iCloud Drive, AirDrop to the new iPhone, or your Mac. See Back Up and Restore. On the new iPhone Open House Rules. With nothing in it yet, the Lobby is empty. The Lobby on the new iPhone: No Sessions Yet, Create Club, Blind Timer not running, and Start Session Restore the file 1. Open Settings and tap Restore from Backup, under Data. 2. Pick the backup file. If you got it with AirDrop, it's in Files, in Downloads. 3. The Restore Backup sheet shows what's in the file: the date, the device it came from, and how many clubs, members, sessions and tournaments it has. On an empty iPhone the choice under How to Restore doesn't matter: either way you get everything from the file. 4. Tap the check mark. Restore Backup on the new iPhone: House Rules Backup, Nov 27, 2026 at 10:21 PM, from iPhone, 1 club, 6 members, 4 sessions, 0 tournaments. How to Restore with Add What's Missing checked Settings with the message Backup Restored: added 1 club, 6 members and 4 sessions The Lobby on the new iPhone after the restore: Recent Sessions from Fri, November 20, 13 and 6, and the Maple Street Game with 6 members and 4 sessions Set these again A few settings live on the iPhone itself, so neither iCloud nor a backup carries them. After the move, open Settings and check: Your Payment Link, under Getting Paid. The switches under Notifications: Level Change, Game Reminders, Who Owes Reminders and Lock Screen. The first time House Rules wants to send you a notification on the new iPhone, iOS asks you to allow it. Good to know With both iCloud sync and a backup, restore with Add What's Missing: what's already come down from iCloud stays, and nothing is added twice. Keep the backup file after the move. It's your copy of the club as it was that day. Related Sync with iCloud Back Up and Restore Settings

title: The Chips Don’t Add Up
headings: Find it first: the Session Log
Can't find it: who covers the short chips
text: When the last player has cashed out, every chip that was sold has come back: the chips on the table come to zero. If they don't, House Rules stops you before Settle Up and says how far off you are. Chips left over are usually rake and dealer tips you haven't recorded yet. Chips short, more coming back than were sold, usually mean a rebuy nobody recorded. This page shows both cases, how to find the cause, and what to do when you can't. The example club All the screenshots come from the Maple Street Game, Dave's home game on Maple Street. The club: Dave hosts for Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya and Sam. They play No-Limit Hold'em at 4/8 blinds with a chip worth $0.25, so a 400-chip buy-in costs $100. Tonight: six buy-ins and two rebuys are recorded, 3,200 chips sold as far as House Rules knows. Late in the night Priya rebought for 400 chips and gave Dave $100 in cash. Dave recorded the money with Collect, the button in the session's Cash Box for money a player pays in, but forgot to record the rebuy itself. So 3,600 chips were really in play. What happens: Sam is the last one at the table and hands back 944 chips. The table only had 544 left, so 400 chips are short. Chips short The cash-out that shows it Only the last player at the table can cash out more chips than are left. For everyone else, the keys won't take more than the table has. For the last player, the keys warn but let you record what they actually hand back: here 400 chips short. You can sort it out in Close Session. The Left on table line goes to −400. Cash Out, Sam: 944 chips. 400 chips short. You can sort it out in Close Session. Bought in 400, Result +$136, Left on table −400. Whole Stack and Cash Out above the keys Record what the player hands back, even when it doesn't fit. Typing a smaller number to make it fit only moves the mistake into their result. Fixing an entry is right only when you know that entry is wrong. After the last cash-out the session says Everyone Cashed Out with the warning 400 chips short. Record them in Close Session. The tiles show the gap: 3,200 buy-ins, 3,600 cashed out. Wrapping Up, Maple Street Game. Everyone Cashed Out: 400 chips short. Record them in Close Session. Tiles: 3,200 buy-ins, 3,600 cashed out, 6 players. Cashed Out list: Dave 400 → 652 +$63, Jenna 400 → 908 +$127, Marcus 800 → 236 −$141. Close Session at the bottom Close Session asks about them Tap Close Session. The Rake and Tips step says 400 chips short, and below the steps there are two cards: Find It First and Who Covers $100. The $100 is the 400 chips at chip value. Settle Up stays locked until the short chips are sorted out: no transfers appear before that. Close Session, Steps: Cash Out done, Rake and Tips 400 chips short, Expenses not needed, Collect done, Settle Up who pays whom. Find It First, a missed rebuy is the usual cause: Session Log, 23 entries. Who Covers $100 with Winners, Everyone and Host. Record Short Chips at the bottom Find it first: the Session Log Before anyone pays for the short chips, look for the cause. Tap Session Log under Find It First. You can also open it any time from More, the button with three dots at the top right of the session. The Session Log lists every buy-in, rebuy, cash-out and cash box payment, newest first. When a player has paid the cash box more than their buy-ins cost, the log says so at the top. Here: Priya paid $100 with no rebuy, with Paid $200, buy-ins cost $100. Add a 400 rebuy? under it. Session Log. At the top: Priya paid $100 with no rebuy. Paid $200, buy-ins cost $100. Add a 400 rebuy? Below, All, Chips and Cash Box, and the entries: Sam cash out 944, Priya +$100, Priya cash out 548, Tyler cash out 312, Jenna cash out 908, Marcus cash out 236, Dave cash out 652, Tyler +$100, Tyler rebuy 400 Tap that line. The rebuy keys open for Priya with 400 already in, and the payment is set to Not Yet, because her $100 is already in the cash box. Picking Cash here would count her money twice. Rebuy, Priya: 400 chips, Cost $100, Total buy-ins 800. Not Yet selected over Cash and Transfer. Suggestions 400 buy-in, 800, 1,200 and 200 next to the keys Tap the check mark. The rebuy goes into the log at the time you add it, not when it happened. Priya's result changes with it: she bought 800 chips and cashed out 548, so she's down 252 chips, −$63, not up $37. And the chips add up: Rake and Tips now says Not needed, and Settle Up is the next step. Close Session, Steps: Cash Out done, Rake and Tips not needed, Expenses not needed, Collect done, Settle Up 0 of 6 marked. From Cash Box: Sam, game +$136, paid in +$100, $236; Jenna, game +$127, paid in +$100, $227. Close for Now at the bottom The log only spots a payment with no rebuy when the money went into the cash box. Other places to look: A wrong number. Tap the player and look at Entries. Tap an entry, or touch and hold it and choose Edit Amount, to fix it. While chips are short, the check mark only turns on once the fix covers the whole shortage. A rebuy paid outside the cash box, straight to another player or by a bank transfer you didn't record. Ask around the table, then give the player the rebuy with Rebuy. A cash-out recorded too high. An earlier player's cash-out typed with an extra digit still fits on the table, but leaves too few chips for the last player. Check each cash-out against what the player really handed back. Can't find it: who covers the short chips If nothing turns up, someone has to pay for the missing chips. In Who Covers $100, choose how to share them, then tap Record Short Chips. Each player's share comes off their result in chips, at chip value. Switch between the options as often as you like: nothing is recorded until you tap the button. Many games agree on this in advance and set it as a house rule, see below. The screenshots below were taken before the missed rebuy was found, so Priya still shows as a winner. That's one more reason to look first: a wrong cause makes the wrong people pay. Everyone: split equally between all the players. Chips that don't divide go to some players, one each. Here four players cover 67 chips (−$16.75) and two cover 66 (−$16.50). Who Covers $100 with Everyone selected: Marcus, Jenna, Tyler and Priya one of 6 players, 67 chips, −$16.75; Dave and Sam one of 6 players, 66 chips, −$16.50 Winners: only players who won chips, in proportion to what they won. Sam won 544 chips and covers 150 (−$37.50), Priya won 148 and covers 41. Losers pay nothing extra. If nobody won chips, the card says Nobody won chips, so everyone covers equally. Who Covers $100 with Winners selected: Sam, won 544, covers 150, −$37.50; Jenna, won 508, covers 140, −$35; Dave, won 252, covers 69, −$17.25; Priya, won 148, covers 41, −$10.25 Host: one player covers all of it. Pick who in Pays. Any player can be chosen, and if the club's house rules name a host who played tonight, they're picked already. Record Short Chips stays off until someone is picked. Who Covers $100 with Host selected. Pays: Dave. Dave covers all 400 chips, −$100 The choice starts from the club's Short Chips house rule when it's set, and from Everyone when it isn't. When your choice matches the rule, the card says House Rules under its title. See House Rules. After Record Short Chips, the step says 400 short chips covered and Settle Up opens. In each covering player's transfer, the line under it shows the share, for example short chips −$16.75. See A Transfer Looks Wrong. Changing any chips afterwards clears the recorded short chips: a rebuy, a cash-out, an edited or deleted entry, a player brought back in, new rake or tips. The step asks again, with your last choice of who covers. Changing the chip value doesn't clear them. There's no separate button to undo Record Short Chips: when you find the real cause later, record the fix, and the short chips clear by themselves. Chips left over The other way round: everyone has cashed out and chips are still on the table. This is another Maple Street night, with no missed rebuy: 3,200 chips were sold and 3,080 came back, so 120 chips, worth $30, are left. The session says No chips should be left on the table (now 120). and a Chips Left on the Table card asks you to assign them to rake and tips before settling up. Wrapping Up. Everyone Cashed Out: No chips should be left on the table (now 120). Tiles 3,200 buy-ins, 3,080 cashed out. Chips Left on the Table: 120, assign them to rake and tips before settling up Settle Up waits for these too. Tap the card, or in Close Session the Rake and Tips button. The sheet starts with all 120 in Rake and 0 in Tips. Close Session with the Rake keys open: Rake 120, Tips 0, On the table 120. Rake and Tips 120 chips left over in the steps behind Rake and tips together must use up exactly the chips left over. Until they do, the keys say how far off you are, like 10 not assigned here with 100 in rake and 10 in tips, and the check mark stays off. Rake 100, Tips 10, 10 not assigned in red, On the table 120. The check mark is off No rake or tips tonight? Then the leftover chips mean someone cashed out too little. Check each cash-out in the player's Entries and fix the wrong one with Edit Amount. More about rake and tips is in Rake, Tips and Rakeback. Good to know Recorded rake and tips can't go below what's already paid from them: the rakeback and expenses paid from the rake, and the tips already paid out of the cash box. Delete those first. The rakeback and the expenses paid from the rake together can't be more than the rake. Short chips are counted in chips, not money: the covering players lose chips from their result, and the chip value turns them into dollars. The Session Log has All, Chips and Cash Box at the top to show only chip entries or only cash box payments. Related Buy-Ins, Rebuys and Cash-Outs Rake, Tips and Rakeback Close Session, Step by Step The Cash Box Doesn't Match

title: The Cash Box Doesn’t Match
text: House Rules knows how much cash should be in your hands: every payment recorded as cash, minus every payout in cash. Count Cash compares that with what you actually count. When the two differ, the cause is usually a payment recorded the wrong way, a payment you forgot to record, or a payout with the wrong amount. Look for it before you write the difference off. This page shows a count that comes up short, how one wrong entry caused it, and what to do with a difference you can't explain, short or over. The example club All the screenshots come from the Maple Street Game, Dave's home game on Maple Street. The club: Dave hosts for Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya and Sam. They play No-Limit Hold'em at 4/8 blinds with a chip worth $0.25, so a 400-chip buy-in costs $100. Tonight: everyone has cashed out, and nobody has been paid out yet. Five players paid their $100 buy-ins and Marcus and Tyler their $100 rebuys: $700 in the cash box. All of it is recorded as cash except Jenna's $100 by bank transfer, so House Rules expects $600 in cash. Sam hasn't paid and owes $52; money that hasn't come in isn't counted. Dave paid for the $48 pizza from his own pocket, not from the cash box, so it doesn't change the count either. What happens: Dave counts the cash before handing out the winnings and finds $500, not $600. Priya had sent her $100 by bank, but her payment was recorded as cash. Count the cash Open the session and tap Cash Box. The tiles split the money by how it came in: $600 in cash and $100 by transfer. Only the cash part is in your hands, so only it is counted. The rake tile is the house's part of the money already in the box: it doesn't change what you count. Cash Box, Maple Street Game. In Cash Box $700: $600 in cash, $100 by transfer, $700 collected, $0 paid out, $52 still owed, $20 rake. Before You Settle Up: Sam owes $52, can stay unpaid until settlement. Collect, Pay Out and Count Cash at the bottom Tap Count Cash at the bottom right and type what you counted. Should be in cash is what House Rules expects, Difference is the gap. Dave types $500: the difference is −$100. Count Cash, $500. Should be in cash $600, Difference −$100 Tap the check mark. When the count matches, it's recorded and a message says Cash matches. When it doesn't, a sheet opens with the difference in its title, here $100 Short. When the cash is short $100 Short. Find It First: Sam, not paid, $52; Session Log. Options: Leave It for Now, count again later, checked; Host Covers It, marked as covered, nothing to split; Split Among Players, $16.67 each, 6 players Find It First lists the players who haven't paid the cash box yet, with what each owes, and a link to the Session Log with every payment and payout of the night. Here Sam really hasn't paid, so that's not it. What to check, most likely first: A payment recorded as cash that came by bank. The money is in your bank account, not your hands. This is Dave's case. A payout or expense with the wrong amount, or one entered twice. Cash paid out that wasn't recorded, like a winner you paid early or a pizza paid from the cash. Cash that left the room, in a pocket or under the chip tray. To look through the entries, tap ✕ to close the sheet. Nothing is recorded, not even the count. Fix the entry Scroll down to Operations in the Cash Box: every payment, payout and count, newest on top. Touch and hold an entry for its menu: Edit Amount fixes the amount. The cash box can't go below zero, so a change that would leave it short is refused. Mark Paid by Transfer moves a payment from cash to bank, and Mark Paid in Cash moves it back. The cash box total stays the same; only the split between in cash and by transfer changes. Delete removes the entry after asking Delete Operation? Priya's buy-in payment is the one that came by bank. Dave touches and holds it and chooses Mark Paid by Transfer. Operations in the Cash Box. Priya, payment, Payment for buy-in, +$100 is held, with a menu: Edit Amount, Mark Paid by Transfer, Delete Her line now says payment by transfer, and the tiles show $500 in cash and $200 by transfer. Operations: Tyler, payment, Payment for rebuy, +$100; Marcus, payment, Payment for rebuy, +$100; Priya, payment by transfer, Payment for buy-in, +$100; Tyler, payment, Payment for buy-in, +$100 Cash Box, In Cash Box $700: $500 in cash, $200 by transfer, $700 collected, $0 paid out, $52 still owed, $20 rake Dave counts again, types $500 and taps the check mark: Cash matches. Cash Box with $500 in cash and $200 by transfer. A message at the bottom: Cash matches Can't find it When you've checked everything and the cash is still short, choose what to do with the difference and tap the check mark: Leave It for Now: only notes the count. Nothing changes, and you can count again later. Host Covers It: the host pays the difference. House Rules records a Cash short expense paid from the cash box and puts all of it on the host, so it comes off the host's result. The host is the one named in the club's house rules, see House Rules. With no host there, or one who didn't play tonight, the option says Marked as covered, nothing to split: it only notes the count, like Leave It for Now. The Maple Street Game hasn't named a host, so that's what the screenshot shows. Split Among Players: everyone who played pays an equal share, here $16.67 each, 6 players. It's the same Cash short expense, split evenly. The $16.67 is rounded: the shares add up to exactly $100, with the odd cents on some players. The Cash short expense shows under Expenses in the Cash Box, and in Settle Up each player's share shows in the line under their transfer as expense share. See Expenses. These options record an expense paid from the cash box, so there has to be enough money in it. If there isn't, the message says There isn't enough money in the cash box. When the cash is over More cash than expected usually means a payment you didn't record: a player paid, but nobody tapped Collect. Record it now and count again. If no player owes anything, the extra may be a rebuy nobody recorded, see The Chips Don't Add Up. Here, after the count matched, Dave finds a $10 bill under the chip tray and counts $510. The sheet says $10 Over. $10 Over. Find It First: Session Log. Options: Leave It, count again later; Add to Tips, dealer tips +$10, checked When the cash is over, Find It First also lists short chips, when the chips are short and not yet recorded (not the case tonight), with what they're worth: Someone may have paid for a rebuy that isn't recorded. Then the options: Leave It: only notes the count. The extra stays in the cash box. Add to Tips: the extra goes to the dealer tips, here Dealer tips +$10. Dave picks Add to Tips and taps the check mark. Operations gets an Extra Cash line, added to tips, +$10. Operations, 10: Extra Cash, added to tips, +$10; Cash Count, count, $10 extra, added to tips, +$510; Cash Count, count, matched, +$500; Tyler, payment, Payment for rebuy, +$100; Marcus, payment, Payment for rebuy, +$100 Every count is kept Each count is a Cash Count line in Operations with the amount you counted and what you did: count, matched, count, $100 short, left for now, count, $10 extra, added to tips, and so on. The amount on a count line is what you counted, not money coming in: a count never changes the cash box total. Good to know Count Cash is off until the cash box has at least one payment or payout. You can also count in Close Session: on the Collect step, the Cash card has Should be in cash and Count Cash, and says when you last counted. See Close Session, Step by Step. If a payment or payout is added while the count sheet is open, the count is refused: This count doesn't match the cash box anymore. Count again. The cash box can't go below zero. Close Session won't settle up while it is, and says The cash box can't go below zero, with the amount. Marking a settlement transfer as paid in cash adds its payment or payout to the cash box too, so count after the transfers if you settle in cash. See Marking Transfers Done. On the iPad, in the full layout with the sidebar, an entry in the Cash Box next to the session has only Edit Amount and Delete in its menu. Related The Cash Box The Chips Don't Add Up Marking Transfers Done Expenses

title: A Transfer Looks Wrong
headings: Read the line under a transfer
Someone pays a player they didn't play against
A player who paid still owes
text: Settle Up balances money, not hands. It works out a short list of transfers that leaves everyone even, so a transfer can look odd: someone pays a player they never played a hand against, or an amount isn't the result you remember. Most of the time the transfer is right, and the line under it says why. This page explains how to read a transfer, what changes the plan, and how to fix a real mistake, even after the session is finished. The example club All the screenshots come from the Maple Street Game, Dave's home game on Maple Street. The club: Dave hosts for Marcus, Jenna, Tyler, Priya and Sam. They play No-Limit Hold'em at 4/8 blinds with a chip worth $0.25, so a 400-chip buy-in costs $100. Tonight: everyone has cashed out. Marcus and Tyler rebought once. 80 chips went to rake and 40 to dealer tips, $30 in all, so the players' results add up to −$30, not zero. Dave paid $48 for pizza, split evenly, $8 each. Payments: everyone paid the cash box for their buy-ins and rebuys, Jenna by bank, except Sam. He lost 176 chips (−$44) and owes $52 with his pizza share. What happens: Dave settles up. Sam pays part of what he owes, and the plan changes under Dave's eyes. Read the line under a transfer The screenshots show the Settle Up step of Close Session. It lists the transfers in three groups: From Cash Box, Between Players and To Cash Box. Under each name a line adds up the amount, part by part: Game: the player's result at the table, chips at chip value. Rakeback: their share of the rakeback. Paid for expenses: what they paid for the group, like Dave's pizza. Expense share: their part of the expenses. Short chips: their share of chips that went missing, see The Chips Don't Add Up. Paid in: what they've already put into the cash box. Taken from cash box: what they've already taken out of it. Parts that are zero are left out. Gains have a plus, costs a minus. From Cash Box, 0 of 5. Jenna: game +$177, expense share −$8, paid in +$100, $269. Dave: game +$63, paid for expenses +$48, expense share −$8, paid in +$100, $203. Priya: game +$37, expense share −$8, paid in +$100, $129. Tyler: game −$122, expense share −$8, paid in +$200, $70. Marcus: game −$141, expense share −$8, paid in +$200, from Sam −$22, $29. Between Players: Sam → Marcus, $22 Take Tyler. He lost $122 at the table and had $8 of pizza, so his night cost him $130. But he paid $200 into the cash box for his buy-in and rebuy. So the cash box gives him $70 back, even though he lost. That's the most common surprise: a loser who paid up front gets money back. Dave won $63, paid $48 for the pizza and had $8 of it, and paid $100 in: $203 from the cash box. Someone pays a player they didn't play against Sam owes $52. Instead of paying it all to the cash box, he pays $22 straight to Marcus, and Marcus's line ends with from Sam −$22: Marcus gets $22 less from the cash box. Any loser can pay any winner, as long as the totals match, and House Rules keeps the number of transfers small. Priya $129, Tyler $70, Marcus $29 with from Sam −$22. Between Players, 0 of 1: Sam → Marcus, $22. To Cash Box, 0 of 1: Sam, owed for the session, $30 Sam's own transfers have no breakdown, only owed for the session. The line is left out when a player has more than one transfer, as Sam does here, and when the only part is the game result. A player who paid still owes The plan only knows payments you recorded. If Sam handed Dave $52 and it isn't in the cash box, Sam still owes it on the screen. Either record the money with Collect in the Cash Box, or mark his transfer as paid, below. See The Cash Box. Mark a transfer Tap a transfer that's still open. The payment keys open with the whole amount, here Cash Box → Dave, $203, Full amount. Tap Mark as Paid. Payment keys: Cash Box → Dave, $203, Full amount. Mark as Paid above the keys, 203 All next to them The transfer is crossed out and ticked. From Cash Box says 1 of 5, and the step says 1 of 7 marked. Settle Up 1 of 7 marked. From Cash Box, 1 of 5: Jenna $269; Dave, ticked and crossed out, $203; Priya $129; Tyler $70 Marked the wrong one? Tap it again and the tick is gone, as long as the plan hasn't been worked out again since, below. Touch and hold a transfer for more: Mark as Paid, Mark Partial Payment (the same as typing a smaller amount), Mark Paid by Transfer for money that went by bank, and Ask, a message that asks the player who gets the money whether it arrived. To remind the player who pays, tap the bell on the transfer. More in Marking Transfers Done. The list changed House Rules works out the plan again when something changes the money: rake or tips, rakeback, expenses, or a partial payment. Transfers you've already marked stay done. They move out of the plan into Already Done, and the new plan counts them. Sam brings Dave $20 for the cash box, not the whole $30. Dave taps Sam's transfer and types 20: the keys say $10 stays open, and the button becomes Record Payment. Payment keys: Sam → Cash Box, $20, $10 stays open. Record Payment above the keys, 30 All next to them The plan is then worked out again from what's still owed, so the $10 doesn't simply stay on Sam's transfer. Sam still owes $32 in all. The cash box now has $20 more, so it can pay Marcus $49 instead of $29, and Sam owes Marcus only $2 instead of $22. The rest, $30, goes to the cash box. Sam's row counts his $20 in too: Paid $20 of $50, $30 to go. Under Already Done, Dave's $203 and Sam's $20 stay recorded: Done before the plan was recalculated. The plan above already counts them. Sam, owed for the session, Paid $20 of $50, $30. Already Done, 2 transfers: Done before the plan was recalculated. The plan above already counts them. Cash Box → Dave $203, Sam → Cash Box $20 So a transfer that "disappeared" was paid before the plan changed: look under Already Done. From then on, its tick is permanent. Transfers under Already Done can't be unmarked with a tap. A cash box one is undone by deleting its entry in the Cash Box, under Operations: it's the one with the note Settlement: payout from the cash box or Settlement: transfer to the cash box. See The Cash Box Doesn't Match for the entry menu. A wrong chip value The chip value turns every chip result into money, so a wrong one makes every transfer wrong by the same factor. If all the amounts look too big or too small, check it: in the session, tap More, the button with three dots at the top right, then Edit Session. The More menu of the session: Edit Session, Rake and Tips, House Rules, Session Log, Share Session, Hand Over Session, Delete Session Chip Value is under the blinds, here 1 chip = $0.25. Tap it to change it, then tap the check mark at the top right. Edit Session is only there while the session can still be changed. Edit Session: Game NLH or PLO, Small Blind 4, Big Blind 8, Ante 0, Chip Value 1 chip = $0.25, Start Nov 24, 2026 A new chip value can be refused if it would make the rake or tips worth less than what's already paid from them: the rakeback, expenses paid from the rake, or tips paid from the cash box. Fix a finished session Once a session is finished, nothing in it can be changed. The screenshots here are from last week's game, a different night with five players. It says This session is finished and can't be changed. To fix a mistake, reopen it. Session Ended, Maple Street Game, Tue, Nov 17, NLH 4/8. This session is finished and can't be changed. To fix a mistake, reopen it. Results: won $59 by 3 players, lost $59 by 2 players. Cash Box $500, Settlement and a lock button at the bottom 1. Tap Settlement at the bottom, then Reopen. Or tap the lock button next to Settlement. 2. House Rules asks Reopen Session?: The settlement will be recalculated. Completed transfers stay. Tap Reopen Session. 3. A message says Session reopened. Fix the mistake, then finish the session again in Settle Up. Settle Up for Tue, Nov 17: Settled Through the Cash Box, five players with paid $100 and their results. The Reopen button with a question: Reopen Session? The settlement will be recalculated. Completed transfers stay. Reopen Session Transfers you marked before stay done and show under Already Done if the fix changes the plan. Good to know The plan is worked out again in Close Session when the money changes. The Settle Up sheet opened from a session works it out when it opens. Kept by House under the rake step is the part of the rake that isn't rakeback. It's not anyone's transfer. In a session you closed with Close for Now, marking the last open transfer finishes it, and a message says Session settled. Related How Settle Up Works Marking Transfers Done The Cash Box Doesn't Match Chip Value

title: FAQ
headings: Which devices does it run on?
Is House Rules a gambling app?
Do my players need the app?
Do I need an account or the internet?
Where are my clubs and sessions kept?
Which currency does House Rules use?
What's the difference between chips and money?
A player will pay later. What do I do?
A player paid by bank transfer. Is that in the cash box?
Why does a player who lost get money back?
Why does someone pay a player they didn't play against?
Can rake, tips and shared costs be counted?
The chips don't add up at the end.
The cash in my hands doesn't match.
Can I change a finished session?
Can two games run at the same time?
Does House Rules do tournaments too?
Does the blind timer keep going when I close the app?
How do I send a session to another phone?
Can another host take over a running game?
Can I see stats for my players?
How do I move everything to a new iPhone?
text: Short answers to the questions hosts ask most. Each one links to the page with the whole story. About House Rules How do I start? Follow Your First Cash Game: a club, a session, buy-ins, cash-outs and Settle Up, step by step. For a tournament, see Your First Tournament. Which devices does it run on? iPhone and iPad with iOS 26 or later. Is House Rules a gambling app? No. House Rules is a notebook for the game you host: who bought in, what they cashed out, what's in the cash box and who pays whom at the end. There's no playing for money in the app, no betting, and no money moves through it. Players pay each other the way they always do, in cash or by bank. Do my players need the app? No. Only the host uses House Rules. Players get their results, transfers and reminders as ordinary messages you send from the app. See Sharing Results and Who Owes and Reminders. Do I need an account or the internet? No to both. There's no sign-up, and everything works offline, at the table or in a basement with no signal. You only need a connection to send a message or a file, and for your devices to sync through iCloud. Where are my clubs and sessions kept? On your iPhone or iPad and, while Sync with iCloud is on, in your private iCloud. Only you can see it there: House Rules has no servers of its own. Your iPhone and iPad signed in to the same Apple Account show the same clubs, sessions and timer. The switch is in Settings, under Data, and it's on from the start. Turn it off and everything stays on the device. See Sync with iCloud. You can also keep a copy of your own: Back Up All Data, under the same Data, saves every club, member, session and tournament as one .houserules file, and Restore from Backup brings it back. The app doesn't make backups by itself, so save one when you want it. See Back Up and Restore. Does it work on iPad? Yes. On the iPad a sidebar on the left holds your clubs, sessions and the blind timer, the blind timer can have its own window, and you can drop a session file right on House Rules. See House Rules on iPad, Timer Window on iPad and Dropping a File on iPad. Money and chips Which currency does House Rules use? The currency of your iPhone's region, the one in the iPhone's Settings, General, Language & Region. All amounts in the app use it. House Rules doesn't convert money: if you change the region, the same numbers show with the new currency's sign. What's the difference between chips and money? Chips are what's on the table, money is what players pay. The chip value links them: at $0.25 a chip, a 400-chip buy-in costs $100. House Rules counts the game in chips and turns every result into money with the chip value. See Chip Value. A player will pay later. What do I do? When you seat them, pick Not Yet instead of Cash or Transfer under the buy-in. They owe the cash box until you collect, and whatever is still unpaid at the end goes into the transfers. See When a Player Pays Later. A player paid by bank transfer. Is that in the cash box? Yes. The cash box counts both, split into in cash and by transfer, so you know how much paper money should be in your hands. See The Cash Box. Why does a player who lost get money back? Because they paid up front. A player who bought in for $200 and lost $122 gets the rest, $78, back from the cash box. The line under each transfer shows what it's made of. See A Transfer Looks Wrong. Why does someone pay a player they didn't play against? Settle Up balances money, not hands. It works out a short list of transfers that leaves everyone even, so any player who lost can pay any player who won. See How Settle Up Works. Can rake, tips and shared costs be counted? Yes. Chips left on the table at the end go to rake and dealer tips, part of the rake can go back to players as rakeback, and shared costs like pizza are split between the players you pick. See Rake, Tips and Rakeback and Expenses. When something looks off The chips don't add up at the end. Chips left over are usually rake and tips. Chips short usually mean a rebuy nobody recorded. See The Chips Don't Add Up. The cash in my hands doesn't match. Use Count Cash in the Cash Box, then look for a payment recorded the wrong way. See The Cash Box Doesn't Match. I typed the wrong number. Right after the entry, tap Undo in the message at the bottom. Later, tap the player's row, then the entry, and type the right amount. See Buy-Ins, Rebuys and Cash-Outs. Can I change a finished session? Yes, after you reopen it. Open the session and tap the lock next to Settlement at the bottom. Transfers you already marked stay done. See A Transfer Looks Wrong. Sessions and devices Can two games run at the same time? Yes. Start another session while one is running, and both run side by side. Does House Rules do tournaments too? Yes: entries, re-entries and add-ons, bounties, the prize pool and payouts, deals and season points. See Your First Tournament. Does the blind timer keep going when I close the app? Yes. It moves to the next level on its own and sends a notification when the level changes. See Notifications and Lock Screen. How do I send a session to another phone? Share it as a .pokersession file from the session's More menu, then open the file on the other phone. Both phones need House Rules. See Export and Import. Can another host take over a running game? Yes. In the running session, tap More, then Hand Over Session, and send the file to the new host. Your copy locks, so only one phone runs the game. If you need it again, Take Back unlocks your copy, but changes made on the other phone don't come with it. See Handing a Session Over. Can I see stats for my players? Yes. Each club member has a total result, sessions played and winning sessions, and you can export them as a CSV file for a spreadsheet. See Player Stats and CSV. For the whole club, buy-ins by month, the house's share and everyone's results, see Club Stats. How do I move everything to a new iPhone? Sign in to the same Apple Account on the new iPhone, install House Rules and keep Sync with iCloud on: your clubs and sessions arrive on their own. A big club can take an hour or more the first time, because iCloud sends sessions in batches. You can use the app meanwhile, and it goes faster with House Rules open on Wi-Fi. Settings shows Syncing until it's done. Restoring your old iPhone's backup works too. Without iCloud, tap Back Up All Data in Settings on the old iPhone, send the .houserules file to the new one and open it there, or tap Restore from Backup and pick it. The file carries everything, clubs with their house rules and seasons included. See Moving to a New iPhone. Still stuck? See Contact Support.

title: Settings
text: Settings is one screen with everything that isn't about a club or a session: help, your data, notifications, your payment link and importing a session from another host. This page goes through it from top to bottom and says where each part is explained in full. Open Settings Tap the gear at the top right of the Lobby. On the iPad, Settings is at the bottom of the sidebar. The Lobby of House Rules with the Maple Street Game and the gear at the top right The top of Settings: Help, then Data with Sync with iCloud on, Back Up All Data and Restore from Backup, then Notifications with Level Change, Game Reminders, Who Owes Reminders and Lock Screen Help The first row opens Help in the app: the same topics as this wiki, a step-by-step first cash game and first tournament, How a Cash Game Flows in six steps, common questions, the Glossary, and Contact Support at the bottom. Search articles and questions finds an answer by a word. See Glossary and Contact Support. Data Sync with iCloud keeps your clubs, sessions, cash boxes and the timer the same on all your iPhones and iPads. It's on from the start. The line under it says how syncing is going. See Sync with iCloud. Back Up All Data saves everything to one file you keep yourself. Once you have one, the date of your last backup shows under it. Restore from Backup brings a backup file back, on this iPhone or a new one. See Back Up and Restore. Notifications Four switches, each with a line saying what it does: Level Change: a notification when the blind timer moves to the next level on its own. See Notifications and Lock Screen. Game Reminders: a day and two hours before a planned game. On game day it also tells you who still owes from past sessions. See Planned Games and Reminders. Who Owes Reminders: once a week, while anyone in your clubs owes. Off from the start. See Who Owes and Reminders. Lock Screen: a running cash game and the blind timer as a Live Activity, a live card on the Lock Screen and in the Dynamic Island. See Lock Screen and Quick Rebuy. If notifications for House Rules are off in the iPhone's Settings app, a row Turn On Notifications shows at the top of this group, in the warning color. Tap it to go straight to the iPhone's notification settings for House Rules. Getting Paid Your Payment Link is a link players can pay you by, for example your page in a payment app. Tap the row, paste the link and tap the check mark. House Rules adds it to the reminders you send when someone owes the cash box, so players can pay with one tap. For a PayPal.me link, the amount is added too. While there's no link, the row says None. Further down Settings: Game Reminders and Lock Screen on, Who Owes Reminders off, then Getting Paid with Your Payment Link, None, Sessions from Other Hosts with Import Session, and About The Payment Link field over the keyboard, with a close button and a check mark, and the note: goes into reminders when someone owes the cash box, for PayPal.me the amount is added The link stays on this iPhone: it isn't synced through iCloud, isn't in a backup and doesn't go into a session file. Sessions from Other Hosts Import Session brings in a .pokersession file that another host sent you. To send one of yours, open the session or tournament and choose Share Session in the More menu. See Export and Import. About Share House Rules sends a link to House Rules to a friend. More Apps opens our other apps in the App Store. The last line of Settings is the version of House Rules with its build number in brackets, for example House Rules 1.0 (26). Put it in your email when you write to support. The bottom of Settings: Getting Paid, Sessions from Other Hosts with Import Session, About with Share House Rules and More Apps, and House Rules 1.0 (26) at the very bottom Good to know Settings on the iPhone itself, like the payment link and the notification switches, aren't synced through iCloud and aren't in a backup. On a new iPhone, set them again, see Moving to a New iPhone. House Rules has no account and no sign-in. Your data stays on your devices and in your own iCloud. Related Sync with iCloud Back Up and Restore Contact Support

title: House Rules on iPad
text: House Rules runs on the iPad with a layout of its own: a sidebar on the left with everything the Lobby has on the iPhone, and the game itself spread over the rest of the screen. With a keyboard, the main actions have shortcuts. Your clubs and sessions are the same as on your iPhone while Sync with iCloud is on, see Sync with iCloud. The example club The screenshots come from Dave's iPad. Dave hosts the Maple Street Game on Tuesdays. Tonight's game is running: Dave, Marcus, Jenna, Tyler and Priya are at the table, 2,400 chips are in play and $600 is in the cash box. Landscape House Rules on the iPad works in landscape: turn the iPad on its side, the layout needs the width. In a window next to other apps, it keeps a size of at least 1000 by 700 points, so the columns always fit. The sidebar The sidebar on the left does what the Lobby does on the iPhone: Tonight: the running session, with the club and how many players are at the table, for example Live, 5 at the table. With no game running, Start Session. Needs Settling: sessions where everyone has cashed out but the settling up isn't finished. The group is there only when there are some. Clubs: your clubs, and New Club to add one. Library: All Sessions, Stats, Blind Timer and Settings. The + at the top of the sidebar starts a new session. With no game running and nothing chosen, the right side shows No Session Running and Start Session. House Rules on an iPad in landscape: the sidebar with Tonight, Start Session, Clubs, Maple Street Game, Office Game, New Club, Library, All Sessions, Stats, Blind Timer and Settings. On the right: No Session Running, Start tonight's game, or pick a club in the sidebar, Start Session A running game Tap the running session under Tonight. The game takes the rest of the screen: At the top, the club and the date, and Table, Cash Box and Settle Up to switch between the table, the money and the end of the night. In the middle, a strip with the chips on the table, bought in and cashed out, the money in the cash box and what's still owed, and under it a tile for each player at the table with their chips. On the right, Tonight: who's at the table and the latest buy-ins and rebuys, with Add Player and Close Session at the bottom. A running cash game on the iPad. The sidebar with Maple Street Game, Live, 5 at the table. In the middle: Table, Cash Box and Settle Up, on the table 2,400, bought in 2,400, cashed out 0, in cash box $600, still owed $0, and tiles for Dave, Jenna, Marcus, Priya and Tyler. On the right: Tonight, 5 at the table, 0 cashed out, the recent buy-ins, Add Player and Close Session Tap a player's tile to work with them. The right side turns into that player's panel: Rebuy, Cash Out and History, with the keys to type the chips. Tap the × to go back to the game. Dave's tile selected. On the right, Dave at the table with Rebuy, Cash Out and History: bought in 400, $100 at chip value, a rebuy of 400 for $100, Not Yet, Cash or Transfer, the keys, and Rebuy 400 at the bottom Cash Box shows the money of the session: what's in the cash box, what's been collected, what's still owed, the rake and the expenses, and every payment in Operations. On the right, Before You Settle Up, with Collect and Pay Out. See The Cash Box. Cash Box on the iPad: in cash box $600, collected $600, still owed $0, rake $0, Expenses, and Operations with each player's payment for the buy-in. On the right: Before You Settle Up, 5 of 5 players at the table, Collect and Pay Out Tap the club's name at the top for the session's menu: Edit Session, Rake and Tips, House Rules, Session Log, Share Session, Hand Over Session and Delete Session. The session menu under Maple Street Game on the iPad: Edit Session, Rake and Tips, House Rules, Session Log, Share Session, Hand Over Session and Delete Session Settle Up, or Close Session, walks you through the end of the night over the whole right side, the same steps as on the iPhone, see Close Session, Step by Step. Keyboard shortcuts With a keyboard attached, these shortcuts work. The menu bar at the top of the screen lists them too, in the File, View and Session menus. ⌘N: New Session ⌘T: Blind Timer ⇧⌘T: Open Blind Timer in New Window ⌘1: Table ⌘2: Cash Box ⌘3: Settle Up ⌘R: Rebuy for the chosen player, or Back in Game for a player who has cashed out ⌘O: Cash Out for the chosen player The Session menu also has Rake and Tips and Close Session, without shortcuts. A menu item is greyed out when it doesn't fit the screen you're on, for example Rebuy with no player chosen. More on the iPad The blind timer in its own window: keep the big clock in a window of its own while you run the game. See Timer Window on iPad. Drop a session file on the window: drag a .pokersession file from Files or Mail onto House Rules to import it. See Dropping a File on iPad. Good to know The iPad and the iPhone are the same app with the same data. You can start a game on the iPad and check it on your phone, as long as both sync with iCloud.
